text: Abercrombie. Abercrombie appears to be a feeble, eccentric hermit dwelling in a dilapidated shack in western Duskwood near Raven Hill Cemetery. Claiming to be a harmless recluse plagued by the horrors of the woods, he readily enlists sympathetic travelers to gather peculiar reagents and supplies on his behalf. Tucked away in the rotting shadows near Raven Hill Cemetery, Abercrombie cuts a pathetic figure. He presents himself as an old man merely trying to survive the terrors of Duskwood, asking travelers to run modest errands into Darkshire for supplies, herbs, and thread. To those unfamiliar with the history of the region, he seems like just another unfortunate soul left behind as the province fell into decay.

Agathelos the Raging. Agathelos the Raging is a colossal armored boar penned within the thorned tunnels of Razorfen Kraul. Reared by the Death's Head quilboar as a living siege engine and avatar of their ancient god, he has been driven into a violent, unnatural frenzy. His sheer mass and strength make him one of the most dangerous beasts lurking under the southern Barrens. Quilboar venerate all swine as descendants of their patron deity and progenitor, the god Agamaggan. To them, boars of exceptional size and tenacity are considered direct blessings from their fallen god. A beast the size of Agathelos—standing roughly twice as tall as a Barrens thunder lizard—carries massive spiritual and ceremonial significance among the Razorfen tribes.

Aggem Thorncurse. Aggem Thorncurse is a spectral quilboar encountered deep within the thorned tunnels of Razorfen Kraul. Bound beyond death to the service of his tribe, he fights alongside Warlord Ramtusk and Death Speaker Jargba to defend their sacred redoubt against intruders. Within the heart of Razorfen Kraul, the quilboar fight desperately to protect their ancestral dens from outsiders. Aggem Thorncurse is not among the living defenders; instead, he lingers as a restless spirit. Bound to the physical realm by dark geomancy and shamanic rites, Aggem takes up arms when intruders threaten the tribe's warlord.

Aku'mai. Aku'mai is a monstrous, three-headed hydra dwelling in the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps along the Zoram Strand. Imbued with primordial shadow and favored by the ancient Old Gods, the beast is revered as a herald of apocalyptic ruin. The Twilight's Hammer cult tends to the creature in its submerged lair, offering living sacrifices to sate its eternal hunger. Long before cultists claimed the sunken temple beneath the sea, Aku'mai haunted the coast of Ashenvale as a living blight upon the Zoram Strand. A creature of deep water and darker powers, this gargantuan hydra carries a fragment of the Old Gods' ancient malevolence within its three ravenous heads. Rather than an ordinary denizen of the tides, Aku'mai is an ancient terror that has lurked in the submerged ruins since the fall of the night elves' temple to Elune, poisoning the waters with Void-tainted malice.

Alanndarian Nightsong. Alanndarian Nightsong is a night elf resident of Auberdine in Darkshore dedicated to tending to the region's beleaguered fauna. She works alongside travelers to remedy the blights plaguing the local wildlife, particularly the native striders and forest creatures corrupted by dark forces. Situated in the coastal settlement of Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong watches over the fragile ecological balance of Darkshore. As mysterious taints seep into the soil and waters, the creatures of the ancient woods have begun to succumb to sickness and unnatural aggression. Alanndarian acts as a guardian and naturalist, seeking practical remedies to ease their suffering and restore their natural vigor.

Althea Ebonlocke. Commander Althea Ebonlocke leads the Night Watch, the beleaguered town guard protecting Darkshire from the terrors of Duskwood. A relative of Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, she shoulders the defense of an isolated region abandoned by Stormwind's regular military. She organizes patrols, tasks adventurers with culling local horrors, and coordinates the town's survival against constant monstrous threats. While her relative, Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, handles civil governance within the town hall, Commander Althea directs Darkshire's thin line of physical defense. When Stormwind failed to deploy royal troops to guard Duskwood against creeping horrors, the citizenry formed the Night Watch. Under Althea's steady, unyielding command, these volunteers patrol the fog-shrouded roads, keeping skeletal undead, ferocious wolves, and spiders from overrunning the town perimeter.

Anastasia Hartwell. Anastasia Hartwell is a prominent Forsaken mage trainer residing in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. She guides fledgling and developing spellcasters in mastering the arcane arts and oversees vital magical research and field missions across Lordaeron and beyond. Standing within the dark, echoing chambers of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Anastasia Hartwell instructs Forsaken and Horde mages in channeling arcane energies. Though the kingdom of Lordaeron fell to ruin, former human practitioners like Anastasia have preserved their scholarly traditions in undeath. She maintains that magic demands strict discipline, warning any traveler she meets that careless incantations will quickly consume the untrained.

Apothecary Johaan. Apothecary Johaan is an alchemist and researcher of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed in Brill. Tasked by his order and Lady Sylvanas, he conducts lethal experiments on local flora and fauna to develop the Forsaken's new plague. Working openly out of the Forsaken settlement of Brill in Tirisfal Glades, Apothecary Johaan represents the scientific ambitions of the newly formed Royal Apothecary Society. Like his colleagues across Lordaeron, Johaan operates under direct orders to craft biological and alchemical weapons capable of securing the Forsaken's fragile future against the living and the Scourge alike.

Apothecary Renferrel. Apothecary Renferrel is a prominent member of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Tasked with advancing the Forsaken's alchemical endeavors, he coordinates extensive field research into the region's corrupted wildlife and undead threats. Travelers through Silverpine frequently assist him with gathering volatile reagents and investigating dangerous Scourge remnants. Operating out of the Sepulcher, Renferrel serves as one of the Royal Apothecary Society's chief field researchers in Silverpine Forest. While Undercity houses the grand laboratories and high leadership of the society, Renferrel handles the practical, muddy work of securing native biological specimens, refining potent concoctions, and analyzing the grim ecology of Lordaeron's western border.

Aramis Hammerhand. Aramis Hammerhand is an undead holy warrior situated within the desecrated chapel of Deathknell. As a Forsaken paladin trainer, he instructs newly risen dead who seek to reclaim their bond with the Holy Light. Walking this path in undeath requires immense discipline, as wielding such radiant energy inflicts agonizing pain upon their decayed flesh. Standing within the somber walls of Deathknell's chapel, Aramis Hammerhand represents an anomaly among the recently awakened Forsaken. In life, many citizens of Lordaeron answered the call of the Silver Hand, only to perish when the Scourge swept across the north. Aramis survived the fall only to be raised into undeath, yet he chose not to abandon the martial and spiritual teachings of his former existence. Now, he offers guidance to others who refuse to surrender their devotion.

Arcanist Doan. Arcanist Doan is a master human mage residing within the Athenaeum of the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing. Formerly an associate of the Silver Hand who assisted in forging the legendary Ashbringer, he now serves the Scarlet Crusade as one of its most lethal arcane specialists and guardian of key crusade archives. Before the Scarlet Crusade turned inward and zealous, Arcanist Doan walked among the Knights of the Silver Hand. During the Third War, he met with Highlord Alexandros Mograine and other founders at Southshore. When Mograine revealed a shadowy crystal taken from an orc warlock during the Second War, Doan observed its unnatural ability to absorb holy energy. Joining his arcane insight with the holy magic of his peers, Doan helped cleanse the void crystal into radiant light, forming the heart of the weapon known as the Ashbringer.

Arugal. Archmage Arugal is a former wizard of Dalaran and Gilneas who unleashed the feral worgen upon Lordaeron. Overcome by madness and grief, he now rules from the heights of Shadowfang Keep, treating the savage beasts as his beloved children while menacing all of Silverpine Forest. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Arugal was a member of the Kirin Tor, though some peers like Dalar Dawnweaver dismissed him as a charlatan whose weak spellcraft relied heavily on enchanted trinkets. When the Scourge swept across the north during the Third War, Arugal sought a weapon powerful enough to stem the tide. Drawing upon the esoteric research of the late Dalaran mage Ur, Arugal pierced the veil between realms and summoned the worgen into the mortal world. The ravenous beasts tore through the undead legions as intended, but their feral ferocity could not be contained, and their savage hunger swiftly turned against innocent mortals.

Asterion. Asterion is an ancient Highborne spirit bound to the ruins of Bashal'Aran in Darkshore. Once the trusted second to governor Athrikus Narassin ten millennia ago, he was mysteriously imprisoned in a magical moonstone seal that held him through mortal life and into the afterlife. Today, his specter remains shackled to the ruined shrine, surrounded by demonic beasts and dreaming of liberation. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran were sister cities blessed by Queen Azshara herself. Azshara appointed Athrikus Narassin to govern the twin settlements, and Asterion served as his right hand. Respected for both his physical combat prowess and his command of arcane sorcery, Asterion lived among the people of Bashal'Aran while frequently traveling between the sister cities to manage the needs of their citizens.

Athridas Bearmantle. Athridas Bearmantle is a night elf druid residing in Dolanaar within the boughs of Teldrassil. Tasked with safeguarding the local settlement, he directs young adventurers to investigate the encroaching corruption affecting the local wildlife and the nearby Gnarlpine furbolgs. Stationed within Dolanaar, Athridas Bearmantle stands as an early line of defense for the night elves emerging from Shadowglen. As the boughs of the newly grown world tree Teldrassil exhibit unnatural signs of decay and unrest, Athridas works tirelessly to coordinate local scouting efforts and protect the peaceful township from surrounding threats.

"Auntie" Bernice Stonefield. “Auntie” Bernice Stonefield is an elder of the Stonefield family, residing at their homestead in south-central Elwynn Forest. Widowed after her husband fell in battle during the kingdom's military campaigns, she is renowned throughout the valley for her famous pork belly pies. She can be found outside the farmhouse alongside Ma Stonefield, keeping a sharp eye on the neighborhood and harboring a deep suspicion of the rival Maclure family. Like many common folk across the Kingdom of Stormwind, Bernice has borne the steep price of ongoing war. Having lost her husband to military campaigns, she now lives out her days on the family homestead with her kin, helping manage daily farm affairs alongside matriarch Ma Stonefield. Despite personal loss, she keeps the household fed and running, earning local fame for her celebrated pork belly pies.

Baine Bloodhoof. Baine Bloodhoof is the son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof and the acting protector of Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. While his father governs the tribes from the towering heights of Thunder Bluff, Baine directly oversees local defense, investigating encroaching industrial exploitation and defending against feral predators. He serves as an essential bridge between youthful tauren braves and the ancestral wisdom of his clan. Born to Cairne and the late Tamaala, Baine spent his youth traveling alongside his nomadic people before they claimed the rich grasslands of Mulgore. His early life was marked by the ever-present threat of the centaur clans. Shortly after the Third War, a centaur warband under Khiragg captured young Baine, plunging Cairne into a grief-stricken stupor that nearly shattered the newly founded settlements. It was only through the courage of the champion Rexxar that Baine was liberated from captivity. That rescue restored Cairne's spirit, allowing the tauren to stand with Thrall's Horde against the invading Kul Tirans and secure their foothold on the continent.

Balthule Shadowstrike. Balthule Shadowstrike is a night elf scout stationed in northern Darkshore near the Tower of Althalaxx. Serving as a forward agent for Delgren the Purifier, he keeps watch over the sinister cultists and dark practitioners occupying the ancient elven ruins. Adventurers traveling along the northern coast are often directed to him to assist in unravelling and disrupting the dark rituals underway at the tower. Perched in the wilderness just west of the Tower of Althalaxx, Balthule Shadowstrike maintains a lonely and perilous vigil. Darkshore's northern reaches are thick with restless spirits and shadowed ruins, but the activity around the tower poses a particularly acute threat. Balthule operates under the direction of Delgren the Purifier, observing the movements of dark casters who have crept into the ancient Highborne remnants.

Baron Aquanis. Baron Aquanis is a powerful water elemental of the flooded Moonshrine Ruins in Blackfathom Deeps, where the Twilight's Hammer has made its lair. He rises from the deep water when someone disturbs the ruins' Fathom Stone. The shamans of the Earthen Ring have long thought him a corrupted elemental power, and they suspect the cult is behind it. Submerged beneath the flooded halls of the Moonshrine Ruins, the Fathom Stone lies right under the noses of the Twilight's Hammer cultists who now occupy the ruins. Inside it is a fathom core, a device that, properly read, tells the history of all elemental activity around it. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring sends Horde adventurers to recover the core, and disturbing the stone draws Baron Aquanis up from the depths.

Baron Silverlaine. Baron Silverlaine was the rightful human lord of the fortress once known as Keep Silverlaine, perched high above Pyrewood Village. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the savage worgen upon the region, the baron and his household were mercilessly slaughtered. Now, his tormented spirit lingers in the ruined dining hall, bound in undeath to defend the very lair that became his tomb. Before the shadow of the wolf-beasts blanketed the southern hills of Silverpine, Baron Silverlaine ruled over a proud noble estate. His fortress provided safety and oversight to the surrounding Gilnean lands. That peace shattered when Archmage Arugal, seeking a weapon against the rampaging Scourge, unleashed summoned worgen into the region. The feral monstrosities could not be controlled; they stormed the stronghold, overran its guards, and butchered the baron along with his entire family.

Baros Alexston. Baros Alexston is the Chief Architect of Stormwind City, stationed within the City Hall overlooking Cathedral Square. A former member of the Stonemasons Guild who helped rebuild the capital after the First War, he chose to accept an official post rather than follow his old friend Edwin VanCleef into open rebellion. Baros grew up on the Alexston Farmstead in the rolling grasslands of Westfall. During his youth, thieves overran and torched his family's homestead, forcing his father to hurriedly stash their most cherished heirlooms across the grounds before fleeing. Baros eventually journeyed to the capital and joined the Stonemasons Guild, dedicating years of grueling labor alongside Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef to raise Stormwind anew from the ashes of the First War.

Bazil Thredd. Bazil Thredd is Edwin VanCleef's lieutenant and most trusted assistant, locked in the Stormwind Stockade since the Stonemasons' riots that killed Queen Tiffin. Now the prison has risen in revolt, and Thredd leads the rioting Defias inmates from its eastern cell block. When the Stonemasons Guild was refused payment by the nobility of Stormwind for rebuilding the city, Edwin VanCleef rejected government appeasements and sparked open revolt. Bazil Thredd stood at VanCleef's side as his chief lieutenant and most trusted assistant. During the violent clashes that followed—which resulted in the death of Queen Tiffin Wrynn—Thredd was captured by the city guard. While VanCleef and the surviving masons fled into Westfall to form the Defias Brotherhood, Thredd was cast into the depths of the Stormwind Stockade.

Bazzalan. Bazzalan is a sinister satyr rogue lurking within the volcanic depths of Ragefire Chasm. Alongside Jergosh the Invoker, he commands the dark activities of the Searing Blade cult directly beneath the Horde capital of Orgrimmar. While Thrall works to establish the Orcs' new home across Durotar, ancient evils have found a roost beneath his feet. Bazzalan, a cunning satyr rogue, has allied with the Searing Blade cult inside the winding lava caverns of Ragefire Chasm. Swift and lethal with twin blades, he serves as one of the cult's primary field commanders.

Bethor Iceshard. Bethor Iceshard is a powerful Forsaken mage based in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Presiding over the arcane and shadow practitioners within the Temple of the Damned, he commands considerable authority in Sylvanas's realm. Beneath his chilly demeanor lies a past entwined with old friends torn apart by the Scourge. Standing within the Temple of the Damned, Bethor Iceshard oversees the practitioners of the arcane arts and shadow magic in the Undercity. Respected and feared for his intellect and icy resolve, Bethor wields sufficient political and magical weight to give direct instructions to provincial magistrates across Lordaeron. He directs agents of the Forsaken to secure valuable grimoires, investigate arcane anomalies, and stamp out rival powers that threaten the Undercity's dominion.

Billy Maclure. Billy Maclure is a mischievous young human boy living at the Maclure Vineyards in Elwynn Forest. Caught in the midst of a bitter feud between his family and the neighboring Stonefields, Billy's petty antics often cause trouble for both farms. His weakness for fresh pastries makes him easy to bribe when his shenanigans get out of hand. Billy Maclure can usually be found loitering outside the barn at the Maclure Vineyards, not far from the farmer Gerard Tiller. Growing up amidst the endless rows of grapevines, Billy spends much of his time dodging chores and running wild across the rural meadows of central Elwynn Forest. Like the rest of his kin, he is keenly aware of the long-standing hostility between the Maclures and the Stonefields, though Billy treats the feud more like a game of pranks and petty theft than a serious conflict.

Blind Hunter. The Blind Hunter is an elusive, albino bat that roosts deep within Razorfen Kraul. Unlike the ordinary bats nesting near the cavern entrances, this rare creature prowls the sunless depths of the quilboar redoubt. Razorfen Kraul is riddled with winding briars and dark subterranean caverns. While common Kraul bats roost nearer to the surface where faint light filters in from the outside world, the Blind Hunter has adapted entirely to the furthest, darkest alcoves of the tangle. Its pale, albino hide and milky gaze are likely the result of generations spent completely isolated from natural sunlight.

Blind Mary. Blind Mary is a tormented banshee haunting an abandoned, ruined farmhouse just southeast of Darkshire in Duskwood. Once a vain and beautiful mortal woman, her violent death and transformation drove her to self-inflicted mutilation in grief over what she had become. Before the shadows fell across Duskwood, Mary was known as a striking mortal woman who took immense pride in her beauty, rarely seen without her treasured looking glass. When the undead swept over the region, Mary was slain along with many of her neighbors. Unlike those who found rest in the earth, her spirit lingered on as an ethereal banshee, condemned to wander the mortal realm in a ghastly, translucent form.

Bloodmage Thalnos. Bloodmage Thalnos is a skeletal spellcaster who haunts the Graveyard wing of the Scarlet Monastery. Once a sadistic interrogator within the Scarlet Crusade, he succumbed to the plague of undeath he fanatically fought against, yet he remains entrenched deep within their holy grounds. Within the zealous ranks of the Scarlet Crusade, Thalnos earned dark notoriety for his brutal methods of torture, used under the guise of purifying prospective recruits of taint. Yet despite his fanatical devotion to rooting out corruption, the sadistic mage ultimately succumbed to the plague of undeath. Rather than being cleansed or permanently destroyed, he rose as a withered skeleton, still clinging to his fiery magic and arcane mastery.

Bolvar Fordragon. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon serves as the Regent of Stormwind and Supreme Commander of its armed forces following the mysterious disappearance of King Varian Wrynn. Standing beside the young boy-king Anduin Wrynn in Stormwind Keep, he strives to hold the kingdom together amid escalating domestic turmoil. Though fiercely honorable, Bolvar often finds his martial decisions influenced and stalled by royal advisor Lady Katrana Prestor. When King Varian vanished en route to a peace summit on Theramore Isle, Stormwind was thrown into political disarray. Ten-year-old Prince Anduin was crowned to maintain continuity, but actual governing power fell to Highlord Bolvar Fordragon as Regent. Bolvar is a venerated paladin devoted to the crown, yet he faces immense strain. Stormwind's military is thinly stretched across Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood. Compounding these crises, Bolvar frequently defers to the counsel of Lady Katrana Prestor, whose dismissive advice consistently blocks him from committing royal troops to peripheral towns.

Brewmaster Drohn. Brewmaster Drohn is an orcish brewmaster living just uphill from the bustling port of Ratchet. Having learned the art of exotic fermentation through ties connected to the legendary wandering pandaren Chen Stormstout, Drohn crafts potent beverages on the arid frontier of the Barrens. Adventurers who discover discarded kegs across Kalimdor often find themselves directed straight to his porch. Overlooking the goblin docks of Ratchet sits Brewmaster Drohn, an orc who has devoted his craft to the science of brewing rather than simple combat. Running Drohn's Distillery from his hillside home, he operates peacefully within the neutral haven established by Gazlowe's Steamwheedle cartel. While most orcs settle for coarse grog or simple spirits, Drohn's work involves rare ingredients, refined balances of flavor, and techniques rarely practiced among his kin.

Brine. Brine is an orc shaman residing in the arid hills of Blackthorn Ridge in the southern Barrens. As an expert on the spirits of water, she guides shaman initiates along the spiritual path to commune with the tides and earn their Water Totem. Perched upon a windswept hill in northern Blackthorn Ridge, Brine lives far from the bustling trading posts of the Barrens. Despite the dry savannas surrounding her, she has dedicated her life to understanding the fluid and fickle element of water. Shaman across the Horde are directed to seek her wisdom once they have mastered earth and fire, for water requires patience and perspective that few understand as deeply as she does.

Bruegal Ironknuckle. Bruegal Ironknuckle is an infamous dwarven prisoner held within the Stormwind Stockade. Unlike the petty criminals and rioting rabble that fill the holding cells, he is a formidable brawler whose presence deep inside the corridors spells immediate danger to anyone trying to restore order. When the Stormwind Stockade erupted into open revolt, many of the city's most volatile cutthroats took control of the subterranean cellblocks. Among them is Bruegal Ironknuckle, a particularly dangerous dwarf inmate known for brutal brawling strength. Rather than staying confined to a single cell, he prowls the riot-torn hallways, ready to bash anyone attempting to quell the uprising.

Cairne Bloodhoof. Cairne Bloodhoof is the venerable High Chieftain of the united tauren tribes and ruler of Thunder Bluff. A towering warrior of immense wisdom, he bound the fate of the tauren to Thrall's Horde after the orcs aided his people in escaping extinction at the hands of the centaur. For generations, the tauren lived as wandering nomads across the Barrens, continually hunted and driven toward extinction by savage centaur marauders. When Thrall and his orcs arrived on the shores of Kalimdor, Cairne recognized a rare nobility in them. Thrall offered military protection, escorting Cairne's desperate caravan across the plains to the safety of Mulgore in exchange for guidance to the Oracle at Stonetalon Peak. Settling upon the towering mesas of Thunder Bluff, Cairne finally established a permanent, unified home for all tauren tribes.

Calor. Calor is a dedicated resident of Darkshire who aids the Night Watch and the Carevin family in defending Duskwood. Operating under the direction of Jonathan Carevin, he actively coordinates efforts to hunt down the vicious worgen stalking the gloomy forests. Adventurers looking to push back the ravenous beasts haunting the woods often find their assignments through him. Stationed within the beleaguered settlement of Darkshire, Calor works closely with Jonathan Carevin, one of the town's prominent defenders. Amid the endless gloom and creeping terrors of Duskwood, Calor devotes himself to supporting the Carevin household's mission: eradicating the supernatural horrors encroaching upon the town's perimeter before the remaining townsfolk are slaughtered.

Canaga Earthcaller. Canaga Earthcaller is a Darkspear troll shaman stationed in the sunbaked Valley of Trials. He instructs novice Horde shamans in communing with the spirits of the land and obtaining their first elemental totems. Beyond ritual guidance, he keeps a watchful eye on wounded scouts and emerging threats near the Den. Perched on the red bluffs of the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller serves as one of the very first spiritual guides for Darkspear trolls and orcs who walk the path of the shaman. While many trainers focus strictly on martial readiness, Canaga teaches newcomers how to quiet their minds and listen to the rumblings of Kalimdor itself, preparing the earth sapta necessary to commune with the spirits.

Captain Grayson. Captain Grayson is the restless spirit of a pirate captain stationed at the Westfall Lighthouse. Having lost his own life when his ship smashed against the dark coastline, he now watches over the beacon to prevent other sailors from suffering his fate. In life, Grayson captained a vessel along the perilous southern seas of the Eastern Kingdoms. His voyage came to a violent end off the jagged shoals of Westfall on a night when the lighthouse fire had gone dark. Cast upon the rocks, Grayson perished alongside his ship, only to awaken as an earthbound phantom trapped upon the coast.

Captain Greenskin. Captain Greenskin is an elite goblin pirate overseeing the construction and crew of Edwin VanCleef's massive ironclad juggernaut. Hidden deep in the subterranean cove of the Deadmines, he commands the pirate forces hired by the Defias Brotherhood. His goal is to bring the warship to readiness to sail against Stormwind. Pacing the main deck of the gigantic juggernaut under construction in the Deadmines cove, Captain Greenskin represents the naval backbone of the Defias conspiracy. A seasoned goblin mariner who previously operated out of Booty Bay, Greenskin was brought into Edwin VanCleef's inner circle to turn an underground cavern into a drydock for an engine of war.

Captain Stoutfist. Captain Stoutfist is the dwarven officer in charge of military defenses at Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. With the Dragonmaw clan pushing aggressively out of their marshland strongholds, Stoutfist coordinates defensive maneuvers and counter-offensives to ensure the vital Alliance port does not fall. Menethil Harbor serves as the principal deepwater port connecting Ironforge and Stormwind to the marshy lowlands of the Wetlands and the sea beyond. As the town's commanding officer, Captain Stoutfist bears the heavy burden of keeping its docks, civilian populace, and garrison secure against surrounding threats. The marshlands are notoriously hazardous, but the biggest peril to the settlement is an organized surge from renegade orcs.

Carendin Halgar. Carendin Halgar is a prominent Forsaken warlock trainer residing in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Sharp-tongued and notoriously short on patience, he oversees the training of fledgling practitioners of the dark arts. He instructs aspiring warlocks on how to subjugate powerful demonic entities from the Twisting Nether, notably teaching the rituals to bind Voidwalkers and Succubi. Within the noxious gloom of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Carendin Halgar instructs those who delve into the Twisting Nether. He demands focus and obedience, holding little tolerance for failure, hesitation, or weakness. Under his watchful gaze, warlocks are pushed beyond basic incantations into the dangerous mastery of summonings and soul manipulation, cementing the Forsaken's ruthless approach to demonic servitude.

Charlga Razorflank. Charlga Razorflank, widely known as the Crone of the Kraul, is the fierce and cunning geomancer chieftain presiding over Razorfen Kraul. Under her leadership, the Razorfen quilboar drove the tauren out of the southern Barrens through ruthless expansion. Within the tangled, massive brambles of Razorfen Kraul rules Charlga Razorflank. Revered by her people as a master geomancer whose experimental magic remains unmatched among quilboar, Charlga organized her fractious kin into a unified, lethal threat. She harnessed the primal earth and giant thorns sprouting from the demigod Agamaggan's remains, reshaping the labyrinthine Kraul into an impenetrable fortress.

Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII is a veteran dwarven engineer stationed atop the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan. Tasked with the upkeep and defense of this monumental feat of engineering, he oversees its delicate mechanisms while keeping watch for sabotage. Those who speak with him quickly discover that grave dangers threaten the integrity of the great dam. The Stonewrought Dam is one of the crowning achievements of dwarven stonecraft and engineering, holding back the massive waters of the Loch. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII bears the immense responsibility of maintaining its structure and operational machinery. Perched along the crest of the dam, he monitors the waterways, sluice gates, and structural stress points against the elements and local hazards.

Chief Hawkwind. Chief Hawkwind is the tribal leader of Camp Narache, the proving grounds nestled in the Red Cloud Mesa of Mulgore. Responsible for guiding the youth of the Shu'halo, he mentors new adventurers as they embark on their traditional rites of passage. Under his watchful gaze, young braves learn humility, respect for the land, and the strength needed to protect their people. Standing at the heart of Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind carries the solemn responsibility of preparing the next generation of tauren for the wider world. Red Cloud Mesa serves as a sheltered haven where fledgling hunters, shamans, druids, and warriors undertake the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. Hawkwind oversees these customs, ensuring that every youth learns duty and endurance before venturing beyond the safety of the mesa.

Clerk Daltry. Clerk Daltry is the civic record keeper stationed in Darkshire Town Hall in Duskwood. Surrounded by ledgers and registry books, he helps investigate the village's past and track down historical records, even if his archives are somewhat neglected and out of date. While Darkshire struggles against encroaching beasts, undead horrors, and supernatural gloom, everyday civic duties fall to Clerk Daltry. Working out of the Darkshire Town Hall alongside Lord Ello Ebonlocke and the local council, Daltry maintains the town's historical ledgers, property rolls, and census data. In a region fractured by disaster, his records are among the few surviving links to the days before Grand Hamlet fell into shadow.

Cliffwatcher Longhorn. Cliffwatcher Longhorn is the stoic tauren leader stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Tasked with safeguarding the isolated Horde outpost, he coordinates defenses against encroaching Galak centaur and monitors the suspicious machinations of the Grimtotem tribe. Perched upon the soaring rock spires of Thousand Needles, Freewind Post relies on sharp eyes and steady leadership to survive. Cliffwatcher Longhorn oversees the day-to-day security of this precarious settlement. With hostile forces gathering on the canyon floor below and along neighboring ridges, Longhorn acts as the settlement's primary coordinator for scouting reports and defensive military efforts.

Coleman Farthing. Coleman Farthing is a bitter Forsaken survivor residing in the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. In life, he worked for the wealthy Agamand dynasty at their extensive flour mills in northern Tirisfal. Convinced to stay and defend the estate against the Scourge, he died alongside his fellow laborers, and now dedicates his undeath to exacting vengeance on his former masters. Before the Third War, Coleman Farthing earned an honest living as a laborer at the Agamand Mills, the largest milling and agricultural operation in Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge poured across Lordaeron, the aristocratic Agamand family refused to flee their valuable lands. Instead, they urged their household and laborers to take up arms alongside them, promising they could hold the farmsteads against the undead horde. Coleman and his fellow workers stayed, believing their masters—a decision that cost every last one of them their lives.

Collin Mauren. Collin Mauren is a human mage residing in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind City. A scholarly researcher and crafter of incantations, he experiments with exotic natural reagents to devise unique utility spells. Among his pursuits is assisting his acquaintance, the gnome engineer and explorer Gaxim Rustfizzle, with specialized arcane scrolls. Situated within Stormwind's bustling Mage Quarter, Collin Mauren spends his days pursuing the quieter, more practical applications of magic. Rather than chasing raw elemental power, he focuses on crafting arcane formulas that solve specific, logistical problems. Collin often turns to natural anomalies and raw components scavenged across Azeroth, weaving their intrinsic properties into functional magic scrolls and reagents for friends and travelers alike.

Commander Springvale. Commander Springvale was once a devoted paladin and the head of Baron Silverlaine's armed guard at Shadowfang Keep. Slain alongside his men during the feral worgen slaughter orchestrated by Archmage Arugal, his vengeful spirit remains behind to haunt the castle halls. Even in death, his ghost fiercely guards the keep and seeks vengeance for his fallen master. Before the ruin of Shadowfang Keep, Commander Springvale stood as an honorable paladin dedicated to the Holy Light and a sworn defender of Baron Silverlaine. Leading the garrison in Silverpine Forest, he oversaw the keep's security during the fraught days following the fall of Lordaeron to the Scourge.

Cookie. Cookie is an elite murloc serving as the ship's cook aboard the juggernaut hidden deep within the Deadmines. An unusual recruit among the Defias Brotherhood, he tends the crew's cauldrons beneath the watchful eye of Captain Greenskin and Edwin VanCleef. He is the only entirely optional boss encountered within the underground dry dock. Beneath the decks of the towering juggernaut in the Ironclad Cove, cooking duty falls neither to a human outrider nor a goblin engineer, but to a solitary murloc known simply as Cookie. How he secured the position remains a private secret kept by Edwin VanCleef himself. Whatever doubts the rest of the crew might harbor about a murloc presiding over their rations, pirates are rarely in a position to be picky, and in the underworld of Moonbrook, a meal is a meal.

Corithras Moonrage. Corithras Moonrage is a night elf scholar and quest giver stationed in the village of Dolanaar on Teldrassil. He guides newly arrived adventurers in understanding the nature of the great World Tree and tasks them with maintaining its sacred moonwells. Through his lessons, he reveals both the spiritual importance of Teldrassil and the growing burdens carried by the kaldorei. Residing in the shaded settlement of Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage serves as an instructor to travelers leaving the sheltered bounds of Shadowglen. As young kaldorei venture into the wider boughs of Teldrassil, Corithras ensures they understand the history of their new home. He teaches that survival in this changing era requires vigilance and reverence for the natural order.

Dalar Dawnweaver. Dalar Dawnweaver is a former archmage of Dalaran who now serves the Forsaken at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Slain during the Scourge's destruction of the magi's city and later freed from the Lich King's control, he turns his magical intellect toward dissecting regional threats. From the shadows of the tomb, he directs efforts to understand Dalaran's lingering presence and undo the madness of Archmage Arugal. In life, Dalar Dawnweaver held high rank among the Kirin Tor, walking the halls of the Violet Citadel when Dalaran was a pinnacle of arcane mastery. His mortal life ended when the Scourge sacked the city to pave the way for Archimonde's summoning. Reanimated into the mindless thrall of the Lich King, Dalar broke free alongside Lady Sylvanas Windrunner when the Scourge's grip faltered. Now stationed at the Sepulcher, he retains the piercing intellect of an archmage, turned entirely toward safeguarding the Forsaken realm.

Daphne Stilwell. Daphne Stilwell tends an isolated orchard nestled atop the coastal cliffs of Westfall overlooking the Longshore. Together with her husband Jordan, she fled turmoil in the north and relocated south, quietly aiding the Church of the Holy Light while defending her home from nearby outlaws. Perched on the bluffs to the west of Moonbrook and the exit of the Deadmines, Daphne Stilwell manages a secluded homestead and apple orchard. From below along the Longshore or above on gryphon routes south to Stranglethorn Vale, the small farm looks quiet and unassuming. Yet running a homestead in modern Westfall is anything but safe. Despite the encroaching bandits and roaming scavengers, Daphne diligently works her trees and keeps watch over her isolated patch of land.

Dark Iron Ambassador. Deep within the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan lurks the Dark Iron Ambassador, an elusive emissary sent by Emperor Dagran Thaurissan. His presence reveals that the fall of the gnome capital involves far more than just wild trogg incursions and madness. While Gnomeregan's catastrophic downfall is publicly blamed on the trogg invasion and High Tinker Mekkatorque's desperate radiation gambit, the presence of the Dark Iron Ambassador points to far darker machinations. Wandering the contaminated depths of the workshop corridors, this rare Dark Iron dwarf suggests that Sicco Thermaplugg did not betray his people in complete isolation.

Darsok Swiftdagger. Darsok Swiftdagger is an orc warrior and scout stationed at the Crossroads in the heart of the Barrens. Known for his fierce hatred of harpies, he directs Horde adventurers north into the Dry Hills to break the avian matriarchy harassing travelers and settlements. He maintains ties across the plains, serving as a trusted contact for Witch Doctor Jin'Zil in Malaka'jin. Amid the bustling hub of the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger keeps a sharp eye on the threats creeping out of the northern scrubland. The trade artery connecting Durotar, Mulgore, and the northern reaches is under constant siege, not only from raiders and centaur, but from organized aerial hunters. Darsok focuses his wrath on the Witchwing harpies, whose roosts in the Dry Hills northwest of the Forgotten Pools directly threaten northern caravans.

Deathguard Dillinger. Deathguard Dillinger is a Forsaken sentry stationed in Brill within Tirisfal Glades. Standing watch over the town's perimeter, he directs newly arrived undead toward necessary services and tasks recruits with keeping the local Scourge remnants at bay. As a member of the Forsaken Deathguard, Dillinger stands at the entrance of Brill, serving as both a frontline protector and an orienting guide for travelers emerging from Deathknell. He provides directions to town amenities such as the inn, the town hall, and local trainers, helping newly awakened undead navigate their new reality under the Dark Lady's rule.

Delgren the Purifier. Delgren the Purifier is a human paladin stationed at Maestra's Post on the northern edge of Ashenvale. Operating alongside comrades Balthule Shadowstrike and Feero Ironhand, he aids the night elves in cleansing demonic and shadow magic threatening the frontier, with a particular focus on the sinister Cult of the Dark Strand. Human paladins are a rare sight deep within the ancient forests of Kalimdor, but Delgren the Purifier arrived with a mission. Affiliated with the Argent Dawn, Delgren traveled west with a cadre of holy warriors determined to assist the Alliance's new night elf allies against the lingering evils of demons and undead remnants from the Third War. Stationed near the border of Darkshore and Ashenvale, he maintains a watchful vigil over travelers passing south from Auberdine.

Denalan. Denalan is an accomplished night elf herbalist and botanist who tends a quiet lakeside plot along the eastern shore of Lake Al'Ameth. Working under a simple awning, he devotes his days to studying the island's plant life and seeking botanical remedies for the strange corruption affecting Teldrassil. He frequently enlists young adventurers to gather samples, study violent timberlings, and test enchanted soils. While many kaldorei focus on martial vigilance or high druidic rites, Denalan pursues the patient, meticulous craft of herbalism. Stationed along the tranquil eastern banks of Lake Al'Ameth, he has established a modest research camp consisting of a cloth awning, simple field tools, and tidy rows of cultivated planter boxes. Rather than retreating to the grand barrows of Darnassus, he prefers to remain close to the loam, directly examining the unusual flora that has sprouted since the planting of the new World Tree.

Dendrite Starblaze. Dendrite Starblaze is a night elf druid residing in the sacred village of Nighthaven within Moonglade. Serving the Cenarion Circle, he acts as a vital mentor and guide for budding druids of both night elf and tauren descent. Through him, practitioners are summoned to the holy grove to master essential rites such as cleansing toxins and communing with nature's forms. Perched within Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze represents the nonpartisan, enduring spirit of the Cenarion Circle. When novice druids learn to attune their spirits to Teleport: Moonglade, Dendrite is among the first to welcome them upon arrival. He bridges the gap between ancient Kaldorei tradition and the emerging path of the tauren, treating all who heed the call of the wild as kin beneath the boughs of the sacred haven.

Devrak. Devrak is an orc wind rider master stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Serving as the primary aerial conduit of central Kalimdor, he oversees the Horde's network of wyverns shuttling supplies and couriers between Durotar, Mulgore, and frontier outposts. He also ensures that crucial logistics, such as game meats and prepared hides, travel smoothly to the Horde's capitals. Positioned at the intersection of Kalimdor's major trade routes, Devrak tends the wyverns that keep the Horde unified across vast distances. The Crossroads sits exposed under the baking sun, vulnerable to quillboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts alike, making rapid aerial transit indispensable. Devrak handles both seasoned wayfarers and untested messengers, pairing riders with trained wind riders capable of crossing the savannah and reaching the mountain heights of Mulgore or the stone canyons of Durotar.

Dextren Ward. Dextren Ward is an infamous criminal and grave robber locked away inside the Stormwind Stockade. Before his capture, he profited by exhuming bodies from Duskwood's Raven Hill Cemetery and delivering them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Now caught in the midst of the prison's bloody uprising, he remains marked for death by the town council of Darkshire. Before ending up in chains beneath the streets of Stormwind, Dextren Ward conducted a grim and lucrative business in the fog-choked woods of Duskwood. Raven Hill Cemetery was already a site of sorrow and growing horror, but Ward treated its burial grounds as a private quarry. Rather than hunting merely for trinkets and heirlooms left with the dead, Ward dealt in flesh, unearthing fresh graves to supply local dark practitioners.

Dirania Silvershine. Dirania Silvershine is a night elf resident of Shadowglen in Teldrassil. Deeply loyal and observant, she watches over the tranquil grove and looks out for her companion Iverron when his reckless ventures land him in peril. Dirania stands among the tranquil boughs of Shadowglen, the secluded vale where young night elves begin their service to Kalimdor and the Alliance. While many in the barrow mounds and sanctuaries look to broad spiritual duties, Dirania stays mindful of those nearest to her, attentive to the quiet dangers that stir even in the heart of Teldrassil.

Dorn Plainstalker. Dorn Plainstalker is a solitary tauren elder residing in the Weathered Nook overlooking the canyons of Thousand Needles. He serves as an overseer of traditional rite of passage trials, challenging Horde adventurers to prove their character and fortitude. Through trials of faith, endurance, strength, and lore, he tests whether travelers are worthy servants of the Earth Mother and their people. Secluded in a shallow cave high atop the canyon ridges of the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker lives apart from the bustle of Freewind Post. Reaching his mountain redoubt requires winding along the sheer northern cliffs overlooking the towering mesas below. From this quiet vantage point, Dorn maintains ancient customs and judges those who seek guidance in the harsh southern barrens.

Duthorian Rall. Duthorian Rall is a respected human knight of the Silver Hand stationed within Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. Renowned as one of the most influential paladins in the Alliance, he oversees the training and spiritual trials of emerging holy warriors. He guides recruits through solemn vows of charity, valor, and devotion to defend Azeroth against the Scourge and lurking domestic threats. Standing within the vaulted transept of the Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall represents the venerable traditions of the Knights of the Silver Hand. With the kingdom unsettled by internal strife and the missing King Varian Wrynn, Duthorian shoulders the vital duty of instilling righteous discipline in fresh initiates. Respected paladins in the field, including Brother Wilhelm in Northshire and Brandur Ironhammer in Ironforge, direct promising recruits to his guidance to begin their sacred trials.

Edwin VanCleef. Edwin VanCleef was the brilliant Guildmaster of the Stonemasons who rebuilt Stormwind City after the Second War. After being cheated of payment by the House of Nobles, he led a violent workers' revolt and formed the outlaw Defias Brotherhood. Operating from deep within the Deadmines of Westfall, he seeks vengeance against the kingdom he helped restore. Following the devastation of the First War, Edwin VanCleef was chosen to lead the Stonemasons Guild in the monumental task of rebuilding Stormwind City. A peerless craftsman and an idealist, VanCleef directed the construction of the capital's grand ramparts and towering cathedrals, and even oversaw the erection of Nethergarde Keep to watch over the Dark Portal. Alongside his mastery of architecture, VanCleef was a remarkably deadly operative; he was trained in stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft by his childhood friend, Mathias Shaw.

Eitrigg. Eitrigg is a seasoned veteran of the First and Second Wars who stands beside Warchief Thrall as an esteemed advisor in Orgrimmar. Once a high-ranking lieutenant of the Blackrock clan, he became disillusioned with the old demonic Horde and lived in exile until an extraordinary friendship with a human paladin changed his fate. Today, he helps guide the New Horde back to its roots of honor and shamanism. Born on Draenor into the Blackrock clan, Eitrigg was once one of Warchief Blackhand's primary lieutenants alongside Orgrim Doomhammer and Varok Saurfang. When Doomhammer seized leadership of the Horde, Eitrigg remained a trusted officer and oversaw the captured half-orc assassin Garona. Although he initially dismissed her revelations regarding Gul'dan and the demonic corruption of the Shadow Council, the horrific battles and ultimate defeat of the Horde in the Second War forced him to confront the dark reality. Sickened by the realization of how his people had been manipulated, Eitrigg walked away from the scattered remnants and retreated into self-imposed exile, seeking only solitude in the wilds of Lordaeron.

Electrocutioner 6000. The Electrocutioner 6000 is a deadly, super-charged spider tank deployed to defend the Launch Bay within the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan. Piloted by the notorious leper gnome Lieutenant Tom 'Sizzlepants' Crankle, it represents Mekgineer Thermaplugg's reckless ambition to weaponize high-voltage electricity. Mekgineer Thermaplugg has never been known for rigorous safety testing. Driven by megalomania and haste, he regularly rushes unproven war machines straight from the drawing board into live combat. The Electrocutioner 6000 was his initial attempt to harness raw electrical currents as an offensive system mounted to an armored spider tank chassis. Rather than working out lethal power surges in a laboratory, Thermaplugg sent it immediately to guard the upper tiers of Gnomeregan's Launch Bay.

Elling Trias. Elling Trias manages Trias' Cheese, a small storefront nestled in the bustling Trade District of Stormwind City. While he presents himself as a jovial and passionate purveyor of dairy, he quietly operates as one of the kingdom's most connected information brokers. Behind wheels of cheese and cordial banter, Trias maintains an ear to the ground that reaches across continents. To the casual customer strolling the Trade District, Elling Trias is merely an artisan dedicated to fine curds, working his shop alongside his wife Elaine and son Ben. He enthusiastically hawks wheels of cheese and chats amicably with townsfolk. Yet those in the know understand that Trias' Cheese is one of the most reliable fronts in Stormwind. The steady hum of city commerce provides perfect cover for operatives, courtiers, and adventurers who need to trade quiet words without drawing the attention of the city watch.

Executor Arren. Executor Arren is a high-ranking Forsaken officer stationed in Deathknell. He oversees the immediate defense and consolidation of the settlement as newly awakened undead emerge from their graves. Arren coordinates the local campaign against mindless Scourge zombies, feral beasts, and the encroaching zealots of the Scarlet Crusade. Standing resolute just outside the chapel in Deathknell, Executor Arren serves as the primary military voice for the nascent Forsaken within their awakening grounds. While the caretakers in the crypts guide newly raised undead through their disorientation, Arren directs their focus outward toward survival. Under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner's banner, he organizes local operations to sweep away mindless zombies that threaten the village borders, establishing secure territory in the shadow of Lordaeron's fall.

Executor Zygand. Executor Zygand is a senior Forsaken commander stationed at the town hall in Brill, overseeing defensive and military operations across central Tirisfal Glades. Reporting directly to the Undercity's high command, he coordinates the purge of Scarlet Crusade forces pressing into Forsaken territory. Positioned at the administrative heart of Brill, Executor Zygand coordinates regional defense for the Forsaken after their initial awakening in Deathknell. Serving as the direct superior to regional officers like Executor Arren and field sentries such as Deathguard Linnea, Zygand synthesizes scout intelligence and dispatches able recruits to safeguard Lordaeron's borders from encroachment.

Fandral Staghelm. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the druids of the Cenarion Circle from the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. Stepping into power after Malfurion Stormrage vanished into the Emerald Dream, he championed the planting of the new World Tree, Teldrassil. Proud, abrasive, and relentlessly ambitious, Fandral advocates for an aggressive Kaldorei resurgence that frequently pits him against High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Following the Third War and the sacrifice of Nordrassil atop Mount Hyjal, the night elves lost their immortality and their sacred sanctuary. While Malfurion Stormrage cautioned patience and warned against vanity, Fandral championed the bold creation of a new World Tree off the coast of Kalimdor. When Malfurion subsequently fell comatose within the Emerald Dream, Fandral seized the initiative and led the druids in raising Teldrassil. He envisioned the colossal bough as a monument to Kaldorei endurance and a vessel to restore their lost supremacy, even though the Dragon Aspects pointedly withheld their blessings from the unapproved endeavor.

Farthing. Bishop Farthing is a human clergyman residing within the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City. To visitors and worshippers, he presents himself as a devout servant of the Holy Light who guides parishioners and directs aid toward beleaguered settlements across the kingdom. Within the serene marble halls of the Cathedral of Light, Bishop Farthing stands as one of the prominent figures attending to the spiritual needs of Stormwind City. Alongside Archbishop Benedictus and the gathered clergy, he offers counsel to travelers, assists those pursuing the holy arts, and attends to the civic and pastoral obligations of the Church of the Holy Light.

Fenrus the Devourer. Fenrus the Devourer is an enormous worg that prowls the upper sanctum of Shadowfang Keep. Kept as a personal pet and guardian by Archmage Arugal, the ravenous beast is bloated on unnatural magics. Anyone daring to breach the archmage's personal study must contend with this feral horror and the master who watches over it. Deep within Shadowfang Keep, just outside Archmage Arugal's personal chambers, lurks the monstrous worg known as Fenrus the Devourer. Unlike the lupine worgen roaming the ramparts, Fenrus is an actual worg, swollen to gargantuan proportions. Prowling the shelves, scrolls, and arcane apparatuses of Arugal's private study, the beast serves both as a pet and as a violent perimeter guard against any intruder seeking the mad mage's head.

First Mate Fitzsimmons. First Mate Fitzsimmons is a ragged, reeking sailor who spends his days drinking outside the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Once the first mate aboard the Wave Mistress of the Kul Tiras Third Fleet, he is the sole known living survivor of the fleet's destruction during the Second War. Haunted by the tragedy, he seeks willing adventurers to face the restless spirits of his drowned comrades. Lounging outside the Deepwater Tavern amid the damp salt air of Menethil Harbor, First Mate Fitzsimmons is an easy man to overlook—or avoid entirely, given his unwashed stench. To most patrons, he is just another broken old salt drinking his memories away. Yet those willing to sit and listen will hear harrowing tales of a proud fleet brought low by fire and claw.

Foreman Oslow. Foreman Oslow is Lakeshire's beleaguered master builder, tasked with repairing the ruined Everstill Bridge in the heart of Redridge Mountains. Beset by Blackrock orc artillery and gnoll raiders, his reconstruction efforts have stalled due to lost shipments and sunken equipment. He relies heavily on traveling adventurers to retrieve his gear and secure materials so Lakeshire can reconnect its vital trade route. Standing by the fractured masonry of the Everstill Bridge, Foreman Oslow faces an uphill battle. The bridge is the lifeline of Lakeshire, spanning the expanse of Lake Everstill and linking the western roads toward Elwynn to the eastern shores. Blackrock orcs, sweeping down from the crags of Stonewatch, targeted the crossing to cripple the town's logistics and military movement, leaving the settlement splintered and vulnerable.

Furen Longbeard. Furen Longbeard is a master dwarven armorer stationed within Stormwind City's bustling Dwarven District. Apprenticed under the renowned smith Grimand Elmore, he specializes in crafting heavy protective gear and sturdy mail for seasoned defenders of the Alliance. Warriors across the kingdom seek out his metallurgical expertise to forge specialized, battle-ready armor. Furen Longbeard plies his craft far from the great forges of Ironforge, making his home instead among the cobblestones and soot of Stormwind's Dwarven District. Like many of his kin, Furen brought traditional dwarven metallurgy south to support the rebuilding and defense of the kingdom. Working amidst blazing hearths and clanging anvils, he maintains strong ties with other artisans throughout the city and beyond.

Gakin the Darkbinder. Gakin the Darkbinder is a master warlock operating covertly deep beneath The Slaughtered Lamb tavern in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. He instructs aspiring Alliance practitioners in the dark arts, testing their resolve before initiating rituals to summon and bind otherworldly demons to their service. While Stormwind's mages practice openly in their towering sanctuaries, practitioners of shadow and fel must dwell where prying eyes cannot reach. Hidden below the taproom of The Slaughtered Lamb is a damp crypt-like cellar equipped with summoning circles and grim tomes. Gakin serves as the anchor of this hidden conclave, ensuring that young warlocks learn discipline and restraint before unleashing horrors they cannot control.

Gan'rul Bloodeye. Gan'rul Bloodeye is a senior orc warlock trainer residing deep within the dark cavern of the Cleft of Shadow in Orgrimmar. Hidden away from the watchful gaze of the city above, he initiates Horde warlocks into darker demonic rites. Under his instruction, initiates learn to bend otherworldly entities like voidwalkers and succubi to their will. While Warchief Thrall tolerates the presence of warlocks in the new Horde, their dark arts are not welcomed in the open sunlight of Durotar. Gan'rul Bloodeye makes his home in the Cleft of Shadow, a subterranean refuge beneath Orgrimmar where shadow weavers, rogues, and fel casters can study unmolested. From this subterranean perch, Gan'rul serves as a primary tutor for rising practitioners of fel magic.

Gann Stonespire. Gann Stonespire is an aggrieved tauren nomad found wandering the roads of the southern Barrens near Bael Modan. Driven from his tribe's ancestral hunting grounds by dwarven excavators, he seeks retaliation against the encroaching dig site. Before the dwarven expedition arrived from Ironforge to carve out the fortress of Bael Modan, the surrounding land served as ancestral territory and hunting grounds for Gann Stonespire's tribe. The dwarven miners drove the indigenous tauren from their soil with pickaxes, firearms, and heavy machinery, refusing peaceful overtures. Now camping along the dusty southern Barrens road, Gann refuses to quietly surrender his heritage, marshaling travelers to strike back at the excavators.

Gaxim Rustfizzle. Gaxim Rustfizzle is an ambitious gnome scholar and tinker stationed at a small Alliance camp along the Webwinder Path in Stonetalon Mountains. A representative of the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, he seeks to prove to skeptical night elves that advanced artifice and alchemy can preserve their woodland realm. His scientific curiosity is matched by a fierce vendetta against the destructive operations of the Venture Company. While night elves traditionally rely on ancient druidism and nature magic, Gaxim Rustfizzle arrived in the craggy passes of Stonetalon to demonstrate a radically different perspective. Representing the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, he genuinely believes that calculated mechanisms and chemical solutions can defend and restore Kalimdor's wilderness just as effectively as prayers to Elune. Camped alongside the sentinel Kaela Shadowspear on the Webwinder Path, he works tirelessly to convince his tall, reclusive allies of engineering's ecological merits.

Gazrog. Gazrog is an orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads in the heart of the Barrens. Tasked with maintaining logistics and security along the savannah's perilous roads, he recruits able Horde travelers to deal with regional threats and investigate lost patrols. The Crossroads serves as the vital junction for all Horde transit through Kalimdor, but its isolation leaves supply lines vulnerable to marauders and beasts alike. Gazrog stands watch alongside the settlement's defenders, working to ensure that cargo, coin, and couriers reach their destinations. Maintaining order in a sprawling wilderness requires constant vigilance, and Gazrog relies heavily on passing adventurers to handle crises brewing beyond the outpost's stockades.

Gelbin Mekkatorque. Gelbin Mekkatorque is the High Tinker of the gnomes, currently residing in exile in Tinker Town within Ironforge. Renowned as a visionary engineer whose inventions include the mechanostrider and the Deeprun Tram, he now carries the heavy burden of Gnomeregan's fall and oversees efforts to reclaim his people's ancestral home. Gnomish leadership is earned through intellect and merit rather than bloodlines, and Gelbin Mekkatorque's rise to High Tinker was propelled by pure inventive genius. A graduate of Gearshaft University, Mekkatorque revolutionized personal transportation with the creation of the first functioning mechanostrider. Over decades of innovation, he drafted the gyromatic micro-adjustor, automated repair bots, and partnered with the Bronzebeard dwarves to engineer their formidable siege engines. When Stormwind required a rapid transit connection to Ironforge after the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard turned to Mekkatorque, who personally drew the schematics and oversaw construction of the subterranean Deeprun Tram.

Gelihast. Gelihast is a ferocious, twin-blade wielding murloc chieftain residing in the Pool of Ask'ar within Blackfathom Deeps. Lured by the dark whispers of the Old Gods, he butchered his way into the sunken temple ruins before earning the reluctant respect of the Twilight's Hammer cultists. While most murlocs stay near coastal shallows, Gelihast felt the dark, ominous tug of the Old Gods deep beneath Ashenvale. Driven by these primordial whispers, he forced his way into the sunken temple of Blackfathom Deeps. When Twilight's Hammer cultists tried to halt his path, he slaughtered nearly a dozen of them single-handedly using his twin swords.

Ghamoo-ra. Ghamoo-ra is an ancient, giant sea turtle inhabiting the Pool of Ask'ar within Blackfathom Deeps. Once a peaceful denizen of Elune's sunken temple, he was captured, tortured, and driven mad by the Twilight's Hammer cult to serve as a vicious guardian. Before the defilement of Blackfathom Deeps, Ghamoo-ra was among the last peaceful natural inhabitants dwelling among the flooded ruins of the night elven temple dedicated to Elune. When the nihilistic Twilight's Hammer cult took control of the sanctuary, they roused the ancient turtle from his quiet life and locked him in captivity. Rather than slain, he was systematically tormented for years, suffering mental and physical flaying at the hands of the cultists.

Gilnid. Gilnid, known as the Smelter, is the goblin master engineer running the forges in the depths of the Deadmines. He oversees the smelting of raw ore into refined metal and munitions for Edwin VanCleef's hidden ironclad juggernaut. Without his fiery operations, the Defias Brotherhood would lack the heavy cannons needed to assault Stormwind. Deep within the Deadmines, the Defias Brotherhood relies on industrial expertise to forge weapons of war. Gilnid serves as VanCleef's head smelter, commanding a small army of goblin laborers, tinkers, and smiths in the central foundry. Towering over most of his kin, he drives his crew relentlessly through smoke and slag, barking orders and refusing breaks to ensure raw iron ore is processed into heavy plating and lethal ordnance.

Glorin Steelbrow. Glorin Steelbrow is a dwarven operative found drinking at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Acting as an associate of Bishop Farthing of Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, he helps adventurers investigate the lost Third Fleet and recover sacred relics and materials scattered across the Wetlands coast. His efforts tie the haunted wilderness of Duskwood directly to the sunken shipwrecks of the north. While Bishop Farthing aids the people of Duskwood against its creeping terrors from Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, he maintains ties far to the north in Menethil Harbor. Stationed inside the bustling Deepwater Tavern, Glorin Steelbrow acts as Farthing's eyes and hands on the coast. He offers aid and direction to travelers sent north in search of sacred metals and forgotten relics, providing a crucial bridge between the troubles of the southern forest and the sunken wreckage of the Wetlands.

Gornek. Gornek is an orc overseer stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. He serves as the primary point of intake for fresh orc and Darkspear troll recruits preparing to prove their worth to the New Horde. Standing directly at the heart of the Valley of Trials, Gornek represents the initial test of discipline for aspiring Horde warriors, scouts, and spellcasters. Under Warchief Thrall's order, every youth and newcomer must earn their place through grit and perseverance rather than entitlement. Gornek assesses those stepping into the valley, reading their introductory orders and directing them to trainers throughout the compound. Whether an initiate carries an encrypted scrawl, a glyphic parchment, or a simple tablet, it is Gornek who receives their credentials and sets them upon their harsh path of survival.

Grelin Whitebeard. Grelin Whitebeard is a dwarven scout stationed in Coldridge Valley by royal decree to assess the Frostmane troll threat. Operating out of an isolated camp with a bumbling apprentice, he relies on rising adventurers to keep the trolls contained while Ironforge's attention remains consumed by the trogg crisis. Grelin Whitebeard and his brother Senir were dispatched to Coldridge Valley under direct orders from the Senate of Ironforge and King Magni Bronzebeard himself. Their mission was clear: assess and neutralize the threat posed by the native Frostmane trolls. With Ironforge's official military fully bogged down combating trogg outbreaks across Dun Morogh, the brothers were given very few resources to accomplish their task. Grelin had to establish an outpost in the snowy hills and look toward local recruits and passing initiates to carry out the necessary work.

Grif Wildheart. Grif Wildheart is a seasoned dwarven hunter trainer stationed outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Renowned among the local mountaineers for his deep affinity with wildlife, he instructs budding marksmen in tracking, marksmanship, and the rites of beast taming. For young hunters emerging from Coldridge Valley, Grif provides the vital bridge between firing a rifle and walking alongside a loyal animal companion. While many Ironforge dwarves prefer the fiery warmth of a forge or the steady clink of pickaxes, Grif Wildheart has dedicated his life entirely to the frozen wilderness of Dun Morogh. Local mountaineers half-jokingly say he spends a bit too much time with four-legged beasts, but none dispute his mastery of the wild. Having spent years tracking across snowbound ridges alongside seasoned hunting companions, Grif possesses an intimate understanding of the natural predators that roam the crags.

Gryan Stoutmantle. Gryan Stoutmantle is a paladin of the Silver Hand and the commander of the People's Militia, operating out of Sentinel Hill in Westfall. Born in Westfall, he returned from the devastated northern kingdom of Lordaeron to protect his homeland after Stormwind's crown abandoned the region to banditry. Gryan Stoutmantle began his service far from the quiet fields of southern Azeroth. Traveling north to Lordaeron as a young man, he took vows as a Knight of the Silver Hand and endured the horrors of the Third War, even witnessing the tragic purge of Stratholme by Prince Arthas Menethil. When news reached him that his native province of Westfall was collapsing into lawlessness, overrun by organized brigands and abandoned by the crown, Gryan left the northern fronts behind. He traded imperial battlefields for the defense of honest farmers, swearing that his home would not fall as the north had.

Guard Thomas. Guard Thomas is a dedicated soldier of the Stormwind Army stationed at the bridge west of the Eastvale Logging Camp. Isolated on the eastern frontier of Elwynn Forest, he oversees the defense of local settlers against predatory wildlife and encroaching murlocs. While much of the realm's attention is focused inward toward the capital or west toward Westfall, Guard Thomas holds one of the quietest yet most precarious posts in Elwynn Forest. Positioned at the stone bridge crossing the river toward Eastvale Logging Camp, Thomas acts as the thin blue line between everyday forestry workers and the aggressive creatures roaming the woods. With the Stormwind military stretched thin, guards like Thomas must rely heavily on passing adventurers to maintain order and carry messages back to central command.

Gunther Arcanus. Gunther Arcanus is an exceptionally powerful necromancer dwelling on an isolated island in Brightwater Lake. Slain during the Third War and raised into undeath, he managed to shatter the Lich King's mental grip entirely on his own. Long believing he was the sole undead possessing free will, he defended his retreat against all outsiders until discovered by the Forsaken. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Gunther was a promising apprentice among the Kirin Tor in Dalaran. Alongside close friends Bethor Iceshard and Thule Ravenclaw, he studied the arcane arts, secretly delving into necromancy despite the Kirin Tor's strict prohibitions against dark magic. To commemorate their brotherhood, the trio once bound their apprentice wands together into a single heirloom.

Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde is a night elf residing in the coastal port of Auberdine. Stationed along the misty Darkshore coast, she watches the tides and directs travelers to investigate the strange remains washing ashore. Her concerns center on the mysterious sea creatures and massive turtles whose carcasses have begun littering the northern beaches. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde makes her home in Auberdine, the bustling seaside haven of Darkshore. While many in town concern themselves with the forest or shipping across the Veiled Sea, Gwennyth keeps her gaze firmly on the coastline. The tides have recently turned grim, depositing the remains of colossal marine life onto the surf. To understand what is happening in the waters offshore, she relies on willing adventurers to scour the sands, retrieve skeletal samples, and bring back answers.

Hamhock. Hamhock is a massive two-headed ogre confined within the depths of the Stormwind Stockade. Locked away beneath the capital alongside hardened Defias insurgents and cutthroats, he looms as a particularly brutal and unexpected inmate amidst the prison riot. The Stormwind Stockade was built to hold petty thieves, murderers, and political dissidents, making a towering two-headed ogre an imposing sight among the cells. When the prisoners rose up and took control of the facility, Hamhock remained entrenched in the chaos, crushing anyone foolish enough to intrude on his cellblock.

Herod. Herod is a renowned champion and berserker of the Scarlet Crusade, commanding the Armory within the Scarlet Monastery. Known for his ferocious martial prowess and unyielding zeal, he trains recruits in the brutal melee combat needed to wage holy war. His death is sought by both Alliance dissidents and the Horde's rulers in Undercity to weaken the Crusade's military core. Within the fortified halls of the Scarlet Monastery's Armory, Herod stands as the embodiment of the Crusade's martial aggression. Unlike the spellcasters and paladins who channel holy magic in the Cathedral, Herod relies on raw, bloodthirsty physical power. Clad in mail and wielding a massive two-handed axe, he personally trains cohorts of Scarlet Trainees, instilling a furious devotion to exterminating anyone not allied with their fanatical cause.

High Executor Darthalia. High Executor Darthalia is a high-ranking Forsaken military commander stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Acting under the direct authority of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and Varimathras, she directs Forsaken operations against the human stronghold of Southshore and local Syndicate brigands. Her leadership is central to securing the Horde's southern flank in Lordaeron. Operating out of Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia serves as the operational commander for Forsaken forces throughout the Hillsbrad Foothills. Her primary strategic concern is halting the expansion of human resistance, keeping the Alliance forces in Southshore contained, and hunting down the lawless Syndicate rogues infesting the surrounding countryside. Every offensive push into southern Hillsbrad flows directly through her command.

High Executor Hadrec. High Executor Hadrec is the military commander of the Forsaken garrison stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. From this central crypt, he oversees defense against regional threats including the gnolls of the Rot Hide clan and investigates the disappearance of scouts across the zone. He serves as the primary officer directing Horde operations throughout Silverpine. Stationed within the gloom of the Sepulcher, High Executor Hadrec directs Forsaken military operations across Silverpine Forest. While Tirisfal Glades is firmly secured by the Dark Lady's forces, Silverpine remains fraught with peril, bordered by hostile Dalaran mages, feral worgen, and encroaching gnolls. Hadrec bears the grim responsibility of consolidating Forsaken territory and stamping out anything that challenges Undercity authority south of the capital.

High Inquisitor Fairbanks. High Inquisitor Fairbanks was once a revered priest of the Knights of the Silver Hand and the most trusted advisor to Highlord Alexandros Mograine. Betrayed, executed, and hidden away behind a secret door in the Scarlet Monastery Cathedral, his rotting, undead form stands as a grim monument to the Scarlet Crusade's dark descent. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Fairbanks was a respected holy man among the Knights of the Silver Hand. When Highlord Alexandros Mograine convened a fateful gathering at the Southshore inn, Fairbanks stood beside him, helping channel holy power into the enigmatic crystal that would eventually become the heart of the legendary Ashbringer. When Prince Arthas dissolved the paladin order, Fairbanks accompanied Mograine to Ironforge, standing witness as King Magni Bronzebeard forged the great blade to combat the Scourge.

High Priestess Laurena. High Priestess Laurena is a respected human priest trainer stationed behind the grand altar within Stormwind City's Cathedral of Light. Having escaped the destruction of Lordaeron as a refugee during the Third War, she now instructs budding Alliance priests in spiritual devotion and arcane wards. Before taking her post within the towering halls of the Cathedral of Light, Laurena dwelt in the northern kingdom of Lordaeron. When the Scourge swept across the land during the Third War, she and her entire family were fortunate enough to survive and flee southward, arriving in Stormwind City as displaced refugees. Despite the immense grief and chaos that shattered her homeland, Laurena remained steadfast in her devotion, eventually rising to become a High Priestess in service to the Church of the Holy Light.

Houndmaster Loksey. Houndmaster Loksey is the officer charged with breeding and training the fearsome war dogs of the Scarlet Crusade. Stationed in the kennels within the Scarlet Monastery's Armory, he directs packs of hounds to hunt down undead, intruders, and perceived heretics. His merciless discipline has made the Monastery's beasts infamous throughout Tirisfal Glades. Within the heavily fortified walls of the Scarlet Monastery, Houndmaster Loksey commands the training of vicious tracking and attack dogs. The Scarlet Crusade relies on these trained hounds to sniff out plague-tainted corpses, uncover hidden infiltrators, and run down any survivors fleeing the zealots' wrath. Loksey holds absolute authority over the Armory's kennel wing, ensuring his charges are primed to tear intruders apart limb by limb.

Illiyana. Illiyana is an ancient dryad stationed in southwestern Ashenvale, dedicated to protecting the woodland from ancient corruption. Wandering near the Shrine of Aessina, she rallies champions of the Alliance to push back against the vicious satyrs that plague the ancient groves. Her vigilance represents the enduring bond between the daughters of Cenarius and the night elven wilderness. Like all dryads, Illiyana is one of the daughters of the demigod Cenarius. Peaceful yet fiercely protective of wild lands, she patrols the woods of southwestern Ashenvale. As dark forces stir and the woodlands suffer under creeping corruption, Illiyana keeps watch over sacred relics and groves, acting as a steward for nature's primal sanctity.

Interrogator Vishas. Interrogator James Vishas is the Scarlet Crusade's master of torment, stationed deep within the Scarlet Monastery's Graveyard wing. Infamous for his shrill voice and sheer cruelty, he takes twisted pleasure in breaking captives and testing the limits of mortal flesh. Few who enter his torture chambers ever leave with their minds or bodies intact. Within the dark crypts and burial grounds of the Scarlet Monastery, Interrogator Vishas tends to the Crusade's captive enemies. While the zealots outside march in gleaming armor under banners of purity, Vishas represents the grim reality behind their crusade: unbridled sadism cloaked in religious righteous fury.
