He approaches interrogation not merely as an intelligence duty, but as a prized craft, reveling in the agony of Forsaken captives, captured Scourge, and any living travelers unlucky enough to be branded heretics.

Islen Waterseer. Islen Waterseer is a respected tauren shaman who dwells beside a quiet fishing hut on the Tidus Stair, overlooking the eastern sea of the Barrens. Possessing an intimate communion with the spirits of water, she guides initiates on the trials necessary to attune with the element. Novice shamans across the Horde seek her wisdom to earn their Water Totem. Far from the bustling crossroads and encampments of the Barrens, Islen Waterseer lives along the craggy coastline known as the Tidus Stair. Here, where the arid plains break against the Great Sea, the presence of the water spirits is raw and pervasive. Rather than dwelling in thunderous halls or busy cities, Islen prefers this quiet outpost, dedicating her days to listening to the tides and assisting shamans who seek communion with the fluid element.

Iverron. Iverron is a young night elf found in Shadowglen, the sheltered starting bough of Teldrassil. Stricken by the venom of the woodland's increasingly agitated arachnids, his plight serves as an early warning of the growing corruption within the World Tree. While wandering through the quiet canopies of Shadowglen, Iverron ran afoul of the webwood spiders nesting in the vale. Succumbing quickly to their toxic bite, the young elf was left incapacitated, unable to return to safety on his own. His helpless condition highlights the sudden aggression sweeping through creatures that once shared the glade in peace.

Jaina Proudmoore. Lady Jaina Proudmoore is the ruler of Theramore Isle and the most powerful human sorceress alive. Formerly a star pupil of Dalaran's Kirin Tor, she led the survivors of Lordaeron across the Great Sea and now strives to maintain a fragile peace between the Alliance and the New Horde. The daughter of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras, Jaina showed remarkable aptitude for the arcane at an early age and studied under Archmage Antonidas in Dalaran. During the Third War, she investigated the mysterious Plague of Undeath alongside Prince Arthas Menethil, witnessing firsthand the tragic downfall of Lordaeron. Guided by the warnings of the Prophet Medivh, she rallied an expedition of human survivors and set sail westward to the forgotten continent of Kalimdor. There, her forces forged an unprecedented alliance with Thrall's Horde and the night elves, standing together atop Mount Hyjal to defeat Archimonde and shatter the Burning Legion's invasion.

Je'neu Sancrea. Je'neu Sancrea is a Darkspear troll and a member of the Earthen Ring stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the Ashenvale coast. Sensing dark disturbances deep beneath the shoreline, he directs Horde adventurers to investigate the corruption infesting the ancient submerged temple of Blackfathom Deeps. While most of the Earthen Ring focuses on elemental harmony across Kalimdor, Je'neu Sancrea keeps watch over the secluded and dangerous Zoram Strand. Perched at Zoram'gar Outpost, he observes the dark tremors and unnatural tides stirring near the ruined temple of Blackfathom Deeps. Though bound by the shamanic duties of his circle, his strong loyalties to the Darkspear tribe and Thrall's Horde keep him working exclusively alongside Horde champions.

Jergosh the Invoker. Jergosh the Invoker is a treacherous orc warlock hiding deep within Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. As a high-ranking leader among the Searing Blade cultists, he practices demonic arts directly under the Warchief's nose and plots against the Horde. While Thrall works tirelessly to lead the orcs along a path of honor and shamanism, Jergosh rejected these ideals in favor of raw demonic power. Concealing himself within the subterranean labyrinth of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, he gathered followers into the Searing Blade, an insidious sect aligned with the remnants of the Shadow Council. Operating in the shadows directly below the Horde capital, Jergosh works to undo everything the new Horde stands for.

Jern Hornhelm. Jern Hornhelm is a dwarven miner affiliated with the Explorers' League, stationed in the town of Thelsamar. He coordinates vital logistics and communication between the settlement, Ironforge, and the archaeological dig site deeper in Loch Modan. Adventurers frequently assist him with shuttling mining supplies and progress reports across the region. Stationed within the rustic town of Thelsamar, Jern Hornhelm plays a key logistical role for dwarven operations throughout Loch Modan. While dwarven scholars and field teams venture out into the wilderness to unearth their ancestral past, maintaining consistent supply chains remains essential. Jern ensures that vital resources, tools, and communications reach the active dig sites safely.

Jitters. Jitters is a terrified, half-starved human hiding among the ruins of Raven Hill in Duskwood. He clings to scraps of food and struggles to speak about the horrors he has witnessed. Found shivering amid the dilapidated houses of Raven Hill, Jitters lives in constant terror of the predators stalking Duskwood's western trails. He relies on passing adventurers for simple sustenance, desperate for food while keeping a frantic eye on the encroaching shadows. His skittish mannerisms and uncanny reflex for leaping clear of sudden danger earned him his moniker long ago, but his frantic paranoia is born from firsthand encounters with horrific horrors.

Jonathan Carevin. Jonathan Carevin is a resolute human hunter residing in Darkshire, dedicated to eradicating the darkness plaguing Duskwood. Unlike the defensive Night Watch, he and his family actively hunt down the undead, worgen, and any heretical threats lurking under the darkened canopies. While Darkshire depends upon the Night Watch to patrol the roads and safeguard the township, Jonathan Carevin believes a mere defensive perimeter is insufficient. Alongside his family and allies like Calor, Jonathan takes the offensive. He actively targets the unholy fiends wandering Duskwood, pursuing a personal crusade to purge all demons, undead, and heretics from the region under the grace of the Light.

Jordan Stilwell. Jordan Stilwell is a skilled human weaponsmith stationed outside the snowy Gates of Ironforge in Dun Morogh. Though originally meant to become a paladin of the Holy Light, he followed his father's craft to become an artisan whose work serves paladins across the Alliance. He is best known for forging Verigan's Fist in honor of his old friend, Bosch Verigan. Though Jordan Stilwell was expected to take holy vows and become a paladin within the Church of the Holy Light, he ultimately chose the way of the forge. He followed in his father's footsteps, taking up his father's enchanted smithing hammer. Jordan refined his craft under the tutelage of the dwarven blacksmith Bailor Stonehand. Despite setting aside the mantle of an anointed holy warrior, Jordan remains deeply faithful to the Light, dedicating his extraordinary craftsmanship to outfitting champions who fight in its name.

Kadrak. Kadrak is a seasoned orc commander stationed at the Mor'shan Rampart on the border between the Barrens and Ashenvale. Tasked with safeguarding the northern frontier, he coordinates the flow of dispatches and reinforcements into the contested forest. For Horde adventurers pushing past the arid plains, Kadrak serves as the gateway to the ongoing struggle against the night elves. Standing atop the fortified timber barricades of the Mor'shan Rampart, Kadrak watches over the primary route connecting the Barrens to Ashenvale. The border is a precarious frontier: to the south lie the sun-scorched plainsclaimed by the Horde, while to the north loom the ancient woods guarded fiercely by the night elves. Kadrak ensures that the defensive perimeter remains unbroken against encroaching Sentinels and hostile woodland creatures.

Kaela Shadowspear. Kaela Shadowspear is a night elf sentinel stationed southwest of Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. From her small outpost, she coordinates with fellow sentinels to monitor escalating tensions and regional disruptions in the wilderness. She relies on brave travelers to scout dangerous territory and bring aid to the land's wounded defenders. Positioned just southwest of the industrial devastation of Windshear Crag, Kaela Shadowspear keeps a watchful vigil over the surrounding passes. The Stonetalon Mountains are fraught with danger as the Horde encroaches and goblin operations exploit the land's natural bounty. Operating alongside the gnome Gaxim Rustfizzle, Kaela acts as an essential forward liaison for the night elves, tracking threats that push deeper into ancestral territory.

Kam Deepfury. Kam Deepfury is a notorious Dark Iron saboteur incarcerated within the depths of the Stormwind Stockade. Unlike the majority of the prison's inmates, he has no allegiance to the Defias Brotherhood, having been captured for orchestrating a devastating explosion along the Thandol Span far to the north. While the Stockade is overwhelmingly filled with disgruntled Stonemasons and Defias rebels, Kam Deepfury stands apart. A Dark Iron dwarf of cunning and violence, Deepfury was captured and brought to Stormwind after masterminding an operation that crippled vital northern infrastructure. He is locked deep within the prison's cells, isolated from his kin beneath Blackrock Mountain but just as hostile to the Alliance as any rebel rioter sharing the corridors.

Lady Anacondra. Lady Anacondra is one of the Fanglords leading the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once a night elf acolyte named Scarletleaf, she was the first to volunteer for Naralex's ambitious effort to heal the Barrens. When her master's Emerald Dream communion turned into a nightmare, her mind broke, twisting her devotion into a venomous drive to see Kalimdor overrun by serpents. Before adopting her serpentine title, Lady Anacondra was known as Scarletleaf. When the elder druid Naralex conceived of tapping into the subterranean springs of the Barrens through the Emerald Dream, she stepped forward as his very first volunteer. Her eager loyalty, however, proved her undoing. As Naralex's mind was seized by dark visions, the nightmare seeped out from the dreaming realm and contaminated his disciples, shattering Scarletleaf's sanity and reshaping her reverie into a cold, reptilian obsession.

Lady Sarevess. Lady Sarevess is a twisted naga sorceress dwelling within the flooded ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, where she dabbles in dark sorceries. Within the Pool of Ask'ar, Lady Sarevess conducts her rituals in a flooded grotto of the ruined temple. A very twisted spellcaster, she dabbles in dark magic while the Twilight's Hammer cultists who also haunt the sunken temple pursue their own worship deeper in the cavern.

Laurna Morninglight. Laurna Morninglight is a night elf priest trainer residing in the tranquil settlement of Dolanaar within Teldrassil. Devoted to the Sisterhood of Elune, she guides budding acolytes emerging from Shadowglen in the spiritual rites and healing graces of the Moon Goddess. Her teachings prepare young night elf priests for the growing threats encroaching on the boughs of the World Tree. Situated amidst the boughs of Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight serves as one of the primary mentors for young priests who have completed their initial rites in Shadowglen. As new initiates step out into the broader reaches of Teldrassil, she instructs them on expanding their communion with Elune, balancing the light of healing with defensive rites necessary to survive an increasingly hostile wild.

Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle is an officer of the Stormwind army currently stationed at the Southshore inn in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Deeply unhappy with his frontier posting, he spends most of his time drinking while outsourcing his duties to passing travelers. His primary military assignment is dealing with the encroaching murlocs along the coast, a chore he eagerly delegates in hopes of securing a transfer back south. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle did not choose Southshore. Dispatched far from Stormwind City, the lieutenant finds the damp, contested shores of Hillsbrad a miserable step down from the civilized comforts of the capital. Instead of patrolling the fields or coordinating defenses with his commanding officer, Marshal Redpath, Orinelle has practically taken up permanent residence inside Southshore's inn. His days are spent sulking, drinking, and dreaming of an official transfer order that will return him to the south.

Lord Cobrahn. Lord Cobrahn, formerly the night elf druid Jarlaxla, is one of the corrupted Druids of the Fang lurking deep within the Wailing Caverns. Once renowned within the Cenarion Circle for his mastery of shapeshifting, he succumbed to the nightmare infecting the cavern springs. Renaming himself after his new lethal guise, Cobrahn now commands broods of deviate serpents and defends the twisted labyrinth. Before adopting the moniker Lord Cobrahn, Jarlaxla was a respected member of the Cenarion Circle, celebrated among his fellow druids for his extraordinary skill in channeling animal forms. When Naralex ventured into the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens hoping to tap their underground springs and restore lush life to the arid wastes, Jarlaxla accompanied him. However, when Naralex's Emerald Dream communion decayed into a twisting nightmare, Jarlaxla's mind shattered alongside his brothers.

Lord Ello Ebonlocke. Lord Ello Ebonlocke is the mayor of Darkshire and the leader of its governing council, stationed inside the Darkshire Town Hall. Surrounded by darkness and creeping horrors, he struggles daily to maintain order and protect his besieged citizens despite receiving little aid from Stormwind. Seated in the gloom of the Darkshire Town Hall, Lord Ello Ebonlocke bears the heavy burden of governing a settlement on the brink of ruin. Once part of the prosperous rural haven known as Grand Hamlet, Darkshire is now smothered by perpetual shadow and besieged by ravenous ghouls, skeletal abominations, and feral beasts. Ello presides over the Council of Darkshire, striving against impossible odds to keep the remnants of civilization functioning while Stormwind turns a blind eye to their plight.

Lord Pythas. Lord Pythas, once a night elf warrior named Aryn, is one of the four corrupted leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. Originally a childhood friend and sworn protector of the archdruid Naralex, he fell victim to the nightmare tainting the oasis underground. Now he wields both martial might and twisted serpent magic against any who try to reach his slumbering master. Before adopting the moniker Pythas, this night elf was known as Aryn. A seasoned warrior and trusted childhood companion to Naralex, he served as the archdruid's personal guard when the expedition ventured into the dry wastes of the Barrens. Eager to better serve Naralex's ambitious dream of restoring lush life to the arid realm, Aryn took up the study of druidism, proving to be an exceptionally fast learner. However, physical discipline and martial valor offered no shelter against the insidious corruption waiting deep within the subterranean fissures.

Lord Serpentis. Lord Serpentis is a corrupted night elf druid who stands as one of the four leaders of the rogue Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once a druid of great power and prestige in the order of Naralex, he was twisted into madness when Naralex's dream became a nightmare within the subterranean springs. Now, he helps command the serpent-worshipping sect deep in the caverns where the corrupted Naralex lies slumbering. Before darkness overtook the cavern springs, Serpentis was a druid of great power and prestige, one of the noble order led by Naralex that hoped to use the caverns' springs and the Emerald Dream to heal the Barrens. However, when Naralex's vision became a corrupting nightmare, Serpentis was among the druids whose minds fell to the emerging madness.

Lorgus Jett. Lorgus Jett is a human member of the Twilight's Hammer cult operating within the flooded corridors of Blackfathom Deeps. Wandering the Moonshrine Ruins, he serves as a ruthless commander in the cult's service to the Old Gods. Horde leaders have singled him out as a primary target to disrupt the cult's encroaching presence along the Ashenvale coast. While many members of the Twilight's Hammer working under Blackfathom Deeps hail from orcish or tauren lineages, Lorgus Jett stands out as a human in the deep recesses of ancient night elf ruins. Roaming anywhere between the upper Moonshrine Ruins and the cavernous tunnels beyond the murloc defiler Gelihast, Jett coordinates the cult's dark rituals and violent ambitions.

Madame Eva. Madame Eva is a revered fortune-teller and matriarch living in Darkshire in the shadowed forest of Duskwood. Practicing older, mystic arts of divination and cartomancy, she often serves as the first townsperson to sense unnatural disturbances across the woods. Travelers frequently seek her out to unravel grim mysteries or procure occult charms against the creeping dark. Dwelling quietly amidst the gloom of Darkshire, Madame Eva practices cartomancy and ancient folk rituals that many in Stormwind's cathedral would view with suspicion. In a forsaken region plagued by feral beasts, the undead, and darker horrors, her eerie insights are tolerated and sought after by desperate townspeople and visiting adventurers alike.

Magatha Grimtotem. Magatha Grimtotem is the matriarch of the Grimtotem tribe and the Elder Crone of Thunder Bluff. A formidable shaman and political schemer, she resides on Elder Rise while continually challenging Cairne Bloodhoof's vision for the tauren nation. Magatha rose to absolute authority over the Grimtotem through an arranged union followed by the sudden, fatal climbing accident of her mate. Operating from Elder Rise with her personal retinue and bodyguards, she stands as the undisputed political and spiritual leader of her reclusive tribe. Unlike Cairne Bloodhoof, Magatha preaches tauren dominance, viewing other mortal races as intruders upon Kalimdor who ought to be eradicated or swept aside.

Maggran Earthbinder. Maggran Earthbinder is a grizzled tauren veteran appointed by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof to lead the Horde encampment at Sun Rock Retreat. Hardened by a lifetime of brutal conflict, he oversees the defense of the craggy valleys of Stonetalon against ravenous beasts and aggressive harpy covens. Though wearied by countless battles, he remains a steadfast guardian of the settlement. Maggran Earthbinder was sent into the Stonetalon Mountains by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof himself. A veteran of countless skirmishes and bloody campaigns, Maggran admits that age and violence have hardened his heart, stripping away the natural gentleness typical of his people. Sun Rock Retreat was meant to be both an outpost under his steady command and a place of respite, where warm winds and mountain sunshine might soothe his battle-worn spirit.

Magistrate Sevren. Magistrate Sevren is the chief administrative official presiding over the settlement of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Standing inside the town hall, he organizes early Forsaken defense and directs arriving champions to stabilize the territory around the Undercity. Operating from the town hall in Brill, Magistrate Sevren coordinates civil authority and strategic efforts in the lands just north of the Undercity. As new Forsaken step forth into Tirisfal Glades, Sevren assesses local crises and dispatches adventurers to restore order, secure ruined infrastructure, and suppress persistent threats lingering in the surrounding hills.

Magistrate Solomon. Magistrate Solomon is the elected ruler and chief magistrate of Lakeshire, presiding over local affairs from the town hall. Besieged by Blackrock orcs and relentless gnoll clans, he spends his days frantically pleading for military aid from an indifferent and distracted Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon governs Lakeshire during the darkest hour in its recent history. The tranquil lakeside settlement is surrounded by hostility: Redridge and Shadowhide gnolls prowl the surrounding hills, while Blackrock orcs descend from the north in organized warbands. Solomon works alongside Marshal Marris to maintain civil order and muster a defense, but Lakeshire's local guards and militia are stretched to their absolute breaking point.

Magni Bronzebeard. Magni Bronzebeard is the Lord of Ironforge, Thane of the Bronzebeard clan, and ruler of Khaz Modan. A peerless smith and veteran commander of the Second War, he leads his mountainous kingdom through grief and political tension while championing dwarven archaeology across Azeroth. The eldest of three brothers, Magni grew up keenly aware of the weight awaiting him under the mountain. When the Horde invaded during the Second War, he held Ironforge behind its impenetrable gates, emerging to pledge Khaz Modan to the Alliance of Lordaeron once the siege was broken. In the years of peace that followed, Magni welcomed his gnomish allies into the city after the fall of Gnomeregan, granting High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his refugees sanctuary within the mountain. To unite the fractured southern and northern kingdoms, Magni petitioned Mekkatorque to engineer an unprecedented subterranean marvel: the Deeprun Tram, connecting Ironforge directly to Stormwind.

Makaba Flathoof. Makaba Flathoof is a tauren survivor hailing from Camp Aparaje in the Stonetalon Mountains. Having witnessed the devastation of his home and people at the hands of the Grimtotem clan, he seeks brave champions of the Horde to bring vengeance upon the attackers and ensure his family's safety. Makaba Flathoof represents the tragic toll of internal strife among the tauren. His home, Camp Aparaje in the Stonetalon Mountains, fell victim to a ruthless surprise attack by the Grimtotem clan. While many tauren strive for peace and unity under the leadership of Cairne Bloodhoof, the treacherous Grimtotem continually sow discord and violence, leaving survivors like Makaba displaced and grieving.

Malfurion Stormrage. Malfurion Stormrage is the first mortal druid and the revered leader of the night elves alongside High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Renowned for defeating the Burning Legion in both the War of the Ancients and the Third War, he is venerated as the Shan'do, or honored teacher. Currently, he lies trapped in a comatose slumber within the Emerald Dream, leaving the kaldorei without his waking guidance. Ten thousand years ago, before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, Malfurion studied under the demigod Cenarius. While Queen Azshara and her Highborne caste delved dangerously into the arcane energies of the Well of Eternity, Malfurion turned toward the primal forces of nature, becoming Azeroth's first mortal druid. His suspicions regarding the Highborne proved tragically correct when Azshara's reckless sorcery pierced the veil and summoned Sargeras and the Burning Legion into Azeroth, igniting the catastrophic War of the Ancients.

Mangletooth. Mangletooth is an imprisoned Razormane quilboar held captive by the Horde inside Camp Taurajo. Facing execution, he trades strategic information about his rivals and the ancient lore of Agamaggan to adventurers willing to do his bidding. Held in a cage at Camp Taurajo by tauren hunters and orc sentries, Mangletooth is a captured Razormane quilboar awaiting execution. Rather than resigning to death, he attempts to manipulate his captors and visiting Horde adventurers into striking down the enemies of his tribe, hoping his cunning will prove his worth or secure his rescue.

Marshal Dughan. Marshal Dughan is the commanding officer of the Stormwind Army detachment stationed in Goldshire. Tasked with protecting the heart of Elwynn Forest, he finds his local garrison stretched thin against growing incursions of kobolds, gnolls, and bandits. To keep the crossroads town and surrounding farmsteads safe, he relies heavily on independent adventurers. Stationed prominently in Goldshire outside the Lion's Pride Inn, Marshal Dughan bears the heavy burden of keeping Elwynn Forest secure while Stormwind's military resources are tied up elsewhere. The surrounding woods are steadily deteriorating: vermin choke the mines, gnolls mass along the riverbanks, and highwaymen harass travelers along the King's Road. With too few footmen under his direct command, Dughan orchestrates local defense by directing fresh recruits to reinforce outposts and scout contested ground.

Marshal Marris. Marshal Marris is the beleaguered military officer commanding the town watch at Lakeshire. Stationed near the town's bridge, he coordinates defense operations against the massive Blackrock orc invasion pressing down from the heights of the Redridge Mountains. With Stormwind's army absent, he relies on visiting adventurers to blunt the horde's advances. Lakeshire stands on the brink of collapse, caught between the gnolls to the west and the terrifying military might of the Blackrock clan to the east. Marshal Marris oversees the guard line at the town's primary bridge, but his resources are depleted and his soldiers are spread impossibly thin. With the kingdom of Stormwind withholding royal reinforcements, Marris carries the heavy burden of keeping the township from being overwhelmed by brute force.

Marshal McBride. Marshal Douglas McBride is the commander of the Stormwind garrison stationed at Northshire Abbey. Tasked with the defense of Northshire Valley, he directs freshly arrived recruits against the rising kobold infestation threatening local farms and mines. He serves as the primary military authority for newcomers beginning their service to the kingdom of Stormwind. Stationed right outside Northshire Abbey, Marshal Douglas McBride represents the direct authority of the Stormwind Army in this quiet valley. While the abbey itself is an enclave of faith and learning, rising turmoil across the kingdom has stretched military garrisons thin. McBride must maintain peace and secure the valley's food and resource supplies with only a handful of sworn guards and an influx of green recruits seeking training under the abbey's masters.

Master Apothecary Faranell. Master Apothecary Faranell is the head of the Royal Apothecary Society, stationed within the depths of the Apothecarium in the Undercity. In life a respected Dalaran scholar, in undeath he directs the Forsaken's search for a devastating New Plague to eradicate both the Scourge and the living. Before the Third War, Faranell was an esteemed alchemist who spent decades studying alongside the learned mages of Dalaran. He spent his mortal days seeking cures, remedies, and potions to improve mortal health. When the Scourge plague claimed his life and he arose as a free-willed Forsaken, his former scientific curiosity curdled into cruelty. Retaining his encyclopedic intellect, he traded healing salves for catastrophic reagents, quickly becoming one of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner's most valued researchers in the bowels of Lordaeron's fallen capital.

Master Gadrin. Master Gadrin is an elderly jungle troll and a venerable witch doctor of the Darkspear tribe, currently residing in Sen'jin Village. Having once trained the tribe's priests and mages alongside the renegade witch doctor Zalazane, he now coordinates efforts to aid his displaced people and break the dark curse gripping their stolen home on the Echo Isles. Long before the Darkspear arrived on Kalimdor, Master Gadrin served as a witch doctor of his tribe in their ancestral South Seas islands, where he guided the mystical training of generations of Darkspear trolls.

Mathias Shaw. Master Mathias Shaw is the leader of SI:7, the covert intelligence agency of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Operating from the shadows of Old Town, he directs spies and scouts to protect the realm from internal conspiracies and external horrors alike. Mathias Shaw stands as Stormwind's foremost spymaster and assassin. From SI:7's discreet headquarters tucked behind the barracks in Old Town, Shaw coordinates a covert network that spans the Eastern Kingdoms and beyond. Pragmatic, calculating, and fiercely loyal to the House of Wrynn, he operates on the philosophy that Stormwind's safety depends just as much on unseen daggers and stolen missives as it does on gleaming armor and palace garrisons.

Mathrengyl Bearwalker. Mathrengyl Bearwalker is a master druid trainer and respected elder of the Cenarion Circle residing in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. Having once served as Archdruid Fandral Staghelm's direct assistant, he guides young Alliance druids through their spiritual trials, shapeshifting rites, and duties across Kalimdor. Perched within the verdant reaches of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker stands as one of the most venerable and balanced druids on Teldrassil. He serves as a primary guide for fledgling Alliance druids, overseeing their communion with Moonglade and testing their readiness to master primal animal forms. Having undergone the intense, bewildering communion with the Great Bear Spirit in his own youth, Mathrengyl understands the weight of these rites, personally charging initiates to prove their spirit against the sacred moonkin Lunaclaw before inducting them into the path of the Druid of the Claw.

Mebok Mizzyrix. Mebok Mizzyrix is an enterprising goblin entrepreneur residing in the port town of Ratchet. Ever eager to turn bizarre wilderness reagents into profit, he hires passing adventurers to gather unusual flora and fauna from across the Barrens and beyond. His most notorious project involves concocting a commercial intellect-enhancing beverage out of raptor horns. Operating out of the bustling, neutral port of Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix embodies the classic Steamwheedle spirit of relentless opportunism. While Ratchet caters to sailors, pirates, and merchants of all stripes, Mebok focuses his keen eye on Kalimdor's wilderness. Rather than mining standard ore or trading mundane cloth, he seeks out rare biological curiosities that he believes can be refined into highly lucrative concoctions and commodities.

Melor Stonehoof. Melor Stonehoof is a veteran tauren huntsman stationed atop Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. As a mentor in the ways of the hunt, he tests the tracking prowess and mettle of Horde hunters by sending them after the most dangerous predatory beasts across the Barrens and Thousand Needles. Perched upon the breezy expanse of Hunter Rise, Melor Stonehoof observes the plains below with a practiced eye. The art of the hunt is sacred to the tauren, entwined with survival, spiritual balance, and respect for nature's greatest predators. Melor ensures that those who carry bow and blade in the name of the Horde understand this balance, directing promising stalkers to master their craft through trials against legendary beasts.

Menara Voidrender. Menara Voidrender is a human warlock residing in the goblin port of Ratchet. She acts as a mentor to ambitious practitioners of the dark arts from both the Alliance and the Horde, sharing her deep knowledge of demon-binding artifacts and arcane craft. Her secluded position in Kalimdor keeps her far from the watchful eyes of orthodox authorities. While most warlocks in the Eastern Kingdoms practice in damp cellars or secluded slaughterhouses beneath their home cities, Menara Voidrender chose the neutral goblin port of Ratchet in the Barrens. Operating far from the scrutiny of the Kirin Tor, Stormwind's guards, or Orgrimmar's overseers, she is free to pursue her occult studies in plain sight. Her willingness to deal with any capable apprentice, regardless of faction, makes her a rare point of commonality among practitioners of the dark arts.

Miner Johnson. Miner Johnson is an elusive, seasoned miner affiliated with the Defias Brotherhood deep inside the Deadmines. Tucked away in a side alcove alongside ordinary laborers, this dangerous prospector oversees excavation efforts ahead of the heavy machinery found deeper underground. Because he wanders the subterranean tunnels erratically, adventurers only occasionally cross his path. While hundreds of laborers pick at the subterranean veins of the Deadmines to supply Edwin VanCleef's hidden fortress, Miner Johnson stands out as an unusually formidable figure among them. Lurking in a shadowed alcove to the left before the lumbering shredders of the Mast Room, he is far tougher and more aggressive than the regular workforce. His unpredictable presence makes him a legendary target for explorers traversing the Defias tunnels.

Morin Cloudstalker. Morin Cloudstalker is a tauren scout keeping watch along the road leading east from Bloodhoof Village toward the Barrens in Mulgore. Standing vigil over the plains, he monitors local trade routes and investigates the encroaching threats endangering tauren travelers. Positioned beside the dirt path winding east toward the Barrens, Morin Cloudstalker acts as both a scout and a guardian for travelers through Mulgore. The grassy plains here are usually peaceful, but the opening of trade routes and shifting territories have drawn opportunists and bandits dangerously close to the heart of the tauren homeland.

Motega Firemane. Motega Firemane is a tauren scholar stationed at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to cataloging the dangerous wildlife of the canyon, he finds his studies disrupted by a vengeful wind serpent spirit and the reckless misadventures of his young assistant. Four years following the Third War, Motega Firemane journeyed south into Thousand Needles to observe and record the distinct beasts surviving among the towering mesas. Accompanied by his youthful assistant, Pao'ka Swiftmountain—whose protective father was reluctant to let him leave Mulgore—Motega set up camp alongside Kanati Greycloud at Whitereach Post. While his original calling was quiet natural observation, the harsh perils of the canyon floor continually demand a more martial approach to survival.

Mr. Smite. Mr. Smite is the imposing tauren first mate serving aboard the Defias Brotherhood's flagship deep inside the Deadmines. An expert weaponmaster under Captain Greenskin, he commands the dockside approach to the hidden juggernaut with ruthless discipline. Intruders who face him must contend with his shifting arsenal and devastating physical strength. Guarding the docks of Ironclad Cove, Mr. Smite serves as first mate to the goblin Captain Greenskin. While the Defias Brotherhood is predominantly composed of disenfranchised humans and allied goblin tinkerers, Smite stands as a striking anomaly: a massive, battle-hardened tauren far from the plains of Kalimdor. Tasked with maintaining strict order among a rowdy pirate crew, he ensures that the labor fitting out Edwin VanCleef's secret dreadnaught proceeds without disruption.

Mull Thunderhorn. Mull Thunderhorn is a tauren elder residing in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Deeply devoted to the Earth Mother and the balance of the land, he watches over the sacred water wells scattered across the plains. As outside exploiters threaten the region's lifegiving waters, Mull guides young tauren through the rituals required to cleanse the ancestral springs. Standing watch in Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn carries the weight of Mulgore's spiritual well-being. The nomadic tribes have gathered under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof to establish a permanent home, yet their lands are already under siege by greed and reckless expansion. Mull serves as a spiritual anchor for the young braves stepping out of Camp Narache, calling upon them to safeguard the vital resources of their ancestors.

Mutanus the Devourer. Mutanus the Devourer is a monstrous, pale murloc manifested directly from the Emerald Nightmare. Lurking in the darkest recesses of the sleeping druid Naralex's mind, it emerges to devour anyone attempting to break the Nightmare's hold over the Wailing Caverns. Slaying this twisted aberration is the final step in freeing Naralex from his tormented slumber. When the night elf druid Naralex tapped into the underground springs beneath the Barrens, he aimed to restore life to the arid wastes by connecting them to the Emerald Dream. Instead, an ancient corruption known as the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts. Trapped in an agonizing vision, Naralex's subconscious fears took physical form. The corruption seized upon a bizarre, primal revulsion in the druid's psyche—his deep-seated terror of murlocs—and amplified it into an immense, albino predator.

Naralex. Naralex is a night elf druid who sought to restore the parched Barrens to a lush forest using the powers of the Emerald Dream. Instead, his slumber was overtaken by a dark nightmare, twisting the Wailing Caverns beneath the earth and turning his followers into venomous fiends. Long before the Great Sundering, the sun-scorched plains of the Barrens were once a vibrant forest. Viewing this loss as a tragedy, Naralex journeyed south from Darnassus with a cohort of devoted disciples to reverse the drought. Deep beneath the savannah, he discovered an intricate subterranean network of underground springs and rushing geysers, naming them the Wailing Caverns after the howling wind and steam that moaned through the rock. He believed that by entering a deep trance and channeling the pristine energies of the Emerald Dream into these subterranean waters, the life-giving flow would reach the surface and cause the entire wasteland to bloom.

Oggleflint. Oggleflint is the chieftain of the trogg tribe dwelling within the volcanic depths of Ragefire Chasm directly beneath Orgrimmar. Once master of the entire subterranean cavern, he and his kin have been pushed toward the upper tunnels by the arrival of the Searing Blade cultists. Now entrenched near the entrance, he commands his savage pack and poses an immediate threat to the Horde capital above. Before shadow cultists infiltrated the chasm beneath Orgrimmar, Oggleflint and his troggs ruled the fiery subterranean tunnels uncontested. Brutal and territorial, they carved out a primitive domain among the molten rock. Though troggs possess little in the way of advanced civilization, Oggleflint maintained absolute authority over the pack through sheer brute strength.

Old Serra'kis. Old Serra'kis is an ancient, massive threshadon dwelling in the submerged subterranean waters of Blackfathom Deeps. While the invading Twilight's Hammer culled much of the temple's aquatic life for provisions, this enormous beast proved entirely lethal to any who attempted to hunt it. When the Twilight's Hammer cultists descended upon the sunken Moonshrine Ruins, they slaughtered the native wildlife beneath the waters for sustenance. Yet beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum, one primeval creature refused to become prey. Old Serra'kis, the largest threshadon in the sunken temple, made short work of any cultist brazen enough to spear him. Eventually, the hunters abandoned their efforts, leaving the ancient carnivore undisturbed in his watery domain.

Onyxia. Onyxia is the broodmother of the black dragonflight and the devious daughter of Deathwing. From her lair in Dustwallow Marsh, she schemes to restore the black dragonflight's dominion over the mortal kingdoms.

Orgnil Soulscar. Orgnil Soulscar is an orc investigator stationed at Razor Hill in central Durotar. He serves as an informal officer of the peace, coordinating defense and intelligence against internal threats to the fledgling nation. His primary concern is the shadow cast by the Burning Blade cult within Durotar's canyons. Positioned at Razor Hill, Orgnil Soulscar takes on the grim responsibility of tracking subversion and insidious threats across Durotar. While grunt patrols look outward toward Alliance footholds and centaur raiding parties, Orgnil focuses on rot brewing from within. He collects reports from scouts across the region, piecing together evidence of ritual corruption and illicit gatherings.

Orgrim Doomhammer. Orgrim Doomhammer was the supreme Warchief of the Old Horde throughout the Second War, remembered as one of the greatest orc warriors in history. Though he died liberating the internment camps in the Arathi Highlands, his legacy endures in the capital of Orgrimmar and through Thrall, who inherited his mighty warhammer and black plate armor. Originally second-in-command to Blackhand of the Blackrock clan, Orgrim refused the demonic blood offered by Gul'dan, though he concealed his doubts beneath fierce loyalty. Near the close of the First War, disgusted by the Shadow Council's treachery and the murder of his childhood friend Durotan, Orgrim slew Blackhand in honorable combat. Assuming the mantle of Warchief, he ruthlessly purged Gul'dan's warlocks and led the Horde across the Eastern Kingdoms during the Second War. Though a devastating strategist who pushed human kingdoms to the brink of ruin, he was ultimately defeated and captured outside Blackrock Spire after the betrayal of Gul'dan split his forces.

Overlord Ramtusk. Overlord Ramtusk is the grizzled commander of the Death's Head tribe's military forces deep within Razorfen Kraul. A massive, aging quilboar warrior, his hide is heavily scarred from decades of brutal clashes across the Barrens. Striking him down shatters the martial backbone of the Kraul's defenders. Overlord Ramtusk has survived decades in one of Kalimdor's most violent frontiers. His thick, leathery hide is crisscrossed with deep scars earned in skirmishes against centaur raiding parties, feral harpies, encroaching orcs, and stalwart tauren braves. While advanced age slows many warriors, Ramtusk's seasoned instincts and physical resilience have only hardened, allowing him to rule Razorfen Kraul's standing garrison with unyielding authority.

Ozzie Togglevolt. Ozzie Togglevolt is a gnome engineer and survivor of Gnomeregan's fall, currently operating out of the snowy village of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Haunted by the tragedy that struck his people, he works alongside his partner Razzle Sprysprocket to research a remedy for the irradiated leper gnomes. Ozzie Togglevolt was inside the subterranean wonders of Gnomeregan when catastrophe struck. When the toxic fallout was vented throughout the corridors to stem the trogg invasion, Ozzie stood right beside his fellow gnome, Gnoarn. A sudden radioactive discharge struck Gnoarn directly, altering him forever before Ozzie's eyes. Though Ozzie made it to the surface alive and reached the haven of Dun Morogh, the horrifying memory of that disaster never left him.

Pelturas Whitemoon. Pelturas Whitemoon is a night elf father dwelling in Astranaar whose young daughter, Relara, has been struck by a terrible, corrupting illness. Desperate to save her, he works closely with local herbalist Orendil Broadleaf and traveling Alliance champions to gather sacred remedies from the surrounding wilds. His quest to heal Relara takes adventurers into some of Ashenvale's oldest sacred groves and ruins. Residing in the serene boughs of Astranaar, Pelturas Whitemoon lives the quiet life typical of forest-dwelling Kaldorei, often venturing out with his young daughter Relara to collect shimmering moonstones around Fallen Sky Lake. However, when Relara falls critically ill with a mysterious affliction, his quiet world collapses into frantic desperation. Astranaar is besieged on many fronts, but for Pelturas, nothing in the great forest matters more than saving his child.

Priestess Alathea. Priestess Alathea is a night elf priest trainer residing within the tranquil halls of the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Devoted to the Moon Goddess, she guides novitiates in the sacred arts and racial blessings bestowed by Elune. Her teachings help night elf practitioners attune their minds to defensive prayers and celestial magic. Standing within the soaring silver heights of Darnassus's grandest sanctuary, Priestess Alathea serves the Sisterhood of Elune as an instructor and spiritual guide. As night elf initiates progress beyond the quiet boughs of Shadowglen, they are directed to the Temple of the Moon to deepen their covenant with the Goddess. Alathea stands among the priestesses ready to impart sacred knowledge to those who dedicate their lives to healing, warding, and divine light.

Raene Wolfrunner. Raene Wolfrunner is an accomplished Sentinel officer and hunter stationed at the heart of Astranaar in Ashenvale. Accompanied by her loyal wolf and saber cat companions, she coordinates defense efforts across the forest against encroaching Horde forces and corrupted furbolg tribes. She serves as a vital anchor for Alliance champions striving to protect the sacred wilderness. Raene Wolfrunner stands watchful in Astranaar alongside her trusty saber cat Korra and wolf Dagri. As an officer among the Sentinels, she oversees patrols throughout Ashenvale and coordinates intelligence reaching beyond its borders, dispatching scouts like Kaela Shadowspear into neighboring regions such as the Stonetalon Mountains. Raene's devotion to the ancient woods is absolute; she has declared she would sooner face the Horde's lumbering forces alone than watch them hack and burn through the sacred timber unhindered.

Rejold Barleybrew. Rejold Barleybrew is a master dwarven brewer stationed in the lakeside settlement of Brewnall Village in western Dun Morogh. Devoted to perfecting hearty mountain spirits, he regularly enlists travelers to gather regional ingredients and test his potent recipes across the snowy valley. In Dun Morogh, brewing is treated not merely as trade, but as a defining art form. Rejold Barleybrew embodies this tradition from Brewnall Village, an outpost nestled near the frozen lake of the Iceflow River. Rather than settling for common tavern swill, Rejold continually refines his blends, seeking rare hops, mountain minerals, and pristine ice water to produce stouts capable of warming the stoutest dwarven warriors.

Rethiel the Greenwarden. Rethiel the Greenwarden is an ancient, sentient bog beast residing in the Green Belt within the Wetlands. Deeply attuned to the natural balance of the marsh, he watches over the land and enlists travelers to cull threats that disrupt its harmony. Standing amidst the damp thickets of the Green Belt, Rethiel is a towering creature of moss, peat, and primal plant life. While many bog beasts in the marshlands wander aimlessly as aggressive predators, Rethiel possesses a rare, conscious awareness and a sorrowful voice. He perceives the wetlands not merely as murky terrain, but as a living ecosystem that currently cries out under the weight of foreign predation and corruption.

Rhahk'Zor. Rhahk'Zor is a hulking ogre serving as the head foreman within the Deadmines. Overseeing Edwin VanCleef's subterranean construction efforts, he keeps the Defias laborers and miners in line through sheer brute force and heavy-handed discipline. Deep beneath the rolling hills of Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood has transformed the abandoned gold mines of Moonbrook into an underground fortress. Coordinating this sprawling construction requires harsh discipline, a role filled by the ogre Rhahk'Zor. Appointed as head foreman, he oversees the excavation crews and laborers, driving them forward to carve out tunnels and assemble VanCleef's secret projects.

Rorian the Dayseeker. Rorian the Dayseeker is an elder Skyborne figure situated in Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. He oversees the initiation of young fledglings as they discover their calling, step into maturity, and attune themselves to the natural elements of their homeland. Under his watchful guidance, newcomers learn the fundamentals of survival, tradition, and service to their community. Within the serene confines of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Rorian the Dayseeker stands as one of the primary mentors for the fledgling Skyborne. Revered for his experience and calm wisdom, Rorian directs youth during their crucial transition into adulthood. It is under his instruction that initiates undertake their traditional rite of passage, marking their readiness to defend and support their island home.

Scarlet Commander Mograine. Scarlet Commander Mograine serves as the military leader garrisoned inside the Cathedral of the Scarlet Monastery. A zealous paladin of the Scarlet Crusade, he defends the chapel alongside High Inquisitor Whitemane. Both the Horde and Alliance target him to disrupt the zealots threatening Tirisfal Glades and the surrounding lands. Stationed within the grand Crusader's Chapel at the heart of the Scarlet Monastery, Scarlet Commander Mograine commands the standing garrison of the Scarlet Crusade. He wields the holy power of a paladin with ferocious dedication, relying on retribution, divine shields, and stunning blows to shatter any whom the Crusade deems corrupted or unclean.

Senani Thunderheart. Senani Thunderheart is a tauren huntress stationed at Splintertree Post in Ashenvale, just north of the Barrens. Serving the Horde, she tests the mettle of passing travelers by challenging them to pursue the fierce wild predators that roam the ancient forest. Through her trials, hunters prove their skill while thinning the deadly beasts prowling near Horde territory. Found keeping camp at Splintertree Post, Senani Thunderheart represents the hunting traditions of the tauren amid the shadowed groves of Ashenvale. Far from the open plains of Mulgore, she directs Horde adventurers to test their tracking and combat prowess against the forest's apex beasts. She views the hunt as both an honorable challenge and a necessary ritual to survive in an untamed, contested land.

Senir Whitebeard. Senir Whitebeard is a dwarven dignitary and field agent stationed outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Serving as a special envoy from the Senate of Ironforge, he is tasked with monitoring the growing threats encircling Dun Morogh. His mission centers on evaluating the Frostmane troll offensive and reporting their movements directly back to the dwarven leadership. While most travelers visit Kharanos for its bustling inn and famous stout, Senir Whitebeard is here on official business. As a representative sent directly by the Senate of Ironforge, his presence highlights how seriously the high halls take the destabilization of Dun Morogh. He serves as an essential bridge between local scouts facing danger on the snowy frontier and the legislators arguing policy behind the city's stone gates.

Shadow Priest Allister. Shadow Priest Allister is a Forsaken priest stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Overseeing intelligence and tactical efforts in the region, he coordinates operations to monitor Dalaran's wizards and secure the borders of Lordaeron for the Dark Lady. Operating out of the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister directs Forsaken reconnaissance throughout Silverpine Forest. From this central crypt settlement, he tracks nearby threats ranging from renegade humans and beastly incursions to the arcane machinations unfolding near Dalaran's shimmering dome.

Shadow Priest Sarvis. Shadow Priest Sarvis stands inside the ruined chapel of Deathknell, serving as one of the primary guides for newly awakened Forsaken. He introduces fresh corpses to their grim reality, directing them to purge mindless undead and gather intelligence on local threats. Under Lady Sylvanas's banner, Sarvis works tirelessly to shape bewildered undead into disciplined servants of the Forsaken. Within the shadowy chapel of Deathknell, Shadow Priest Sarvis waits for those who have just clawed their way out of the grave. The awakening of a Forsaken soul is jarring and horrific, with many immediately losing their minds to mindless frenzy or despondency. Sarvis acts as an anchor, giving purpose to the newly risen. He assigns new recruits to put down the shambling, mindless corpses roaming the cemetery and directs them to secure Deathknell's borders against the encroaching Scourge.

Shael'dryn. Shael'dryn is an inquisitive dryad residing beside the Moonwell of Purity, east of Iris Lake in Ashenvale. Known for her lighthearted wit and fondness for wordplay, she serves as a vital contact for night elf scouts investigating forest corruption. She plays a pivotal role in aiding Astranaar's sentinels with cleansing relics to combat demonic and foul influences spreading across the wilderness. Daughter of Cenarius like all dryads, Shael'dryn approaches the perils of the wild with an unexpectedly playful spirit. Companions and travelers know her as a lover of puns and spoken jests, often using lighthearted humor to cut through the brooding tension of the tainted woodland. Yet behind her teasing demeanor lies deep devotion to the well-being of Ashenvale and its ancient spirits.

Shenthul. Shenthul is a jungle troll rogue trainer based in the shadowy subterranean reaches of the Cleft of Shadow in Orgrimmar. As an operative of the Shattered Hand, he orchestrates espionage operations across Kalimdor and initiates rising rogues into the guild's covert ranks. Tucked away inside the murky depths of the Cleft of Shadow, Shenthul serves as one of the Horde's foremost rogue mentors. While the warriors and shamans above march openly across the red dust of Durotar, Shenthul trains those who prefer stealth, ambush, and subterfuge. Under his tutelage, initiates master essential fieldcraft and lethal arts, learning to operate within the unforgiving politics and harsh wilderness of Kalimdor.

Sneed. Sneed is the Defias Brotherhood's goblin lumbermaster stationed deep within the Deadmines. Operating from the lumber chamber known as the Mast Room, he pilots a heavy shredder of his own design to process timber for Edwin VanCleef's secret juggernaut. While the Defias Brotherhood draws its core membership from disenfranchised human stonemasons and common laborers, building an ironclad warship requires specialist trades. Edwin VanCleef recruited Sneed specifically for his engineering know-how and ruthless goblin efficiency. Stationed in the Mast Room along the subterranean rail network, Sneed oversees the rapid felling, cutting, and shaping of timber needed to frame VanCleef's colossal dreadnaught.

Sneed's Shredder. Sneed's Shredder is an imposing mechanised lumber harvester stationed deep within the Deadmines. Piloted by the goblin taskmaster Sneed, this deadly machine acts as both heavy industrial machinery for Edwin VanCleef's shipwrights and a terrifying perimeter defender. Within the goblin-dominated foundry of the Deadmines, mechanical shredders serve a dual purpose: processing vast amounts of timber and lumber required for Edwin VanCleef's hidden juggernaut, and serving as armored shock engines against intruders. Sneed, the overseer of the lumber works, operates this modified mechanical beast directly, turning an oversized buzzsaw into an instrument of defense.

Sprite Jumpsprocket. Sprite Jumpsprocket is an apprentice gnome engineer currently residing in the busy Dwarven District of Stormwind City. Like many gnomes who sought refuge following the fall of Gnomeregan, she pursues technical craft and innovation alongside her fellow tinkers. Her presence highlights the thriving community of dwarven and gnomish artisans who keep the capital city supplied with gears, gadgets, and mechanical expertise. In the soot-covered streets and bustling workshops of the Dwarven District, gnomes and dwarves work shoulder-to-shoulder forging metal and designing intricate contraptions. Sprite Jumpsprocket serves as an apprentice engineer in this vibrant hub. Having integrated into the kingdom's capital, apprentice tinkers like Sprite hone their craft under experienced masters, contributing their inventive minds to the everyday mechanisms and technological marvels of the Alliance.

Sputtervalve. Sputtervalve is a stressed goblin engineer stationed in the port town of Ratchet. Serving the Tinkers' Union under Director Riddlevox, he oversees regional shredder research and development under crushing corporate deadlines. To keep his standing, he frequently hires adventurers to engage in industrial espionage against the rival Venture Company. Operating out of Ratchet, Sputtervalve answers to Director Riddlevox of the Tinkers' Union. Put in charge of shredder development, he quickly discovered that keeping pace with modern mechanization is brutal work. Facing fierce competition and an unforgiving deadline, Sputtervalve found himself with few working prototypes of his own. Rather than admit failure to the Union, he turned toward the classic goblin solution: stealing better designs from whoever built them first.

Sten Stoutarm. Sten Stoutarm is a practical dwarven outfitter and courier stationed outside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. Responsible for keeping new recruits equipped and managing local dispatches, he helps ensure that novice mountaineers stay warm, fed, and informed despite the harsh mountain conditions. Positioned near the heart of Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm is one of the first friendly faces new dwarven and gnomish recruits encounter outside Anvilmar's tavern. With the valley isolated by winter blizzards and encroaching dangers, Sten takes it upon himself to outfit green apprentices with sturdy gear before they freeze or wander unprepared into the drifts.

Strahad Farsan. Strahad Farsan is a master human warlock who dwells in a secluded stone tower overlooking Ratchet in the Barrens. Renowned across faction lines, he operates outside conventional Alliance and Horde politics, training aspiring summoners in the dangerous arts of binding higher demons. Practitioners of fel magic from Stormwind, Orgrimmar, and the Undercity alike seek his severe guidance. Perched on the bluffs above the goblin port of Ratchet, Strahad Farsan's tower stands apart from the bustling trade docks below. Ratchet's neutrality offers Strahad the freedom to conduct perilous demonic summonings away from the prying eyes of Alliance magistrates or Horde shamans. Surrounded by his acolytes, he studies the deeper mysteries of the Twisting Nether in relative seclusion, unbothered by petty territorial squabbles.

Sven Yorgen. Sven Yorgen is a grieving farmer camped along the Hushed Bank in northern Duskwood, accompanied by his companion Lars. Having survived the brutal slaughter of his family at the Yorgen Farmstead, Sven is consumed by a relentless drive to uncover who brought ruin upon his home and exact vengeance. Sven was born before the First War, old enough to recall the days before the region became shrouded in gloom following Medivh's fall. For years he worked the soil at the Yorgen Farmstead in southern Duskwood alongside his wife and children. That quiet existence ended in sudden violence when mysterious Dark Riders raided his homestead while he was away, butchering his family and turning the farm into a graveyard.

Sylvanas Windrunner. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner is the Banshee Queen and supreme ruler of the Forsaken, holding court in the Undercity beneath the ruins of Lordaeron. Once the brave Ranger-General of Silvermoon, she was slain and raised into undeath by Arthas Menethil before breaking free from the Lich King's grip. Now allied with Thrall's Horde out of mutual survival, she is fiercely dedicated to securing a future for her free-willed undead and exacting vengeance upon the Scourge. In life, Lady Sylvanas was the celebrated Ranger-General of Silvermoon, commanding the defense of Quel'Thalas during the Third War. When Prince Arthas Menethil marched the Scourge into the high elven kingdom to reach the Sunwell, Sylvanas fought fiercely to delay his advance. Frustrated by her resistance, Arthas murdered her, but denied her a clean death. He ripped her soul from her corpse and twisted it into a vengeful banshee, forcing her to serve the Scourge and assist in the slaughter of her own people.

Tallonkai Swiftroot. Tallonkai Swiftroot is a night elf resident of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Concerned with the emerging corruption tainting the great boughs, he enlists young adventurers to recover enchanted relics and stem the foul forces plaguing the woods. Dwelling in the canopy settlement of Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot keeps a watchful eye over the surrounding woods. Like many night elves living beneath the boughs of the newly grown World Tree, he is alarmed by the unnatural agitation of the wildlife and the unsettling shadows gathering at the edges of their settlements.

Taragaman the Hungerer. Taragaman the Hungerer is a hulking felguard lurking within the molten caverns of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. While widely feared as the demonic master behind the Searing Blade cult, his presence in the fiery depths serves a darker, more deceptive purpose. The Horde seeks his destruction to eliminate the demonic taint poisoning the city's underbelly. Prowling amidst the magma pools of Ragefire Chasm, Taragaman the Hungerer represents an immediate and terrifying threat to the safety of Orgrimmar. For many scouts and young warriors sent into the dark chasm, the demonic felguard appears to be the central ringleader of the Searing Blade cultists, wielding infernal strength to bend the weak-willed and corrupt the subterranean passages beneath Thrall's fortress.

Targorr the Dread. Targorr the Dread is an infamous Blackrock orc executioner imprisoned deep within the Stormwind Stockade. Known for his brutal tortures of captured Stormwind soldiers, his execution was indefinitely delayed by bureaucratic incompetence and corruption. When the Stockade erupted into revolt under the Defias Brotherhood, Targorr broke free and allied with the rioting convicts. Before his capture, Targorr the Dread served as the supreme executioner for the Blackrock clan under Warlord Gath'Ilzogg. Operating out of the occupied ruins in Redridge, his cruelty stood out as exceptionally savage even by the violent standards of the Dark Horde. Stormwind guards and militiamen who fought to defend the borderlands were subjected to agonizing torment and slow death at his hands, making his name one of the most reviled in the kingdom.

Tavernkeep Smitts. Tavernkeep Smitts is the barkeep of the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. Operating at the social center of Duskwood, Smitts possesses an encyclopedic knowledge of town gossip and unsolved local tragedies. His long memory and keen eye make him an invaluable contact for anyone investigating the region's dark history. Behind the bar of the Scarlet Raven Tavern, Tavernkeep Smitts offers warm hearth fires and drink to the weary travelers, local townspeople, and nervous Night Watch guards braving Duskwood's perils. As one of the longest-standing public faces in town, Smitts hears every rumor that filters through the gloom. While other townsfolk shrink behind locked shutters, Smitts maintains a pragmatic, observant eye on everyone who passes through his door, noting unusual behavior, hurried departures, and strange patrons.

Telf Joolam. Telf Joolam is a Darkspear jungle troll shaman watching over the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. He guides initiates of the Horde through the trials required to commune with and command the volatile element of fire. Perched among the crags overlooking the borderlands, Telf Joolam tends the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. Unlike the calm certainty of earth or the patient depth of water, the fiery spirits require sharp discipline and unwavering focus. Telf acts as a trialmaster, preparing young shamans to prove their worth to the wild embers before they are consumed by them.

Terenthis. Terenthis is a night elf druid stationed in the coastal settlement of Auberdine. Representing the Cenarion Circle, he is investigating the alarming corruption spreading through Darkshore and Teldrassil. He enlists capable travelers to gauge rising threats along the coast and assist local allies trapped by corrupted wildlife. Sent to Auberdine by the Cenarion Circle, Terenthis focuses on tracking the spread of Fel Moss and other corruptive forces seeping into Darkshore from Teldrassil. The night elves view this creeping blight with immense concern, fearing the wild balance of northern Kalimdor may fracture completely if left unchecked. Terenthis works to uncover the root causes of the rot and devise ways to halt its advance before it consumes the forests.

Theocritus. Archmage Theocritus is an eccentric human wizard who resides at the peak of the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest. Formerly affiliated with the Kirin Tor of Dalaran, he now lives independently, surrounded by servants and magical scrying devices. From his high sanctum, Theocritus directs his arcane talents toward keeping watch over the kingdom and combating his dark rival, the rogue mage Morganth. Once a member of Dalaran's prestigious Kirin Tor, Archmage Theocritus chose to establish an independent stronghold far to the south in the kingdom of Stormwind. He settled in the prominent Tower of Azora, situated near the eastern road to Redridge. Theocritus is known for his eccentric habits and comfortable lifestyle, employing an extensive household staff that includes numerous gnomish attendants and his own dedicated clothier, Morley Eberlein. Though he keeps himself largely detached from the mundane concerns of local villagers, his presence serves as a critical magical bulwark in eastern Elwynn.

Thork. Thork is an orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads who oversees the settlement's local defenses. Charged with securing the bustling crossroads of the Barrens, he directs Horde adventurers to push back raiders, secure vital supply lines, and weed out internal threats. The Crossroads serves as the beating heart of Horde transit in Kalimdor, connecting Durotar, Mulgore, and the wilds beyond. Holding it is no easy feat. Thork shoulders the responsibility of defending the town from constant external pressures. Between quillboar raids, centaur aggression, and marauding harpies, his forces are stretched thin, forcing him to rely on capable travelers and emerging champions to handle critical security tasks.

Thotar. Thotar is a seasoned orc hunter trainer stationed in the settlement of Razor Hill in Durotar. He guides aspiring Horde scouts and marksmen in the ancient traditions of tracking, archery, and bonding with wild beasts. For young orcs and trolls taking their first steps outside the Valley of Trials, he provides the foundational rites needed to master Kalimdor's rugged fauna. Perched within the fortified hub of Razor Hill, Thotar serves as a veteran instructor for marksmen of the Horde. While new recruits learn the very basics in the Valley of Trials, it falls to Thotar to guide hunters as they face the harsher predatory wilderness of Durotar. Drawing upon traditions passed down through countless generations of orcs, he teaches not only marksmanship, but the deeper respect required to live alongside and direct Kalimdor's deadliest creatures.

Thrall. Thrall is the Warchief of the Horde and the ruler of Durotar, holding court from the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar. Once a human slave raised to be an arena gladiator, he broke the chains of his people, rediscovered their ancient shamanic traditions, and led them across the Great Sea to build a new homeland. Born Go'el, the son of Frostwolf chieftain Durotan and Draka, Thrall was orphaned as an infant when his parents were murdered by Gul'dan's assassins. He was discovered by human commander Aedelas Blackmoore, who named him 'Thrall'—meaning slave—and raised him at Durnholde Keep as an arena fighter with an education in human tactics. Aided by his foster sister Taretha Foxton, Thrall eventually escaped his captors. Guided by the Frostwolf exile Drek'Thar, he cast aside demonic corruption to master the elemental spirits, becoming the first of a new generation of orcish shaman.

Thyn'tel Bladeweaver. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver is a night elf sentinel stationed at the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus. She is deeply troubled by the disappearance of Priestess Velinde Starsong and dispatches trusted Alliance adventurers to track down clues regarding her whereabouts. Through her inquiries, she seeks to piece together the unraveling mystery behind the Scythe of Elune. Standing watch over Darnassus from the Warrior's Terrace, Thyn'tel Bladeweaver represents the vigilant military arm of the kaldorei. When Priestess Velinde Starsong mysteriously vanished without leaving word, Thyn'tel refused to let the trail go cold. Sensing that grave forces were involved, she takes it upon herself to commission adventurers willing to dig into the priestess's personal belongings and uncover where her journey led.

Tirion Fordring. Tirion Fordring is a legendary paladin and former lord of Mardenholde Keep, now living in quiet exile in the Eastern Plaguelands. One of the original five paladins anointed into the Knights of the Silver Hand, he was stripped of his title and lands for honoring a debt of honor to an enemy orc. From his modest cabin along the Thondroril River, he watches over the tragedy unfolding across Lordaeron and worries for his son. Before the ruin of Lordaeron, Tirion Fordring was renowned as one of the kingdom's finest knights. During the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol chose him alongside Uther the Lightbringer, Turalyon, Saidan Dathrohan, and Gavinrad the Dire to create the Knights of the Silver Hand. Armed with plate, holy devotion, and the Libram of Retribution, Tirion led soldiers through brutal clashes against the Old Horde, including the bloody Siege of Blackrock Spire. He was revered as an unyielding paragon of the Holy Light.

Tiza Battleforge. Tiza Battleforge is a veteran dwarven paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand stationed within Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries. Renowned for her steadfast devotion and insight, she guides young dwarven paladins along the path of virtue, charity, and self-sacrifice. Through study of the sacred texts and trials in the field, she tests whether initiates are truly ready to wield the Light's gift of resurrection. Within the serene chambers of the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge stands as one of the most respected dwarven paladins of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Initiates across the Alliance—directed by tutors such as Brandur Ironhammer in Ironforge, Azar Stronghammer in Dun Morogh, and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker in Stormwind—are sent to her to advance their spiritual education. Tiza believes that the Holy Light demands more than martial skill; it requires humble service, compassion, and unwavering fortitude against the encroaching darkness of the Scourge and other threats.

Tonga Runetotem. Tonga Runetotem is a knowledgeable tauren druid stationed outside the inn at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Dispatched from Thunder Bluff, he investigates an unnatural corruption seeping into the region's sparse oases and sickening the native wildlife. His research aims to trace the spiritual disturbance back to its origin before the delicate ecosystem collapses entirely. Amid the dust and bustling commerce of the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem keeps a quiet vigil. Sent down from the high mesas of Mulgore by his elders in Thunder Bluff, Tonga possesses an intimate understanding of the arid savannah. Where others see only barren scrub and predatory beasts, he reads the subtle currents of the land's health. In recent times, those currents have soured dramatically, compelling him to recruit capable travelers to investigate the heart of the savannah's life: its isolated oases.

Turak Runetotem. Turak Runetotem is a revered tauren druid trainer residing in the Hall of Elders atop Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise. Serving as a trusted assistant to Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem, he guides novice tauren along the sacred paths of nature and balance. Through Turak, young druids undertake foundational trials to commune with spirits and master animal aspects. Within the serene confines of the Hall of Elders, Turak Runetotem stands as one of the Horde's foremost druidic mentors. Renowned for his deep patience and balanced demeanor, he assists Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem in reviving the ancient druidic arts among the tauren people. Turak ensures that every aspiring druid honors the will of the Earthmother, teaching that physical power must always be grounded in spiritual respect and harmony with nature.

Twilight Lord Kelris. Twilight Lord Kelris is an orc warlock and high-ranking leader within the Twilight's Hammer cult operating deep inside Blackfathom Deeps. From his perch in the Moonshrine Sanctum, he leads dark rituals and tends to the primordial hydra Aku'mai, aiming to usher in a reign of cosmic chaos. Twilight Lord Kelris directs the cultists of the Twilight's Hammer who seized the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. For years, Kelris slipped through the grasp of watchful eyes in Darnassus, evading the Argent Dawn and earning a grim reputation: whenever ancient malice stirred across Kalimdor, Kelris was suspected of orchestrating it. Rather than serving warlords or clans, this orc has pledged himself entirely to the Old Gods, seeking to unmake mortal civilization and return Azeroth to a state of absolute, primordial chaos.

Tyrande Whisperwind. Tyrande Whisperwind is the High Priestess of Elune and the supreme leader of the night elves. Alongside her beloved, the Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage, she guided her people through the cataclysmic War of the Ancients and ten millennia of the Long Vigil. Now governing from the sacred boughs of Teldrassil, she commands the Sisterhood of Elune and directs the Sentinel army in defense of Kalimdor's sacred wilderness. Born in the ancient city of Suramar, Tyrande grew up alongside the twin brothers Malfurion and Illidan Stormrage. While the brothers followed druidism and sorcery, Tyrande entered the service of Elune as a novice in the sisterhood. When the demonic Burning Legion first invaded Azeroth during the War of the Ancients, the dying High Priestess Dejahna chose Tyrande as her successor. Blessed with direct favor from the Moon Goddess, Tyrande transformed the Sisterhood into a radiant fighting force, wielding both divine restoration and searing lunar wrath to deliver her people from the brink of total annihilation.

Varimathras. Varimathras is a dreadlord of the nathrezim race who serves as the chief lieutenant and military advisor to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Forced to pledge loyalty to the Banshee Queen after suffering defeat during the civil war for Lordaeron, he now stands at her right hand in the Royal Quarter of the Undercity. Before the Third War, Varimathras and his fellow dreadlords worked directly under Kil'jaeden to break and reshape the spirit of Ner'zhul into the Lich King. Bound alongside his brothers Detheroc and Balnazzar, he oversaw the Scourge in Lordaeron while Archimonde invaded Kalimdor. When the Legion fell at Mount Hyjal, the triumvirate remained entrenched in the ruins of the Capital City, entirely unaware of their master's demise until Prince Arthas returned to drive them into hiding.

Verdan the Everliving. Verdan the Everliving is a colossal bog beast lurking deep within the verdant tunnels of the Wailing Caverns. Once a peaceful protector of the underground springs and flora, he was twisted by the waking nightmare radiating from the sleeping druid Naralex. Now bound to the corrupted Druids of the Fang, Verdan violently attacks any who venture into his damp hollows. Long before Naralex arrived to tap into the natural springs of the Barrens, Verdan was formed from the overgrown foliage, silt, and moisture filling the caves. Thought to be the original guardian spirit of the subterranean oasis, Verdan was an ancient, gentle elemental keeping watch over the underground flora.

Verner Osgood. Verner Osgood is the resident blacksmith of Lakeshire, stationed just outside the town smithy. Balancing local civilian trade with the crushing demands of the Stormwind military, he works tirelessly to keep horses shod and defenders armed amid relentless gnoll raids. Standing by the forge in central Lakeshire, Verner Osgood represents the strained industrial backbone of the Redridge Mountains. Tasked with crafting basic supplies like horseshoes for local mounts, Verner finds his stock constantly co-opted to manufacture weapons and armor for the Stormwind Guard. With the kingdom stretching its borders thin and local garrisons lacking supplies, independent smiths like Verner must carry the logistical burden of the realm's defense.

Viktori Prism'Antras. Viktori Prism'Antras is an eccentric stargazer residing in a small hillside hut overlooking Darkshire. While the town around him succumbs to dread and looming horrors, Viktori focuses intently on building a telescope to view the heavens clearly. To realize his vision, he relies on adventurous travelers to acquire intricate parts based on gnomish schematics. Perched up the slope just beyond the gryphon roost, Viktori Prism'Antras spends his days peering outward from the gloom of Duskwood. Amid undead incursions, ravenous spiders, and creeping shadows, his obsession lies far beyond the suffocating canopy. He dreams of building a magnificent optical telescope capable of bringing the stars into brilliant focus, offering a quiet escape from the dread that engulfs the hamlet.

Viscous Fallout. Viscous Fallout is a corrupted water elemental wandering the irradiated corridors of Gnomeregan. Once a pure spirit inhabiting the city's pristine aquifers, it was twisted into a toxic monstrosity by Mekgineer Thermaplugg's devastating radiation release. Before the fall of Gnomeregan, the gnomish capital relied on sophisticated, intricate waterways and clean subterranean aquifers to power and sustain its mechanical marvels. A solitary water elemental dwelt peacefully within this pristine water supply. When the radiation vents were opened on Mekgineer Thermaplugg's treacherous advice to wipe out the invading troggs, the resulting chemical contamination seeped deep into the city's reservoirs, trapping the elemental and corrupting its very substance.

Vol'jin. Vol'jin is the chieftain of the Darkspear trolls and a master shadow hunter. Residing in Grommash Hold alongside Warchief Thrall, he acts as a trusted advisor to the Horde while working to secure his displaced people a permanent home in Durotar. Vol'jin took up leadership of the Darkspear tribe following the tragic death of his father, Sen'jin, on their ancestral island home. When sea witch-worshipping murlocs and human forces nearly destroyed the isolated tribe, Thrall's orcs intervened, forging a deep bond between the two peoples. After evacuating the ruins of their islands, Vol'jin pledged his trolls to the New Horde and brought them across the Great Sea to Kalimdor.

Warden Thelwater. Warden Thelwater is the besieged overseer of the Stockade, Stormwind City's underground maximum-security prison. Caught unprepared when a violent riot erupted among the Defias prisoners, he now desperately recruits capable adventurers to quell the rebellion before word spreads to the city above. Hidden beneath the canals of Stormwind, the Stockade holds the kingdom's most dangerous miscreants, petty thieves, and political conspirators. Warden Thelwater was charged with keeping them securely locked away, but an organized revolt took the guards completely off guard. With the prisoners overwhelming security and taking control of the cells, Thelwater found himself barricaded at the threshold, struggling to contain an armed insurrection right beneath the streets of the capital.
