William Pestle. William Pestle is a human alchemist staying inside Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn. Together with his brother Morgan, he helps run the apothecary shop in Stormwind's Trade District. He frequently employs traveling adventurers to gather odd reagents like kobold candles, murloc kelp, and herbal supplies. While his brother Morgan Pestle manages the counter at Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District of Stormwind City, William operates out of the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. Being stationed in Elwynn Forest allows him to work closely with local gatherers and secure raw materials that city shops constantly require. He maintains regular shipments back to the capital, ensuring Stormwind's citizens have steady access to restorative salves, draughts, and powders.

Wizbang Cranktoggle. Wizbang Cranktoggle is an eccentric gnome engineer residing on the upper floor of the Auberdine inn. Despite being far from the cog-filled halls of Gnomeregan or Ironforge, he has turned his mechanical ingenuity toward setting up and maintaining automated communication devices known as buzzboxes across the wild coast of Darkshore. While the night elves of Auberdine prefer living in harmony with nature and leaning upon ancient customs, Wizbang Cranktoggle represents the curious, tinkering presence of the Alliance. Perched on the top floor of Auberdine's inn, surrounded by tools and spare components, Wizbang pays little mind to the solemn druidic traditions of Kalimdor, focusing instead on pragmatic mechanical challenges.

Yaw Sharpmane. Yaw Sharpmane is an experienced tauren hunter trainer stationed in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. He guides young hunters venturing out from Camp Narache, helping them master the wild beasts of their ancestral plains. Positioned amidst the tents and fires of Bloodhoof Village, Yaw Sharpmane serves the Shu'halo as an instructor in the ways of marksmanship, tracking, and survival. Young hunters who have proven themselves in Red Cloud Mesa are directed to Yaw to hone their craft as they step onto the broader plains of Mulgore.

Addle's Stead. Addle's Stead is an abandoned farmstead in southwestern Duskwood, lying quiet under the forest's gloom south of Raven Hill. While its original homesteaders fled long ago, the farm has become a hidden staging ground for the Defias Brotherhood. Like many of the forgotten homesteads scattered across Duskwood, Addle's Stead fell into disrepair when darkness and ruin enveloped the region. Rather than remaining empty, the farm has been repurposed by the Defias Brotherhood. Agents prowl the perimeter, lurk within the decrepit farmhouse, and stash supplies in the barn, using the shadowy cover of southwestern Duskwood to escape the notice of both the Night Watch and Stormwind authorities.

Agama'gor. Agama'gor is a major Bristleback quilboar encampment situated in the southern Barrens, nestled just north of the road leading west toward Mulgore from Camp Taurajo. It represents a constant thorn in the side of the nearby Horde outpost, teeming with hostile quilboar fiercely clinging to their rugged territory. Sprawling across the dusty plains of the southern Barrens, Agama'gor serves as a fortified settlement for the aggressive Bristleback tribe of quilboar. Located dangerously close to Camp Taurajo, the quilboar here maintain a dense network of brambles, huts, and crude totems. Their heavy presence poses an active threat to travelers moving between the Barrens and the grassy hills of Mulgore, prompting Horde scouts and hunters to wage a perpetual war of containment against them.

Agamand Family Crypt. Tucked into the hills just north of Agamand Mills, the Agamand Family Crypt is the ancient resting ground of one of Tirisfal's wealthiest farming dynasties. Now claimed by the Scourge under Captain Dargol, its tombs have been ripped open, and the slumbering ancestors raised as mindless terrors. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held expansive estates across northern Tirisfal Glades, entombing their forebears within this hillside mausoleum. When the Plague brought ruin to the kingdom, the crypt fell into the clutches of Captain Dargol, an agent of the Scourge. Rather than letting the wealthy lineage rest in peace, Dargol employed dark necromancy to awaken the entombed skeletons and vengeful apparitions, transforming a sacred burial ground into an aggressive Scourge foothold right on the edge of Forsaken territory.

Agamand Mills. Agamand Mills is a sprawling farm and windmill complex nestled in the northern heights of Tirisfal Glades. Once the proud estate of the wealthy Agamand dynasty, it has fallen into ruin and stands as the largest Scourge stronghold in the region. Centuries ago, wealthy noble immigrants from Strom established the Agamand estate, building a vast milling network across northern Tirisfal. When the Third War broke out and the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the patriarch Gregor Agamand refused to flee, fortifying the compound and convincing his retainers and laborers to make their stand. Their provisions and stone walls might have held, but their youngest son, Devlin Agamand, betrayed his blood. Devlin slaughtered the estate watchmen and let the walking dead into the sleeping quarters. Crippled from within, the remaining defenders were wiped out, and the family joined the mindless ranks of the undead.

Aldrassil. Aldrassil is the colossal bough-tree and settlement nestled at the heart of Shadowglen in northeastern Teldrassil. Serving as the primary refuge and training ground for young kaldorei, its carved hollows shelter trainers, merchants, and local leadership. Rising high above the secluded vale of Shadowglen, Aldrassil functions as both shelter and civic hub for young night elves taking their first steps in the world. Built into and around the colossal trunk of this ancient growth, winding ramps lead past class trainers and artisans to the high roost where Tenaron Stormgrip oversees the glade's protection. While the world bough Teldrassil stretches across the horizon, Aldrassil provides a safe, grounded canopy where novices learn their arts before venturing down into the troubled wilds of Kalimdor.

Alexston Farmstead. The Alexston Farmstead is a derelict farm in Westfall, overgrown and prowled by haywire Harvest Watchers. Once the childhood home of Stormwind's city architect, Baros Alexston, it has fallen into ruin like much of the breadbasket around it. Situated amidst the dry plains of Westfall, the Alexston Farmstead stands as another grim testament to the kingdom's neglect. Like neighboring estates, the farm was abandoned by its caretakers when banditry erupted across the countryside. Today, the fields are overgrown, and the mechanical Harvest Watchers left behind to tend the crops have spun out of control, violently attacking anyone who approaches the barren farmhouse.

Algaz Station. Algaz Station is a dwarven military outpost situated in northwestern Loch Modan, directly south of the fortified pass of Dun Algaz. Manning the approach to the northern tunnels, its garrison of Mountaineers helps safeguard travelers and watch the frontier leading toward the Wetlands. Perched just east of North Gate Pass and south of Dun Algaz, Algaz Station serves as a vital strategic watchpoint for the kingdom of Ironforge. A cadre of dwarven Mountaineers maintains a permanent vigil here, keeping the vital road between Loch Modan and the northern lowlands open to trade and troop movements. Given the frequent threats in the surrounding hills, from wandering beasts to encroaching troggs, the outpost provides respite, repairs, and martial support for weary travelers before they venture through the mountain tunnels.

Alterac Mountains. The Alterac Mountains are a rugged, snow-capped range rising directly above the rolling pastures of Hillsbrad. Once the heart of a proud human kingdom, the slopes now harbor ruined settlements, bandit factions, and dangerous wilderness where travelers rarely walk unguarded. Long before the hills fell into chaos, these highlands formed the sovereign nation of Alterac, one of the seven kingdoms born from ancient Arathor. That legacy shattered during the Second War when King Aiden Perenolde struck a clandestine pact with the Old Horde, allowing orcish forces passage through the peaks in exchange for his kingdom's safety. The Alliance of Lordaeron uncovered the betrayal and deposed Perenolde, leaving the region fractured by martial law and territorial disputes.

Alther's Mill. Alther's Mill is a ruined lumber mill tucked into the rugged hills northeast of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains. Once a vital source of processed timber for local builders, the abandoned grounds have deteriorated into a haven for feral scavengers and prowling predators. For adventurers traveling east toward Stonewatch, the dilapidated structures serve as a grim landmark marking the boundary of safe frontier territory. Before the region fell prey to invading predators and orc raids, Alther's Mill bustled with timber trade that supplied the construction of Lakeshire and surrounding settlements. Its quiet clearing northeast of Lake Everstill provided ready access to mountain timber stands. As turmoil mounted across the kingdom of Stormwind and the Blackrock clan pushed down from the heights of Stonewatch, local millers abandoned the facility, leaving the dry timber buildings and wheel to decay into rot.

Ambermill. Ambermill is a fortified human settlement in central Silverpine Forest, situated just southwest of Lordamere Lake. Originally a Gilnean lumber village, it is now occupied by surviving wizards and apprentices of Dalaran who are tapping into ancient ley lines. Their presence represents a dangerous outpost of human resistance on the southern borders of the Forsaken realm. Before the Third War, Ambermill was a quiet lumber town on lands owned by the Gilnean nobleman Darius Crowley. When King Genn Greymane erected the Greymane Wall to seal his kingdom away, Ambermill was left stranded outside alongside Pyrewood Village. In the chaotic aftermath of Lordaeron's fall, the surviving wizards of the Kirin Tor moved in and fortified the settlement. Dalaran spellscribes, conjurors, and apprentices now patrol its buildings and stables, using Ambermill as a forward redoubt against the undead.

Amberstill Ranch. Amberstill Ranch is a tranquil dwarven homestead nestled along the snowy roadway toward Loch Modan, directly north of Gol'Bolar Quarry. It serves as the primary breeding and training grounds for Ironforge's celebrated mountain rams. Adventurers visit the ranch to acquire hardy dwarven mounts, train in riding, or help the family defend their livestock from local predators. Tucked against the crags of Dun Morogh, Amberstill Ranch is renowned throughout Khaz Modan for raising the sturdiest mountain rams in the Eastern Kingdoms. The Amberstill family manages the stables and paddocks, training these sure-footed beasts to navigate treacherous snowy passes and steep alpine cliffs. Outside of supplying riding mounts and domestic livestock, the family often contends with the savage fauna of the hills, particularly wandering wendigos drawn by the scent of fresh flock.

Ameth'Aran. Ameth'Aran is an ancient ruin in southern Darkshore, once a thriving city where Queen Azshara's Highborne practiced arcane sorcery. When the Great Sundering shattered the ancient world, the city fell with it. Today, its broken colonnades are haunted by the vengeful ghosts of the elves who died there. Before the Great Sundering, Ameth'Aran and its sister settlement, Bashal'Aran, stood as twin centers of Highborne influence along the ancient coastline. Under the favor of Queen Azshara, the city boasted bustling bazaars and graceful shrines to Elune, though its ruling nobility dedicated themselves to unrestrained arcane experimentation. Governed from afar by the sorcerer Athrikus Narassin in the Tower of Althalaxx, the city thrived until the catastrophic collapse of the Well of Eternity tore the Kaldorei Empire apart.

Angerfang Encampment. The Angerfang Encampment is the primary stronghold of the Dragonmaw clan in the central Wetlands. Led by Chieftain Nek'rosh Skullcrusher, these renegade orcs use the sprawling camp as a staging ground to threaten nearby dwarven settlements and plot the destruction of Menethil Harbor. Sprawling across the muck of the central Wetlands, the Angerfang Encampment serves as the fortified heart of Dragonmaw power in the region. Unlike the scattered raiding parties found wandering the marshes, this compound boasts heavily defended barricades, watchtowers, and a formidable host of warriors, bonewarders, and dark spellcasters loyal to the old ways. From here, the Dragonmaw project military force across the marshlands, raiding travelers along the roads and menacing nearby dwarven digs like Whelgar's Excavation Site.

Anvilmar. Anvilmar is a fortified dwarven outpost nestled in the snowy depths of Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh. Centered around a massive stone forge, it serves as the primary training grounds and rallying point for young Bronzebeard dwarves and displaced gnomish refugees beginning their adventures. Tucked away in the northern crags of Coldridge Valley, Anvilmar stands as an enduring symbol of dwarven perseverance. Dominated by a roaring central forge, this sturdy masonry complex houses class mentors, supply vendors, and veteran mountain mountaineers who drill recruits before sending them out into the wider kingdom. Though sheltered behind towering drifts, the settlement remains on constant guard against the hostile Frostmane trolls and aggressive wild beasts prowling the frozen valley.

Apothecarium. The Apothecarium is the southwestern quarter of the Undercity and the headquarters of the Royal Apothecary Society. Within these noxious laboratories, Forsaken alchemists labor tirelessly under Master Apothecary Faranell to concoct virulent plagues, toxins, and engineered horrors. It stands as the grim heart of Undercity's biological research, vital to Lady Sylvanas's campaign against the living and the Scourge. Occupying the southwestern terrace of the subterranean capital, the Apothecarium is a labyrinth of bubbling vats, dissection tables, and pungent chemical fumes. Led by Master Apothecary Faranell, the Royal Apothecary Society utilizes this district to advance their understanding of mortality and rot. Here, alchemists and surgeons experiment on tissue grafts, vivisection, and the assembly of mighty abominations. Their overriding purpose, mandated by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, is the formulation of a new plague capable of eradicating both the Scourge and the lingering human presence across Lordaeron.

Astranaar. Astranaar is the primary Night Elf settlement in central Ashenvale, built across a serene lake island straddling the ancient forest road. Serving as the beating heart of Alliance operations in the region, it provides vital refuge to travelers facing encroaching threats from hostile furbolgs, satyrs, and the Horde. Situated atop an island in the middle of a forest lake, Astranaar stands as the largest night elven settlement in Ashenvale. Connected to the mainland by wooden footbridges spanning the waters, the town houses sentinels, priests, and artisans who keep vigil over the woodlands. In addition to offering basic comforts such as an inn, traders, and an expert leatherworker, its elevated perches host a flight master providing hippogryph travel to distant outposts across Kalimdor.

Auberdine. Auberdine is a coastal night elven port town on the gloomy shores of Darkshore, serving as the Alliance's primary maritime gateway to northern Kalimdor. Sheltered beneath overcast skies and pine-covered bluffs, it connects the island home of Teldrassil to the Eastern Kingdoms while serving as an administrative haven against the encroaching wilderness. Resting along the shores of the Veiled Sea, Auberdine is the only major settlement to successfully endure in modern Darkshore. Unlike the secluded treetop cities of Teldrassil, Auberdine looks outward, serving as the Alliance's busiest port in the north. Regular ships sail between here and Menethil Harbor in the Eastern Kingdoms, while local ferries run to Rut'theran Village at the boughs of the World Tree. Because of its trade role, Auberdine embraces a more cosmopolitan air than traditional elven enclaves; visitors find lamps illuminating stone-laid streets, bilingual signs in Darnassian and Common, and outland merchants including dwarves and gnomes mingling among the low-slung, arched timber houses.

Azurelode Mine. Azurelode Mine is an active Alliance iron mine nestled in the southwestern hills of Hillsbrad Foothills. Guarded by Southshore's militia and worked by human laborers, its steady supply of ore fuels the local human war effort against the Forsaken of Tarren Mill. Situated southwest of the open farmland and just west of Southshore, Azurelode Mine has long tapped into the mineral-rich ridges along the coast. Before the Greymane Wall was sealed, these hills were considered part of Gilnean territory. Today, human miners labor deep underground under the watchful eye of Foreman Bonds, extracting iron to forge arms and armor for the Alliance defenders holding the region against the Undercity.

Bael'dun Digsite. The Bael'dun Digsite is a dwarven excavation carved deep into the mountains along the western edge of Mulgore. Established by Prospector Khazgorm's team out of Bael Modan, the quarry is viewed by the local tauren as a direct desecration of their ancestral homeland and an insult to the Earth Mother. Perched on the mountain slopes of western Mulgore, the Bael'dun Digsite represents the southernmost reach of the dwarven Explorers' League expedition based out of Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. Unconcerned with territorial borders or the spiritual traditions of the newly settled tribes, dwarven prospectors arrived with picks, shovels, and blasting powder to unearth ancient Titan relics buried beneath the plains.

Bael'dun Keep. Bael'dun Keep is an imposing dwarven fortification overlooking the Bael Modan excavation in the southern Barrens. Under the command of General Twinbraid, this fortress anchors the Alliance's controversial presence in the region, bringing them into violent conflict with the surrounding Horde territories. Constructed according to designs by the dwarven architect Haggis Boatmurder, Bael'dun Keep serves as the fortified military heart of the Ironforge presence in the southern Barrens. Towering over the expansive excavation trenches of Bael Modan, the fortress protects the Prospectors and archaeologists searching for ancient titan artifacts. Heavily armed with ironworks and artillery, its garrison maintains a vigilant watch, securing dwarven supply lines and projecting Alliance martial power straight into Kalimdor's heartland.

Bael Modan. Bael Modan is a fortified dwarven outpost and archaeological dig site located in the southern Barrens. Established by dwarven excavators searching for ancient Titan relics, the heavily armed installation has ignited a bitter conflict by displacing the indigenous Stonespire tauren. Bael Modan consists of the fortified Bael'dun Keep, an array of massive siege cannons, gyrocopter landing pads, and a deep open excavation pit. Dwarven prospectors arrived in Kalimdor under the conviction that an ancient Titan facility rests buried beneath the red earth. However, their blasting operations ripped directly through sacred ground belonging to the Stonespire tauren. Rather than negotiating, the dwarven expedition drove the Stonespire off their ancestral lands with gunfire and explosives, leaving the surviving tribesmen scattered and vengeful.

Balnir Farmstead. The Balnir Farmstead is a derelict estate in eastern Tirisfal Glades, northeast of the Ruins of Lordaeron. Once renowned for raising the famed white horses favored by Lordaeron's royal family, the lands now lie ruined and infested by wandering Scourge. Today, the estate stands as a somber monument to Prince Arthas Menethil's early life and the site where he claimed his undead steed. For generations, the Balnir family bred the legendary white stallions of Lordaeron from their homestead in the rolling hills of Tirisfal. As a boy, Prince Arthas Menethil frequently visited the farm to escape royal court life, befriending the young Jarim Balnir. It was here that Arthas assisted in the foaling of the colt he named Invincible. Years later, after a tragic riding accident claimed the steed's life, Invincible was laid to rest in the soil of the farmstead upon Arthas's personal request.

Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Ban'ethil Barrow Den is a sacred subterranean sanctuary hollowed out within the roots of Teldrassil. Originally created as a resting place for the sleeping Druids of the Talon, the cavern complex has recently fallen into chaos. The corrupted furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe have overrun its chambers, turning a place of peaceful slumber into a perilous den of madness. Barrow dens serve as sacred resting chambers where night elf druids slumber while projecting their spirits into the Emerald Dream. Ban'ethil Barrow Den was dedicated specifically to sheltering the Druids of the Talon as they communed with nature. Divided into upper and lower subterranean chambers, the den once resonated with tranquil reverie and deep meditative magic. However, the affliction sweeping Teldrassil's wildlife did not spare the Gnarlpine furbolgs, who invaded the complex, turning its hollowed halls into a fortified warren.

Ban'ethil Hollow. Ban'ethil Hollow is a rugged ravine cutting into the woodland just south of the main road connecting Dolanaar and Darnassus. It has become a dangerous haven for corrupted, aggressive furbolgs who pose a constant threat to travelers. Tucked away in the back of the ravine lies the entrance to the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Situated off the highway between Dolanaar and Darnassus, Ban'ethil Hollow is a sharp reminder that the boughs of Teldrassil are not entirely safe. Furbolgs driven mad by the strange affliction plaguing the World Tree have taken refuge throughout the rocky descent. They frequently stalk the nearby path, waiting to ambush unwary couriers and wandering sentinels. Deep within the ravine sits the threshold of the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, where slumbering druids and ancient tunnels face encroachment from the maddened beasts outside.

Bandarion Keep. Bandarion Keep is a fortified redoubt associated with Tyr's Watch, nestled in the western reaches of Tirisfal Glades near the Whispering Forest. Named in honor of Garek Bandarion, the outpost serves as an isolated bulwark amidst lingering threats across the woodland frontier. Its defenders contend with everything from hostile coastal murlocs to roving zealots and unstable undead. Situated near the secluded Whispering Forest in western Tirisfal Glades, Bandarion Keep stands as a solitary sentinel for the Forsaken. Named after Garek Bandarion, this stronghold is closely tied to Tyr's Watch. Quartermasters like Jorin Croge work diligently to keep the garrison supplied despite its remote and challenging position far from the bustling courtyards of the Undercity.

Baradin Bay. Baradin Bay is the expansive body of water lying between the shores of Khaz Modan, the Wetlands, the Arathi Highlands, and southern Lordaeron. Once vigorously patrolled by the powerful navy of Kul Tiras during the Second War, its waters now conceal treacherous reefs, sunken warships, and hostile aquatic predators. Framed by the coasts of Dun Morogh to the south and Lordaeron to the north, Baradin Bay serves as a vital maritime passage connecting the harbors of the Eastern Kingdoms. The bay is anchored by busy ports like Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands and Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. However, navigating these waters is perilous: shallow sandbanks, jagged shoals, and dangerous fauna like murlocs, crocolisks, and deep-sea sharks pose constant threats to sailors and travelers alike.

Bashal'Aran. Bashal'Aran is an ancient Highborne ruin situated in northern Darkshore, just east of Auberdine. Once a flourishing sister city to Ameth'Aran before the Great Sundering, the site now crawls with demonic satyrs and grells feeding on lingering arcane magic, while a solitary elven ghost remains trapped by a centuries-old curse. Before the Great Sundering broke ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne subjects in the twin towns of Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran. Governed by the powerful mage Athrikus Narassin, the cities boasted splendid markets and temples dedicated to Elune. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the cataclysm laid both settlements to waste. For reasons lost to time, Athrikus used his arcane mastery to bind his own second-in-command, the mage Asterion, into a moonstone seal within Bashal'Aran. Even after his physical body perished, Asterion's ghost remained shackled to the ruined shrine.

Bathran's Haunt. Bathran's Haunt is an ancient kaldorei ruin nestled in northwestern Ashenvale, east of the Zoram Strand. Recently, Forsaken herbalists and their guardians have overtaken the site to harvest local flora for their alchemical research, steadily withering the surrounding woodland. North of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran, crumbling night elf pillars stand swallowed by thick Ashenvale foliage. What was once a tranquil kaldorei relic has fallen under the shadow of the Forsaken. Skulking among the broken marble, undead herbalists and their enforcers have set up a crude open-air laboratory. Their presence alone blights the ancient soil: grass rots into a sickly brown, vibrant blossoms wilt, and an unnatural decay creeps through the grove as they methodically harvest rare woodland reagents for their experiments.

Beggar's Haunt. Beggar's Haunt is an abandoned Stormwind scout tower perched on a hillside in northeastern Duskwood, near the mountain road to Deadwind Pass. While originally built to keep watch over the kingdom's eastern borders, it has become an outpost for Forsaken infiltrators deep within Alliance territory. Perched above the foggy hills east of Manor Mistmantle, Beggar's Haunt was once an active observation post manned by the Stormwind Guard to secure the eastern approaches to the realm. As Grand Hamlet collapsed into the gloom of modern Duskwood and kingdom patrols withdrew to Darkshire, the stone tower was abandoned to the elements. Today, its commanding vantage point serves a far more sinister purpose: agents of the Forsaken, including members of the Royal Apothecary Society and Deathstalkers, use the ruined stronghold to conduct research and monitor the region under the Alliance's nose.

Beren's Peril. Beren's Peril is a secluded mountain cavern tucked in the rocky hills southwest of Ambermill in Silverpine Forest. It serves as an entrenched redoubt for rogue Scourge loyalists serving the necromancer Thule Ravenclaw, plotting against the nearby Forsaken. Tucked away high in the crags southwest of Ambermill, Beren's Peril consists of a shadowed cave and winding mountain path hidden from the main roadway. Following the devastation of the Third War, rogue Scourge undead under the command of the renegade necromancer Thule Ravenclaw fortified this enclave. Rather than bowing to the Dark Lady or retreating north, Ravenclaw's thralls—regents, guardians, and drudgers—gathered here in secret to muster an assault against the Forsaken base at the Sepulcher. Their presence was uncovered by Forsaken scouts, turning the quiet cliffside into an active warzone for Horde operatives sent to eliminate the threat before an attack could materialize.

Blackthorn Ridge. Blackthorn Ridge is a jagged, bramble-choked valley tucked away in the southern reaches of the Barrens, immediately north of Razorfen Kraul. The area crawls with aggressive Razormane quilboar guarding their thorny settlements. High on the ridge above sits the camp of the orc shaman Brine, watching over an unusually pure pool of mountain water. Nestled near the towering burls of Razorfen Kraul, Blackthorn Ridge is dominated by dense thickets of massive, sharp briars. The Razormane quilboar consider these grounds ancestral territory, using the natural barricades to ambush outsiders and stage skirmishes into the southern Barrens. Despite the constant danger, travellers seek out the ridge for the hermit orc shaman Brine, who tends a camp perched above a spring noted across Kalimdor for its remarkable clarity and spiritual purity.

Blackwolf River. Blackwolf River is a waterway flowing out of Cragpool Lake down through Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. Once a clean mountain stream, its waters have become thoroughly polluted by the Venture Company's aggressive logging and industrial operations. Descending from Cragpool Lake, the Blackwolf River cuts across the basin of Windshear Crag. What should be a pristine alpine tributary has instead borne the brunt of unchecked goblin enterprise. As the Venture Company clears the surrounding woodlands with heavy machinery and buzzsaws, sludge, oil, and logging waste leach steadily into the current. The despoiled river stands as a vivid example of the commercial plunder threatening Stonetalon's wilderness.

Blackwood Den. Blackwood Den is a corrupted furbolg encampment nestled in the southern reaches of Darkshore near the border of Ashenvale. Once a peaceful dwelling, the cave and surrounding camps have fallen into madness alongside the rest of the Blackwood tribe. A lone night elf scout named Volcor sits trapped within the cavern, awaiting aid from Auberdine. Situated near the southern border where Darkshore meets Ashenvale, Blackwood Den consists of a winding network of crude camps and a rocky cave. The Blackwood furbolgs who dwell here have succumbed to the pervasive corruption gripping the region, turning violently hostile toward outsiders. Deep inside the den's cave, the night elf Volcor remains pinned down and endangered by the aggressive tribe, desperately needing assistance from scouts and travelers dispatched from Auberdine.

Bladefist Bay. Bladefist Bay is the rugged stretch of coast lining eastern Durotar just outside the gates of Orgrimmar. Named in honor of Kargath Bladefist, the bay serves as a natural harbor facing the Great Sea, shadowed by craggy bluffs and the nearby southern shores of Azshara. Stretching along the northeastern edge of Durotar, Bladefist Bay opens directly into the vast waters of the Great Sea. Flanked by rocky cliffs and treacherous surf, it functions as a primary maritime threshold for the Horde capital of Orgrimmar. The tides frequently deposit driftwood, ocean refuse, and flotsam onto the coastline, earning it a reputation among locals as a natural collection point for ocean debris. Directly north, the ancient red cliffs and ruins of Azshara loom across the water, making the bay a vital maritime boundary for Durotar.

Bloodhoof Village. Bloodhoof Village is a central tauren settlement resting along the banks of Stonebull Lake in Mulgore. Named in honor of the Bloodhoof tribe, it serves as the first major gathering hub for young hunters and braves journeying out from Camp Narache toward Thunder Bluff. Led by Baine Bloodhoof, the village coordinates local defense, trade, and traditional rites across the plains. Situated around the clear waters of Stonebull Lake, Bloodhoof Village is a bustling center of commerce, craft, and ceremony in central Mulgore. Young tauren departing their trials at Camp Narache arrive here to hone their skills before venturing onward to the great mesas of Thunder Bluff. It is also well-known across Kalimdor for its master drum makers and the patient breeders who tame wild kodo beasts for travel.

Bloodtooth Camp. Bloodtooth Camp is an encampment of hostile, corrupted furbolgs tucked into central Ashenvale, situated just west of the Falfarren River. Led by the chieftain Ran Bloodtooth, these once-peaceful creatures have succumbed to dark madness and attack anyone who approaches. The camp is a primary target for Alliance scouts working to cleanse the surrounding woodlands. Nestled southwest of the southern Moonwell and west of the Falfarren River, Bloodtooth Camp serves as a stark reminder of Ashenvale's encroaching decay. The furbolgs living here were once connected to the sacred wilderness of Kalimdor, but a lingering spiritual corruption has consumed their tribe. Under the command of Ran Bloodtooth, they guard their crude settlement with rabid hostility, turning upon travelers and night elven protectors alike.

Bough Shadow. Bough Shadow is a secluded grove tucked away in the far northeastern corner of Ashenvale, east of Forest Song. It centers around a colossal Great Tree rooted over an ancient portal leading directly into the Emerald Dream. Bough Shadow houses one of the rare Great Trees grown from a cutting of the World Tree, Nordrassil. Planted long ago by druids following Fandral Staghelm, its roots plunge deep into the earth around a natural crossing into the Emerald Dream. Today, the tranquil yet imposing grove is heavily guarded by the Green Dragonflight. Emerald drakes such as Phantim and Dreamstalker circle above the canopy, while patrols of Emeraldon dragonspawn and oracles keep a vigilant, unyielding watch over the swirling green portal at its base, turning away any mortal who approaches unbidden.

Boulder Lode Mine. Boulder Lode Mine is an aggressive excavation cut into the hills of the northeastern Barrens. Though orcish banners and watchtowers suggest the Horde first established the site, it is now firmly seized and operated by the ruthless Venture Company. The presence of weathered orcish architecture around the mouth of Boulder Lode Mine indicates that the Horde once held or founded the claim. Today, however, the area crawls with Venture Company overseers and enforcers working under the direction of Boss Copperplug. The goblin syndicate strip-mines the canyon with little regard for the local ecosystem or their workers, driven purely by the search for valuable minerals, high-yield gems, and industrial machinery.

Boulderslide Cavern. Boulderslide Cavern is a subterranean warren tucked at the deepest end of Boulderslide Ravine in the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as the primary den and excavation site for the local Boulderslide kobolds, who obsessively tunnel in search of glowing mineral formations. The Boulderslide kobolds have burrowed deep into the crags of Stonetalon, establishing Boulderslide Cavern as their stronghold. Unlike ordinary vermin merely seeking shelter, these kobolds mine frantically for resonite, a rare glowing purple crystal embedded throughout the stone. The crystals pulse with lingering earthen magic, driving the creatures into a defensive frenzy against any intruders who approach their dig.

Boulderslide Ravine. Boulderslide Ravine is a rugged, secluded canyon tucked away in the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains, reached via Webwinder Path. Largely spared from the direct clashes between the Horde and Alliance, it serves as the rocky approach to Boulderslide Cavern and remains home to wild mountain beasts. Tucked away off Webwinder Path, Boulderslide Ravine is a narrow cut of rock in the Stonetalon heights. While loggers, night elves, and the Horde battle over timber and sacred glades throughout the region, this craggy pass remains relatively undisturbed by military forces. Wild mountain rams and roaming crag beasts like Cliff Stormers make up the local fauna, navigating the treacherous ledges and sheer stone walls. Prospectors also keep an eye on the ravine, as rich mineral veins frequently crop up along the rocky slopes leading deeper toward the cavern network.

Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. Brackwell Pumpkin Patch is an overrun farmstead in southeastern Elwynn Forest. Once home to the Brackwell family, the fields and cottage have been thoroughly seized by the Defias Brotherhood as an operational hideout. It serves as a meeting point for rogue conspirators and a staging ground for smuggling stolen gold. Situated southeast of the Stonefield homestead, the Brackwell farm was once a productive patch of Elwynn farmland. Today, the rightful owners have vanished without a trace, driven out or worse by the rising criminal tide. In their absence, the Defias Brotherhood claimed the farm's sturdy cottage and overgrown fields. The area functions as a safehouse and transfer post, where brigands regroup away from the watchful eyes of Goldshire's patrols. High-profile conspirators like Morgan the Collector use the isolated patch to receive shipments of illicitly gathered gold skimmed from the forest's mines.

Brambleblade Ravine. Brambleblade Ravine is a rugged canyon cutting into the northeastern edge of Red Cloud Mesa. It serves as a fortified den for the Bristleback quilboar tribe, who persistently raid the nearby tauren settlement of Camp Narache. Young tauren braves are sent here to prove their strength and protect their homeland from these fierce interlopers. Carved into the sun-scorched earth of Red Cloud Mesa, Brambleblade Ravine is choked with dense, thorny briars and quilboar encampments. The Bristleback tribe uses this natural fortress as a staging ground for raids against Camp Narache, threatening the safety of young tauren coming of age. Bristleback shamans and warriors, led by Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle, dwell deep within the ravine among trained battleboars. For the Shu'halo, striking into the heart of the canyon is a crucial rite of passage and a grim necessity to secure the plains.

Bramblescar. Bramblescar is a heavily fortified Razormane quilboar settlement situated in the southern Barrens. Thick, thorny brambles shield the encampment as its inhabitants wage a brutal war against the rival Bristleback tribe across the Gold Road. Carved into the jagged, giant briars of the southern Barrens, Bramblescar serves as a vital redoubt for the Razormane quilboar. These defensive brambles grow thick and sharp enough to deter casual wanderers, but the quilboar within are far from peaceful. Fiercely territorial and hostile to outsiders, they mount continuous skirmishes against anyone who ventures near their borders, viewing all non-quilboar as intruders upon land blessed by their ancient boar gods.

Brewnall Village. Brewnall Village is a small dwarven settlement nestled in Chill Breeze Valley near the entrance to Gnomeregan. Established by the Barleybrew family, this outpost serves as a proving ground for bold brewing experiments and regional defense against wild beasts. Despite being called a village, it functions largely as a rustic encampment in the snowy gnomish lowlands of Dun Morogh. Tucked away in the snowdrifts of Chill Breeze Valley, Brewnall Village lies squarely within the traditional gnomish reaches of western Dun Morogh. The settlement is home to the Barleybrew clan, stalwart dwarven brewers devoted to perfecting age-old recipes and crafting the ultimate stout. Though dubbed a village, the outpost consists mostly of tents and outdoor brewing equipment rather than permanent stone architecture. Between testing experimental batches of ale and defending against the ferocious local wolves and bears, the Barleybrews rely heavily on wandering mountaineers to gather rare ingredients and keep the valley secure.

Brightwater Lake. Brightwater Lake is the largest body of water in Tirisfal Glades, stretching across the mist-shrouded lowlands northeast of Brill. Once a tranquil retreat for the kingdom of Lordaeron, its waters now lie cold and dark, surrounding a central isle where an outcast necromancer conducts his forbidden research. Spanning the northern plains between the town of Brill and the Scarlet Watch Post, Brightwater Lake is a quiet and eerie landmark in the heart of Tirisfal. Thousands of years ago, its misty banks bore witness to ancient conflicts, including early clashes against the dreadlord Kathra'natir. In the peaceful centuries that followed under the Kingdom of Lordaeron, the lake served as a scenic country haven. Today, like the rest of the glades, its pristine character is long gone. The Plaguelands lie not far to the east, and the murky, chilled waters reflect only grey skies, withered trees, and the constant threat of roving murlocs and hostile undead.

Brightwood Grove. Brightwood Grove is a shadowed expanse of woodland located just west of Darkshire in Duskwood. Once part of the region's serene agrarian landscape, it is now infested with savage Nightbane worgen who make camp among ruined homesteads and attack any travelers wandering too close. Situated within sight of Darkshire's perimeter, Brightwood Grove represents the creeping peril threatening the town's borders. The homesteads and fences that once demarcated peaceful farmland now lie collapsed and rotting. In their place, crude camps have been erected by the Nightbane worgen, who prowl the overgrown clearings. The proximity of these wolf-beasts poses an ongoing threat to the town, forcing the Night Watch and passing adventurers to continually cull their numbers before the settlement is overrun.

Brill. Brill is the primary Forsaken settlement in the heart of Tirisfal Glades, situated just north of the Ruins of Lordaeron. Once a prosperous human town, it now serves as the administrative and military hub for newly awakened undead stepping beyond the confines of Deathknell. Before the Third War, Brill was a lively village under the sway of regional nobles such as the Barov and Agamand families. That prosperity ended when Kel'Thuzad chose the area for the Cult of the Damned's earliest experiments with the Plague of Undeath. The devastating blight swept through the population so quickly that local militia were driven out, leaving a sprawling mass graveyard in its wake. Now rebuilt by the Forsaken under the leadership of Magistrate Sevren, the town retains its weathered Lordaeron architecture beneath an atmosphere of grim purpose. Brill functions as the regional command center, coordinating defenses against Scarlet Crusade incursions, roaming Scourge remnants, and native beasts warped by necromantic decay.

Brill Town Hall. Brill Town Hall is the administrative heart of the settlement of Brill in central Tirisfal Glades. Standing as the most prominent structure in town, it serves as the civic headquarters from which the Forsaken govern their local holdings and coordinate the defense of the glades. While much of Lordaeron lies shattered and ruined, Brill Town Hall remains standing as a functioning civic center under undead rule. Inside, Magistrate Sevren directs town affairs from his podium, handing out vital commissions and directives to Forsaken adventurers. Aside from the Defiler's Den in the Arathi Highlands, it is one of the only recognized town halls in the known world actively run by the Forsaken, serving as a bleak parody and functional continuation of old Lordaeron's municipal bureaucracy.

Burning Blade Coven. Tucked into the northern cliffs of the Valley of Trials, the Burning Blade Coven is an infested cave network threatening the Horde's newest recruits. Corrupted cultists and summoned demons lurk within, turning an old mineral cavern into a staging ground for dark magic right on Durotar's doorstep. The dusty red mountains rimming the Valley of Trials were once simply a testing wilderness for young orcs and Darkspear trolls taking their first steps in service to the Horde. In recent days, however, dark rituals have taken hold of the northern caves. Imps and lesser fiends spill from the cavern mouth, stirring chaos and threatening recruits. Led by the shadowy warlock Yarrog Baneshadow, the Burning Blade cult has entrenched itself deep inside, turning what was once a routine training ground into an active battleground against demonic corruption.

Calmbreeze Inn. Calmbreeze Inn refers to the primary establishments offering shelter and services across Zephras Isle, found in both Shen'dar Village and Valaanar. They serve as essential rest stops for travelers exploring the island, housing local trade trainers, innkeepers, and historical artifacts. The Calmbreeze Inns provide sanctuary amid the winding trails of Zephras Isle. In Shen'dar Village, the inn operates under Coriella Calmbreeze and doubles as a central hub where island tradesfolk gather, including mentors in herbalism, skinning, and enchanting. Across the way in Valaanar, another Calmbreeze Inn accommodates local wayfarers and shelters rare curios, including an audio crystal recording the history of the ancient rebellion in Eldre'Thalas.

Camp Aparaje. Camp Aparaje was once a peaceful tauren village nestled in the eastern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. Today, it lies overrun and occupied by the hostile Grimtotem tribe, who slaughtered the original settlers and took the outpost for themselves. Perched along the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, Camp Aparaje was established by peaceful tauren looking to live quietly in the highlands. That tranquility was shattered when raiders from the nearby Grimtotem Post, led by Grundig Darkcloud, launched a brutal and unprovoked assault. The villagers were butchered or driven away, and survivors such as Makaba Flathoof were left mourning the destruction of their home while dreading the fate of captive kin.

Camp Narache. Camp Narache is a secluded village nestled upon Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore. It serves as the ancestral home of the Hawkwind tribe and the proving ground where young tauren begin their training. Sheltered high above the plains, the camp maintains ancient traditions while constantly guarding against encroaching quilboar and lingering centaur threats. Situated at the northern edge of the elevated Red Cloud Mesa, Camp Narache is the primary settlement of the Hawkwind tribe. The village consists of several large hide lodges and pavilions, including a communal tent for wounded braves, an armory, a bakery tent, and a spirit lounge dedicated to meditation and ancestral communion. At the center of the camp, tribal elders and path trainers stand in a circle at the heart of the camp, where the venerable Greatmother Hawkwind still offers guidance, guiding newly initiated youth as they step into their roles as defenders of the Earth Mother.

What is Camp Narache? Camp Narache is the starting village for young tauren, located atop Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore. It is the central encampment of the Hawkwind tribe, serving as a sanctuary where fledgling hunters, warriors, druids, and shamans master their crafts before traveling outward to Bloodhoof Village and Thunder Bluff.

Who leads the village? Chief Hawkwind guides the tribe's braves and coordinates the defenses of the mesa, alongside the tribe's revered elder, Greatmother Hawkwind. The tribe's trainers and elders gather at the center of the camp to instruct young adventurers.

What threats does the camp face? The encampment is continually harassed by Bristleback quilboar operating out of Brambleblade Ravine to the east. In addition to feral battleboars and striders wandering the surrounding bluffs, the lingering danger of predatory centaur bands keeps the Hawkwind braves on constant alert.

Can travelers easily leave the mesa? Red Cloud Mesa is naturally bounded by sheer cliffs. The only way down into the greater plains of Mulgore is along a guarded mountain path leading north, watched over by Hawkwind braves to prevent hostile beasts and quilboar from ambushing travelers.

Camp Taurajo. Camp Taurajo is a quiet tauren settlement nestled in the southern Barrens, sitting right along the mountain pass leading west into Mulgore. It serves as a vital frontier haven, offering tired wanderers an inn, supplies, profession mentors, and wind rider transit between the plains and central Kalimdor. Situated at the eastern mouth of the pass to Mulgore, Camp Taurajo is often the first glimpse of the wider Barrens seen by young tauren venturing out from Bloodhoof Village. Surrounded by dry scrubland and rugged mesas, the camp operates as both an outpost and a trading hub. It shelters hunters, leathercrafters, and field herbalists while maintaining wind rider connections to Thunder Bluff, the Crossroads, and Freewind Post deeper south.

Canals (Stormwind City). The Canals are a network of stone-lined waterways weaving through Stormwind City, separating its distinct districts. They serve as quiet thoroughfares for pedestrians and anglers, while quietly harboring hidden hazards and the entrance to the city's prison. The Canals link and define the districts of Stormwind, dividing the bustling markets of the Trade District from the aged alleys of Old Town, the cathedral gardens, and the Dwarven District. Stone bridges, archways, and waterside walkways frame quiet establishments like the Gallina Winery, tailor shops, and quiet residential homes. In addition to serving local merchants and recreational fishermen, the waterways conceal the fortified entrance to the Stockade, where Stormwind's most dangerous criminals and rebels are held beneath street level.

Canals (Undercity). The Canals form a murky, circular moat winding between the distinct quarters of the Undercity. Filled with an unnatural, noxious green slime rather than fresh water, they serve as both a sewage system and a grim symbol of the Forsaken's subterranean stronghold. Carved into the subterranean depths beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, the Canals encircle the heart of the Undercity, dividing its quarters with wide channels of sluggish green sludge. While mortal cities channel flowing river water to clean their avenues, the Forsaken have filled these stone conduits with industrial refuse, chemical runoff, and alchemical waste. The liquid emits a faint, sickly glow and foul vapors, making it impossible to traverse by ordinary magical means like water walking. Despite the lethality of the slurry, desperate anglers occasionally haul bizarre, tainted curiosities from the muck.

Cathedral of Light. The Cathedral of Light is the spiritual heart of Stormwind City and the primary sanctuary of the Church of the Holy Light. Standing tall over Cathedral Square, it serves as the central bastion for human priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Rebuilt after its devastation during the First War under the guidance of Archbishop Alonsus Faol and then-Bishop Benedictus, the Cathedral of Light stands as a towering beacon of resilience. Its vast halls and subterranean catacombs sheltered desperate refugees during the darkest hours of Stormwind's reconstruction. With the fall of Lordaeron to the Scourge during the Third War, the seat of the Church shifted south to Stormwind. Today, Archbishop Benedictus shepherds the faithful from this grand hall, providing spiritual guidance to the entire Alliance.

Cathedral Square. Cathedral Square is the spiritual and civic heart of Stormwind City, dominated by the majestic Cathedral of Light. Beyond serving as a place of worship and devotion, the bustling plaza houses municipal institutions like City Hall, the city orphanage, and the regional headquarters of the Argent Dawn. Situated northwest of the Trade District and southeast of the Dwarven District, Cathedral Square serves as the epicenter of faith in the Kingdom of Stormwind. Dominating the skyline is the Cathedral of Light, the preeminent sanctuary for followers of the Holy Light across Azeroth. Priests, paladins, and healers gather here to study, pray, and train. Citizens, pilgrims, and local schoolchildren led by School Mistress Danna regularly mingle in the square for conversation and contemplation.

Cavern of Mists. The Cavern of Mists is the expansive outer antechamber leading into the depths of the Wailing Caverns. Fed by subterranean geysers that erupt through the rock, its central pool and hanging fog harbor strange, mutated wildlife roaming just outside the portal threshold. Before descending into the true heart of the Wailing Caverns, travelers must navigate the Cavern of Mists. Thick, warm vapor hangs permanently in the air, fed by natural geysers erupting from the cavern floor into a deep central pool. Though it serves as an entryway, it is far from peaceful. Swarms of raptors, serpents, oozes, and semi-aquatic threshadons wander the ledges and waters, alongside notorious beasts like the hydra Trigore the Lasher. It provides adventurers an ominous preview of the unnatural growth festering deeper below.

Cenarion Enclave. The Cenarion Enclave is the verdant northwestern district of Darnassus, serving as the central gathering place and seat of power for the Cenarion Circle in the capital. While Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage lies slumbering within the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the night elven druids from the great hollows and living boughs of this grove. Occupying a high terrace above the Temple Gardens, the Cenarion Enclave is shaped from ancient oaks and ashes marked with runic bark. Convocations of the Cenarion Circle gather within structures molded directly from living wood and stone. With Malfurion Stormrage absent in the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm oversees affairs here, pushing his ambitious vision for Teldrassil despite lingering political friction with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Beyond the druids who meditate among its streams, the enclave also hosts the capital's elven hunters and the stables where skilled riders learn to tame Darnassian nightsabers.

Champions' Hall. Tucked away in the southern reaches of Old Town, the Champions' Hall serves as the officer's barracks and supply armory for the Alliance's decorated veterans in Stormwind. Beyond its threshold, quartermasters dispense specialized weapons, plate, and regalia to proven warriors of the faction. Access is strictly guarded, reserved only for officers who have demonstrated valor on the field of war. Hidden behind a guarded threshold in Old Town, the Champions' Hall is a restricted haven for the Alliance's most distinguished combatants. Military commanders gather here over tactical maps of Azeroth to confer on ongoing campaigns, flanked by armaments and the grand insignias of rank. Only soldiers who have climbed the Alliance hierarchy to achieve officer status—specifically the rank of Knight or higher—are permitted entry. Inside, military quartermasters supply battle-hardened soldiers with elite arms, armor, and mounts crafted specifically to turn the tide against the Horde in contested zones across the world.

Charred Vale. The Charred Vale is a smoldering valley in southwestern Stonetalon Mountains, devastated by the reckless deforestation and machinery of the Venture Company. Once a thriving haven for treants and chimaeras, it is now engulfed in flames, roving elementals, and hostile harpies. Not long ago, this southwest basin was a flourishing alpine wood guarded by majestic treants and inhabited by native chimaeras and harpies. Its ruin began with the arrival of the Venture Company. The greedy goblin outfit clear-cut the forest with explosive machinery, corrupting the guardians and awakening chaotic fire elementals. Though the treants eventually forced the goblins back, the land was left broken, scarred by fire, and tainted by whatever foul devices the retreating loggers deployed.

Chill Breeze Valley. Chill Breeze Valley is a rugged, snow-covered pass in western Dun Morogh linking the dwarven settlement of Kharanos with the embattled city of Gnomeregan. While its main path is a well-traveled thoroughfare for young travelers and refugees, its secluded recesses harbor dangerous beasts and bloody dens. Chill Breeze Valley forms a T-shaped trench through the mountains of western Dun Morogh. The main east-west trail sees steady foot traffic from novice dwarves and gnomes journeying between Kharanos and the outskirts of Gnomeregan. However, straying into the valley's north-south offshoot is another matter entirely. Strewn with bloodstains and mangled carcasses, these shadowy reaches harbor ferocious predators—most notably savage wendigos that lair in deep ice caves and prey on anyone reckless enough to wander into their hunting grounds.

Clean Zone. The Clean Zone is a fortified, decontamination enclave nestled inside the ruined city of Gnomeregan just past the upper Hall of Gears. It serves as the sole safe haven within the irradiated facility where uncorrupted gnomish forces hold ground against surrounding troggs and leper gnomes. Here, field medics, technicians, and specialized Sparklematic machines offer respite and salvage operations amid the radioactive ruins. While most of Gnomeregan succumbed to Mekkatorque's disastrous venting of radioactive waste, the Clean Zone remains untainted. Positioned strategically between the trogg-infested Dormitory below and the contested corridors of the Hall of Gears above, it acts as a fortified forward base. Resolute gnome defenders, technicians, and field medics hold the barricades day and night, ensuring Alliance expeditions have a stable staging ground to regroup, mend wounds, and maintain machinery.

Cleft. The Cleft is a darkened hollow located northwest of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a tranquil corner of the boughs, it has been claimed by the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs, who use it as a stronghold to ambush travelers moving along the main highway toward Darnassus. Situated off the highway between Dolanaar and Darnassus, the Cleft has turned into one of the most perilous dens on the world tree. Driven mad by the foul taint spreading through Teldrassil, the resident Gnarlpine furbolgs have fortified this hollow. From this redoubt, the maddened beasts terrorize the local roads, threatening to cut Dolanaar off from the capital.

Cleft of Shadow. Tucked deep within the subterranean caverns beneath Orgrimmar, the Cleft of Shadow houses the city's practitioners of stealth, sorcery, and demonology. Far from the proud warrior ethos of Thrall's upper districts, it serves as a necessary haven for rogues, warlocks, and mages operating in the shadows of the Horde. While Thrall's new Horde champions honor, shamanism, and strength of arms, practical leadership demands a place for subtler arts. Carved into the damp stone caverns below the capital, the Cleft of Shadow hosts the Shadowswift Brotherhood of rogues, the Darkfire Enclave of warlocks, and the scholars of the Arcane Enclave. Kept away from the everyday bustle of the valley districts, this dark quarter allows practitioners of poison, fel energy, and arcane magic to ply their trades out of direct public view while remaining under the watchful eye of Orgrimmar's leadership.

Cliffspring Falls. Cliffspring Falls marks the dramatic origin of Darkshore's vital Cliffspring River, tumbling down from the eastern cliffs into the coastal forest. Long celebrated as the principal source of clean drinking water for the region, its waters have recently fallen victim to a foul, spreading taint. The subterranean cavern feeding the waterfall has become infested with hostile naga and shadowy Twilight's Hammer cultists. Pouring out from caverns perched high in the rocky bluffs along Darkshore's eastern border, Cliffspring Falls feeds the Cliffspring River, which winds westward across the woods to empty into the sea. Traditionally, this cascade provided the purest drinking water for local night elf settlements. In recent times, however, the waters have turned foul and murky, spreading sickness and ecological decay throughout the river basin. Investigating naturalists have discovered that the cave network at the falls' headwaters is overrun by vile naga and dark cultists, who plot in the shadows while demonic corruption from neighboring Felwood threatens to seep through the highland bedrock.

Cold Hearth Manor. Cold Hearth Manor is a blighted farmstead located just west of Brill along the main road of Tirisfal Glades. Once a bustling, hospitable estate known for bountiful crops, the outbreak of the Plague of Undeath wiped out its residents, leaving the surrounding fields choked with mindless Scourge. Today, the Forsaken have secured the main farmhouse as an outpost and waystation for travelers. Before the Third War, this homestead bore a reputation for warmth and hospitality, supporting rich harvests in the heart of Lordaeron. When the Plague swept through the kingdom, the entire family and their laborers succumbed, rising again as husks bound to the Scourge. While feral undead still stumble through the ruined fields, Forsaken forces managed to push the mindless dead out of the main farmhouse, reclaiming the structure to serve as a trading post and foothold along the road toward the eastern glades.

Coldridge Pass. Coldridge Pass is a rugged, snowbound tunnel cutting through the southern mountain ridge of Dun Morogh. It serves as the sole overland route connecting the secluded training grounds of Coldridge Valley to the rest of the kingdom, emerging near the bustling town of Kharanos. Because hostile troggs have overrun the passage, any traveler attempting the journey must either fight their way through or make a desperate dash for the other side. For young dwarven recruits and gnome novices taking their first steps beyond Coldridge Valley, Coldridge Pass is a harsh rite of passage. Chiseled straight through the rock, this tunnel forms the primary link sending newly trained adventurers eastward toward the frontier hub of Kharanos. What was once a secure mountain corridor has become a perilous choke point, infested with aggressive troggs that have pushed up from dark sub-terrains to menace any soul trying to travel between the sheltered valley and the wider reaches of Dun Morogh.

Coldridge Valley. Coldridge Valley is a sheltered, snow-covered vale tucked into the southwestern heights of Dun Morogh. Centered around the hamlet of Anvilmar, it serves as the training ground where young dwarves and gnome refugees first take up arms in service of Ironforge. A single tunnel, Coldridge Pass, connects this secluded hollow to the wider mountain realm. Cradled by sheer mountain cliffs, Coldridge Valley remains largely cut off from the bustling trade routes of Dun Morogh. At its heart sits Anvilmar, a sturdy stone hall and hamlet where veteran dwarven instructors and displaced gnome scholars train fresh recruits in the arts of battle, stealth, and sorcery. Outside the warmth of Anvilmar's hearths, the valley floor is carpeted in thick snow and prowled by boars and hungry winter wolves, providing novices with their first real taste of frontier survival.

How do you leave Coldridge Valley? The only overland route out of the valley leads through Coldridge Pass, a snowy tunnel cutting northeast through the mountain ridge. Once through the pass, the road heads east directly toward the town of Kharanos and onward to the great gates of Ironforge.

Why are gnomes starting here alongside dwarves? Following the tragic fall of Gnomeregan to troggs and radioactive fallout, surviving gnomes fled into Dun Morogh as refugees. High Tinker Mekkatorque's people were welcomed by King Magni Bronzebeard, leading many exiled gnomish apprentices to train side by side with young dwarves in Anvilmar.

What threats are troubling the valley? The valley faces two major menaces: the hostile Frostmane trolls, who resent dwarven settlements on their mountain territory, and crude Rockjaw troggs, who have clawed up from the deep earth to choke Coldridge Pass. Local predators like wolves and boars also harass unwary travelers.

What is Anvilmar? Anvilmar is the central fortress-lodge and settlement within Coldridge Valley. It houses class trainers, forge-masters, and local mountaineer officers who coordinate the defense of the valley and prepare newly forged adventurers for the wider world.

Command Center. The Command Center, often referred to as the Stormwind Barracks, stands in the heart of Old Town as the operational headquarters for the city's military officers. In peacetime, it houses the standing army, but with Stormwind's forces dispatched to distant frontiers, it currently operates with a seasoned skeleton crew focused on drilling recruits and local militia. Situated within the weathered streets of Old Town, the Command Center serves as the primary garrison and martial training ground for the kingdom of Stormwind. Normally packed with regular infantry and ranking officers, the facility is uncharacteristically sparse. With much of the royal army committed to campaigns abroad, the barracks relies on a veteran cadre of instructors—including Ander Germaine and martial artist Wu Shen—to train fresh warriors, while figures like Wulf Hansreim drill marksmen to bolster the city's defenses.

Commons. The Commons serves as the vibrant commercial heart of Ironforge, connecting the city entrance directly to its vast caverns. Teeming with merchants, travelers, and bankers, it is the busiest thoroughfare in the dwarven capital and the central marketplace for the entire Alliance. Located just northeast of the Gates of Ironforge, the Commons is the first district that greets travelers entering the mountain kingdom. Carved directly out of the stone, this bustling market street houses the primary Alliance Auction House, the Stonefire Tavern, and the city's central bank within the Vault of Ironforge. Broad avenues connect it seamlessly to the Great Forge, the Mystic Ward, and the Military Ward, ensuring that nearly all foot traffic in the mountain passes through its bustling storefronts.

Craftsmen's Terrace. The Craftsmen's Terrace is the bustling artisan district situated in the northern reaches of Darnassus. It serves as the primary trade and manufacturing hub for the night elf capital, housing workshops, profession trainers, and a lively inn. The district also hosts external representatives, including an embassy for the neutral Argent Dawn. Spanning the northern edge of the canopy city, the Craftsmen's Terrace gathers the diverse trades that keep Darnassus running. Woodworkers, leathercrafters, alchemists, and other artisans operate their shops here, integrating classic night elven methods with practical craft. The district also provides essential community amenities, including an inn, a guild master, and guild petition vendors. Bridges connect the terrace directly to the Cenarion Enclave to the west and the Warrior's Terrace to the south.

Crag of the Everliving. The Crag of the Everliving is a verdant cavern chamber nestled deep within the Wailing Caverns. Dominated by lush, corrupted flora and predatory plant creatures, it serves as the domain of the Fanglord Lord Pythas. Its towering upper reaches shelter the ancient entity after whom the crag is named. While much of the Wailing Caverns is carved of damp subterranean stone, the Crag of the Everliving bursts with unruly, twisted vegetation fueled by the Nightmare corrupting Naralex's slumber. Towering mossy platforms and winding paths are choked with Deviate Shamblers—living plant hulks prowling the undergrowth. Lord Pythas, one of Naralex's fallen disciples, watches over the crag's central reaches, having traded his noble druidic vows for the venomous rites of the Druids of the Fang.

Cragpool Lake. Cragpool Lake is a body of water tucked inside Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. Looming above its dark waters sits a massive timber structure erected by the Venture Company, while the depths below harbor a notoriously aggressive beast. Nestled deep within Windshear Crag, Cragpool Lake lies directly beneath the towering logging apparatus built by the Venture Company. An enormous wooden structure spans above the water, once serving as the prime vantage point from which Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle commanded clear-cutting operations across the mountain valley. While much of the syndicate has scaled back their presence in the crag, holdouts and sentries linger across the catwalks and platforms overhead. Down below, the lake has been declared strictly off-limits by the goblins due to the arrival of Cragjaw, a massive and predatory fish prowling the murky water beneath the gears.

Crossroads. The Crossroads is the beating heart of Horde travel through central Kalimdor, situated where the north-south Gold Road intersects the path from Ratchet to the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as a bustling trading outpost, military staging area, and transit hub for travelers journeying between Durotar, Mulgore, and northern frontlines. True to its name, the Crossroads sits squarely at the crossing of the Gold Road and the east-west route cutting from the goblin port of Ratchet into the Stonetalon Mountains. Despite having modest lodgings, the outpost functions as a bustling regional hub. Wind rider masters, merchants, blacksmiths, and trainers maintain permanent setups beneath its watchtowers. For young warriors traveling out from Durotar or Mulgore, the settlement is often the first place they witness the vast, multi-front logistics binding the new Horde together.

Crusader Outpost. Crusader Outpost is a fortified watchtower perched atop the rugged hills of eastern Tirisfal Glades. Manned by zealous members of the Scarlet Crusade, it guards the approaches leading toward their stronghold at the Scarlet Monastery. From this height, Crusaders observe travel along the road and stand ready to repel any Forsaken incursion. Built into the bluffs overlooking the eastern road, the Crusader Outpost serves as a primary early-warning station for the Scarlet Crusade. From their elevated tower, sentries watch over movement between Brill and the eastern reaches of Lordaeron, ensuring that wandering undead or scouting parties are spotted long before reaching the Monastery gates. The tower also grants the garrison tactical flanking capability against any force seeking to march up the valley toward their holy bastion.

Crusader's Outpost. Crusader's Outpost is a fortified scout tower manned by the Scarlet Crusade in western Tirisfal Glades. Situated adjacent to the Solliden Farmstead, it serves as the Crusade's westernmost position in all of Lordaeron. Its perilous distance from the main Scarlet bastions leaves its garrison isolated in the heart of hostile Forsaken territory. Perched inside the western Tirisfal hills just west of Deathknell, this stone tower represents the farthest reach of the Scarlet Crusade's power in Lordaeron. The garrison stationed here works in tandem with the surviving human laborers of the nearby Solliden Farmstead, attempting to hold back the encroaching undead. From the top of the tower, lookouts keep watch over the surrounding pumpkin fields and forest paths, vigilant against both roaming Scourge fiends and patrols from the Undercity.

Crystal Lake. Crystal Lake is a body of water lying just east of Goldshire in the heart of Elwynn Forest. While once a peaceful spot, its shores have been overrun by aggressive murlocs, turning it into a frequent hazard for local villagers and passing travelers. Situated within walking distance of Lion's Pride Inn, Crystal Lake should be an idyllic rural retreat, but it is plagued by dangerous wildlife. Tribes of freshwater murlocs have claimed the shoreline and shallow shoals, attacking anyone who strays too close. Local alchemist William Pestle frequently hires passing adventurers to venture to the water's edge, directing them to defeat the creatures and harvest the crystal kelp they carry for use in his experimental concoctions.

Cut-Throat Alley. Cut-Throat Alley is a secluded, unpopulated back corner of Stormwind City hidden away behind the canal shops. Tucked behind a storefront called the Shady Lady near the Dwarven District border, it consists of a quiet courtyard and an empty residence cut off from normal city foot traffic. Cut-Throat Alley is one of Stormwind's quietest and most secretive corners. Though technically charted alongside the Dwarven District, it shares none of the district's roaring forge fires or heavy soot. The alley cannot be reached from any of the city's main avenues; the only foot path leads straight through the Shady Lady, a small shop lining the canals just south of the bridge from Cathedral Square. Beyond the shop door lies a small paved dead-end lined with stacked crates, forgotten barrels, and a single unoccupied two-story residence. Completely hidden from passing guards and ordinary citizens, it sits entirely silent amidst the bustle of the capital.

Dagger Hills. The Dagger Hills form a rugged ridge rising across southern Westfall, directly behind the blighted town of Moonbrook. Long neglected by the crown, this rocky highland serves as a hostile hideout for cutthroats, bandits, and creeping terrors that threaten the surrounding plains. Rising high above the dilapidated settlement of Moonbrook, the Dagger Hills mark the jagged southern reaches of Westfall. Stripped of official royal patrols from Stormwind, this arid highland has become a natural fortification for the Defias Brotherhood. Knuckledusters, pathstalkers, and highwaymen lurk among the rocky crests and scrub, ambushing unwary travelers and keeping watch over the approaches to their strongholds below.

Darkcloud Pinnacle. Darkcloud Pinnacle is a fortified tauren settlement perched atop several interconnected mesas east of the Great Lift in Thousand Needles. Held by the aggressive Grimtotem clan, the aerial stronghold serves as a base of operations for regional disruption and shady dealings. Spanning three main mesas joined by rope bridges, Darkcloud Pinnacle commands the canyon basin below. The heights are accessible only by a steep natural slope leading from the canyon floor across wooden bridges, or via a high crossing near Razorfen Downs. From these windswept rocks, the Grimtotem watch the valley, safe from casual assault and isolated from the broader tauren tribes.

Darkened Bank. The Darkened Bank is the northern shoreline of Duskwood, bordering the river that separates the shadowed woods from Elwynn Forest. Stretching from the far west all the way east toward the Redridge Mountains, it marks the boundary between the relative safety of the north and the dark terrors of the forest. Running along the southern bank of the river opposite Elwynn Forest, the Darkened Bank forms the northern edge of Duskwood. It extends from the western riverbends east toward the stone span leading to the Redridge Mountains. While visually gloomy under the pervasive canopy of Duskwood's curse, this shoreline is often the first foothold for travelers venturing south from Elwynn. Near its far western tip sits a makeshift campsite where displaced refugees, including Sven Yorgen and Lars, have taken shelter just barely outside the grasp of the deep woods.

Darkshire. Darkshire, formerly known as Grand Hamlet, is a battered settlement in eastern Duskwood. Cloaked in an enduring, unnatural gloom and neglected by Stormwind, the town survives only through the vigilance of the Night Watch and the stubborn endurance of its people. Once a peaceful woodland settlement called Grand Hamlet, the village was razed by the Old Horde during the First War and later rebuilt. Its fortune turned truly bitter following the fall of Medivh at Karazhan, whose lingering death throes cursed Brightwood into the shadowy wilderness now called Duskwood. Despite being a nominal holding of the Kingdom of Stormwind, the town hall receives virtually no aid from the crown. Political paralysis in Stormwind City has left the garrison unstaffed and the borders unpatrolled, forcing Mayor Ello Ebonlocke and the local council to administer their own harsh, insular justice in the shadows.

Darkshire Town Hall. Darkshire Town Hall stands on the western edge of the town square as the seat of local governance in Duskwood. From inside these dimly lit halls, Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke and his council attempt to administer a settlement besieged by creeping darkness and undead monstrosities. Located directly west of the main town square, the Town Hall is where Darkshire's civic leadership gathers to govern an increasingly isolated territory. Within its weathered walls sits Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke, struggling to preserve civil order and protect the populace while Stormwind offers little in the way of military aid. Alongside the mayor, municipal officials like Clerk Daltry work to track local records and the travelers braving Duskwood's dangerous roads, though keeping ledgers current is a grim and challenging task in such perilous times.

Darkspear Strand. Darkspear Strand is the stretch of coastline in southern Durotar where the Darkspear trolls washed ashore following their exile from the Echo Isles. Located directly beside Sen'jin Village, this beach marks the bitter beginning of the tribe's mainland refuge under Vol'jin's leadership. When the witch doctor Zalazane went mad and seized control of the Echo Isles, the surviving Darkspear trolls were forced to abandon their offshore home. Desperate refugees crossed the narrow waters and landed along this sun-bleached coast. Rather than scatter into the hostile red wastes of Durotar, the survivors banded together just yards inland from the shoreline to construct Sen'jin Village. Today, the strand serves as a quiet reminder of their displacement, looking out across the surf toward the islands they still hope to reclaim.

Dawning Isles. The Dawning Isles are a cluster of low-lying islets situated within Lordamere Lake along the eastern edge of Silverpine Forest. Once idyllic retreats, they have succumbed to the blight of the Plague of Undeath and are overrun by aggressive murlocs. Before the Third War, the Dawning Isles were known as scenic keys resting on the calm, clear waters of Lordamere Lake. When the Plague of Undeath swept across Lordaeron, corruption seeped into the lake's shallows. The vegetation turned pallid and rotting, driving away idyllic peacefulness. Today, the Vile Fin murloc tribe dominates the muddy shores and tangled brush, aggressively defending their burgeoning colonies from anyone seeking to traverse the lake.

Dawning Wood Catacombs. Carved deep beneath Raven Hill Cemetery, the Dawning Wood Catacombs are a dark labyrinth teeming with the fiercest undead in Duskwood. Those who brave the subterranean tunnels face entrenched swarms of skeletal guardians and flesh-eating ghouls. Long before the twilight curse settled over the forest, the Dawning Wood Catacombs served as a grand resting place for the honored dead of Grand Hamlets and the surrounding homesteads. Now buried beneath the ruined Raven Hill Cemetery, these dark stone corridors hold the most lethal undead in the region. The catacombs feature two distinct subterranean wings: the western passages are held by ranks of animated skeletons guarding ancestral tombs, while the eastern passages descend into a foul warren overrun by ravenous, disease-bearing ghouls. Lone travelers rarely survive deep within their depths.

Dead Acre. The Dead Acre is a ruined, smoldering farmstead in southeastern Westfall near the river bridge to Duskwood. Burned to ash by the Defias Brotherhood during their uprising across the countryside, the blackened fields are now abandoned by people and stalked by rogue harvest golems. Situated just north of the road linking Sentinel Hill to Duskwood, the Dead Acre was once a productive homestead among the breadbasket farms of Westfall. When the Defias Brotherhood rose in revolt and drove out the local landowners, this farm met a violent end. The homestead and its surrounding crops were put to the torch, leaving behind scorched timber, smoking earth, and wandering mechanical Harvest Watchers that still reap the barren soil.

Dead Field. The Dead Field is a blighted, abandoned farmstead situated in northern Silverpine Forest.
