Once quiet rural farmland, it has been seized by the Rot Hide gnolls and transformed into a forward staging ground for Scourge forces. Repeated Forsaken attempts to clear the area have faltered under the command of the banshee Nightlash. Little remains of the original farmstead in the northern reaches of Silverpine Forest, its previous living occupants long lost to the Third War. Today, the ruined plot serves as a base of operations for the Rot Hide gnolls, who act as willing servants to the Scourge. As their numbers swelled, Deathstalker scouts passing through the region noted signs of imminent military mobilization threatening Forsaken supply lines and outposts. Small Forsaken assaults against the farm have repeatedly failed, turned back by the wailing apparition Nightlash—a banshee who manifests whenever her gnoll thralls are endangered.

Deadeye Shore. Deadeye Shore is a windswept stretch of coastline along Durotar's eastern edge, directly east of Drygulch Ravine. Named in memory of the legendary Bleeding Hollow chieftain Kilrogg Deadeye, the barren sands are roamed primarily by wild raptors, scorpids, and feral boars. Stretching beneath the red bluffs of central Durotar, Deadeye Shore takes its name from Kilrogg Deadeye, the one-eyed chieftain of the Bleeding Hollow clan who fought in the First and Second Wars. From high above, the sand and rocky outcrops faintly mirror the shape of a skull with a missing eye socket. While lacking major settlements or military outposts, the shoreline is far from peaceful: aggressive wildlife dominates the sands, and shadowy cultists from the Burning Blade have been known to prowl down toward the water from their nearby hideouts in the ravines.

Deathknell. Deathknell is a fortified village nestled in a secluded valley in southwestern Tirisfal Glades. It serves as the primary awakening grounds for newly freed undead breaking free from the Lich King's grasp to join the Forsaken. Besieged by mindless Scourge remnants, local zealots, and aggressive wildlife, the settlement is a harsh proving ground for those claiming a place in Sylvanas Windrunner's kingdom. Tucked away behind jagged hills just north of the Silverpine border, Deathknell is where newly awakened undead first open their eyes to their bleak reality. Unlike most settlements in Tirisfal Glades that preserved their human names from the fallen Kingdom of Lordaeron, Deathknell was explicitly renamed by the undead who claimed it. The town itself is cleaved in two: the Forsaken cling stubbornly to the southern grounds around the old church, while the northern half—including the village forge—remains overrun by mindless Scourge zombies and feral ghouls. Elite Deathguards keep the narrow gorge out of the valley securely sealed against intruders, allowing local caretakers to induct new arrivals into the Banshee Queen's service.

Why was the town renamed Deathknell? Deathknell was renamed after it became an undead settlement, unlike most communities in Tirisfal that retained their human names. The reason for the new name is unknown.

Why is the northern half of the town overrun by undead? Not every corpse raised in the wake of the Third War broke free with their minds intact. The northern village square and forge are infested by the 'Mindless Ones'—feral zombies, ghouls, and skeletons still driven by the residual, lingering will of the Scourge. Forsaken defenders regularly clear them out to salvage equipment and defend the church.

What is the Scarlet Crusade doing near Deathknell? A detachment of the Scarlet Crusade maintains an encampment in the hills southeast of the village. Fanatically dedicated to destroying all undead indiscriminately, they monitor the pass, ambush newly awakened Forsaken, and exchange scouting intelligence with Scarlet strongholds elsewhere in Lordaeron.

Why can't the Forsaken use the local gold mine? Night Web's Hollow, the gold mine situated in the cliffs northwest of the village, is completely overrun by aggressive spiders. Securing natural resources like gold is critical for the Forsaken war effort, but until the infestation is cleared, the settlement cannot exploit the vein.

Decrepit Ferry. The Decrepit Ferry is a ruined dock on the eastern shore of Silverpine Forest that once provided passage across Lordamere Lake to Fenris Isle. Following the fall of Lordaeron, the ferry was destroyed, its operator murdered, and the shoreline overrun by undead and vicious Rot Hide gnolls. Before the Third War, this dock bustled with daily traffic across Lordamere Lake. Local farmers brought fresh produce down to the water, selling their crops directly to the wealthy lord of Fenris Isle and his household. For a modest fee, the ferryman carried trade goods, messengers, and visiting nobles back and forth between the mainland and the keep. That peaceful commerce ended abruptly when the Scourge swept through the kingdom. The ferryman was brutally killed, the boats were smashed, and the pier fell into decay.

Deep Elem Mine. Deep Elem Mine is an excavation site nestled in the heart of Silverpine Forest. Once an active operation, it was overrun when Archmage Arugal's dark magic swept through the region, transforming its miners into savage worgen. Situated central to Silverpine Forest, the Deep Elem Mine once served the living inhabitants of Lordaeron as an ordinary resource vein. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the lupine nightmare upon the forest, his feral curse spread deep into the tunnels. The laborers inside succumbed to the affliction, turning into vicious worgen who abandoned their pickaxes to claim the cavern as a predatory lair.

Deeprun Tram. The Deeprun Tram is an subterranean marvel of gnomish engineering linking the Alliance capitals of Ironforge and Stormwind City. Commissioned by King Magni Bronzebeard following the Second War, it allows citizens and soldiers to cross vast distances beneath the earth in mere minutes. The enclosed twin tracks cut beneath mountain and lake, serving as a vital artery for Alliance military support and commerce. Following the devastation of the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard grew increasingly frustrated with how slowly dwarven aid and construction supplies reached Stormwind across the mountain passes. To solve the logistical hurdle and guarantee that dwarven soldiers could rapidly reinforce the human capital in times of crisis, Magni turned to High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque. The master gnomish engineer drafted designs for an enclosed underground railway powered by cutting-edge technology. Despite excavation complications—including cutting right through a vast subterranean lake and battling relentless infestations of underground rats—the tram became a crowning achievement of the Alliance, moving thousands of travelers free of charge between Ironforge and Stormwind.

Deepwater Tavern. The Deepwater Tavern is the bustling seaside inn of Menethil Harbor, nestled in the damp marshlands of the Wetlands. It serves as the primary meeting spot, resupply point, and resting place for travelers and mariners navigating the busy port town. Between hearty drinks and harbor rumors, patrons frequently find work or run into volatile tavern brawls. Standing within the sodden streets of Menethil Harbor, the Deepwater Tavern offers travelers a welcome shelter from the perpetually drizzly, treacherous marshlands outside. Sailors, dockworkers, merchants, and weary adventurers gather beneath its timber beams to trade news, share a warm fire, and patch their wounds. Beyond the usual amenities of a harbor inn, it houses a resident first aid trainer and local merchants catering to those bound for the perils of the marsh or embarking across the Great Sea. The atmosphere is boisterous and occasionally hazardous; disputes flare up quickly over spilled ale, with notorious troublemakers like Tapoke 'Slim' Jahn known to spark the occasional tavern-wide brawl.

Defias Hideout. The Defias Hideout is an unassuming, derelict house situated on the southern edge of Moonbrook. Though it blends in with the surrounding ruined settlement, its upper floor conceals the primary overland entrance into the extensive subterranean network of the Deadmines. To the casual eye, the Defias Hideout looks like any other ransacked manor or farmhouse in Moonbrook, overrun by destitute vagrants and Defias thugs. However, its modest interior masks the nerve center of Edwin VanCleef's southern operations. Ascending to the upper floor reveals an opening that leads directly down into the sprawling labyrinth of the Deadmines. Because the Brotherhood focuses its manpower on guarding the perimeter of Moonbrook and laboring deep underground, the hideout itself is sparsely garrisoned, functioning more as a heavily monitored bottleneck than an active stronghold.

Demon Fall Canyon. Demon Fall Canyon is a scarred, fel-corrupted gorge situated in southern Ashenvale. It marks the legendary battleground where Grommash Hellscream and Thrall confronted the pit lord Mannoroth, ending the demonic blood curse that had enslaved the orcish race for a generation. Carved into the rugged southern borders of Ashenvale near Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Ridge, this canyon bears the heavy scars of the Third War. It was here that Warchief Thrall and chieftain Grommash Hellscream tracked down the pit lord Mannoroth to break his hold over the Horde. During the fierce duel, Mannoroth incapacitated Thrall, but Grom seized the opening to drive his axe, Gorehowl, straight into the demon's chest. The resulting infernal explosion shattered the pit lord and slew Grom as well, permanently liberating the orcs from their lingering demonic servitude.

Demon Fall Ridge. Demon Fall Ridge is a blighted highland in south-eastern Ashenvale, overlooking the canyon where Mannoroth fell. Swarming with lesser demons and corrupting magic, the ridge centers around a desecrated night elf barrow den claimed by the Burning Legion. Rising directly west and above Demon Fall Canyon, Demon Fall Ridge is stained with lingering fel residue from the Third War. While the canyon below marks the site of the catastrophic clash between Grommash Hellscream and the pit lord Mannoroth, this high ground serves as a staging area for surviving demonic invaders. Lesser demons patrol the rocky cliffs, defiling the ancient woodland and threatening any travelers traversing the southern border of Ashenvale.

Demont's Place. Demont's Place is a ruined homestead nestled in southwestern Westfall, just west of the forsaken town of Moonbrook. Once a working agricultural plot, the farm was driven to ruin alongside the rest of the region and claimed by the rogue agents of the Defias Brotherhood. Today, its weathered fences and empty fields stand as another casualty of the realm's fading prosperity. Situated within sight of Moonbrook and the rotting expanse of the Dead Acre, Demont's Place was once among the private family holdings feeding the Kingdom of Stormwind. Economic collapse and the sudden rise of outlaw brigands stripped the farm of its livelihood, forcing out its original caretakers. Much like its neighboring fields, the plot has degenerated into a rough hideout, overrun by outlaws using its weathered grounds as an extension of the Defias stronghold in Moonbrook.

Dolanaar. Dolanaar is a tranquil night elf settlement nestled in the central-eastern boughs of Teldrassil. Situated just southwest of Shadowglen, it serves as the first true town young kal'dorei encounter after departing their sheltered training grounds. Here, rangers, druids, and craftsmen gather to guide newcomers and address the strange, encroaching afflictions disturbing the World Tree. Resting beneath the lush canopy southwest of Shadowglen, Dolanaar serves as a vital crossway for travelers traversing Teldrassil. Built in the traditional night elven manner, its homes and platforms sit seamlessly woven into the woodland. The village provides newcomers with their first comprehensive training in trades, martial arts, and nature crafts, and sits on the road to the capital city of Darnassus. Because of its central location, reports of corrupted wildlife, aggressive furbolgs, and foul mosses from the surrounding boughs inevitably find their way into Dolanaar's council.

Dor'Danil Barrow Den. Dor'Danil Barrow Den is an ancient night elven sanctuary carved into the earth of central Ashenvale, south of Splintertree Post. Once a tranquil resting place for slumbering druids commune with the Emerald Dream, it has fallen into horror following Forsaken meddling that severed the dreamers' spirits from their bodies. Barrow dens across Kalimdor are revered sanctuaries where night elven druids historically slept for centuries, roaming the Emerald Dream while their mortal frames remained protected underground. When the Horde pushed into Ashenvale, Dor'Danil fell deep behind enemy lines. The orcs largely ignored the comatose elves, but the newly allied Forsaken saw an opportunity. Forsaken operatives infiltrated the depths and began gruesome experiments designed to sever the sleeping druids from their spirits, fracturing their minds and driving them hopelessly insane. The darkened hollows now crawl with sinister Forsaken assassins and the furious, torment-maddened spirits of druids who can no longer return to their bodies.

Dormitory. The Dormitory is a residential sector within the fallen technological capital of Gnomeregan. Once providing living quarters for countless gnome citizens, it now lies choked with radioactive fallout and crawls with savage, irradiated troggs. Situated just past the decontamination chambers of the Clean Zone, the Dormitory formerly housed the inventors, laborers, and families of Gnomeregan. When High Tinker Mekkatorque initiated the emergency radiation venting to combat the invading trogg horde, this densely populated sector became a trap. Today, its communal halls and living units are completely abandoned by gnomish life, occupied instead by mutated troggs that thrive in the radioactive miasma. Travelers descending toward the lower levels of the city must fight through this tragic reminder of the catastrophe to reach the lower Hall of Gears.

Drag. The Drag is a bustling, shaded thoroughfare carved into the red rock of Orgrimmar, linking the Valley of Strength to the Valley of Honor and the Valley of Wisdom. Known throughout Durotar as the heart of the capital's commerce, its canyon walls are lined with crafters, traders, and artisans. It also conceals the cavernous descent into the notorious Cleft of Shadow. Tucked deep between the red canyon walls of Orgrimmar, the Drag serves as the commercial backbone of the Horde's capital. While the Valley of Strength focuses on military muster and administrative command, the Drag is where daily city life unfolds. Shaded under high cliffs and hides, the street is thick with the smells of tanning vats, bubbling alchemical cauldrons, and the clatter of tinkerers' gears. Craftsmen of almost every discipline gather here to practice their trades and teach aspiring adventurers, from leatherworking and tailoring to goblin-led engineering workshops like Nogg's Machine Shop.

Dreadmist Den. Dreadmist Den is a subterranean cavern carved beneath the crags of Dreadmist Peak in the northern Barrens. Controlled by the Burning Blade cult, the cavern is perpetually smothered in an unnerving red haze and serves as a shrine to demon worship. Dreadmist Den lies tucked within the jagged slopes of Dreadmist Peak, serving as a dark sanctuary for the Burning Blade cultists. Inside, the air hangs heavy with a thick, crimson vapor that blankets the cavern in an eerie twilight. Far from the watchful eyes of the Horde in the plains below, the cult conducts foul demonic rites within these stone tunnels, guarding their blasphemous relics and plotting to spread their corruption across Kalimdor.

Dreadmist Peak. Dreadmist Peak is a jagged, desolate mountain looming northwest of the Crossroads in the Barrens. Shrouded in an unnatural, crimson miasma, the peak serves as a secluded redoubt for the demonic cultists of the Burning Blade. Rising high above the arid savannas of the Barrens, Dreadmist Peak stands out as a site of palpable evil. As travelers wind their way up the crags, the bright sky is blotted out by a dense, reddish haze—the residual miasma of an ancient demonic curse. At the mountain's crest and within its subterranean hollows, the Burning Blade cult operates in secret, harboring warlocks, toxicologists, and fiendish grellkin. From this vantage, the cultists spread poisons into the nearby water table and scheme against the nascent powers establishing control over central Kalimdor.

Dreamer's Rock. Dreamer's Rock is a secluded natural sanctuary tucked deep within the Wailing Caverns past the Screaming Gully. Here lies the sleeping night elf druid Naralex, whose noble effort to revive the Barrens has instead birthed a living nightmare. It serves as both a sacred barrow chamber and the epicenter of the corruption mutating the surrounding subterranean ecosystem. Located in the heart of the Wailing Caverns, Dreamer's Rock functions much like an improvised barrow den. Here, the night elf druid Naralex entered a deep trance to tap the underground springs and channel the Emerald Dream into the arid soil of the Barrens. Instead of bringing life, his connection was seized by dark forces. The nightmare twisting his thoughts now spills physically into this chamber, twisting the local wildlife, turning his followers into the venomous Druids of the Fang, and manifesting terrifying aberrations into the waking world.

Dry Hills. The Dry Hills form the rugged northwestern corner of the Barrens, nestled against the foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains. Contrary to their name, these uplands are noticeably greener than the arid plains below, though they are notoriously dangerous due to the aggressive Witchwing harpies roosting along their crags. Tucked away where the arid plains rise toward the Stonetalon Mountains, the Dry Hills are somewhat of a misnomer, possessing far more verdant brush and shrubbery than the sun-bleached savannas to the south. Yet this lush foothill region offers little safety for travelers. The bluffs are dominated by the Witchwing harpies, led by the matriarch Serena Bloodfeather. From these heights, their raiding parties sweep down to prey on supply caravans using the northern stretch of the Gold Road, leaving abandoned orcish fortifications and derelict siege engines rotting in the brush.

Drygulch Ravine. Drygulch Ravine is a rugged, hidden gorge tucked into the rocky bluffs of eastern Durotar. Accessible only through an obscure cave passage from Razorwind Canyon or a perilous drop from above, this craggy trench is overrun by nesting Dustwind harpies who menace nearby supply caravans. Carved deep into the crags east of Orgrimmar, Drygulch Ravine is almost entirely cut off from casual travel. Its only ground-level access is a cramped natural tunnel connected to Razorwind Canyon. Fed by a modest river, this sheltered depression once saw peaceful orc habitation, but wild beasts and roosting Dustwind harpies have turned it into a lawless pocket of Durotar. The winged scavengers use the steep cliff faces to nest their broods and stockpile stolen goods taken from Horde supply trains passing along the regional trails.

Dun Algaz. Dun Algaz is the fortified mountain pass and network of tunnels connecting Loch Modan to the Wetlands. Historically contested during the Second War, this vital trade artery has recently fallen under siege by Dragonmaw orcs, cutting off easy transit between Ironforge's territories and Menethil Harbor. Dun Algaz predates the War of the Three Hammers, originally serving as the passage the Wildhammer clan used to migrate north after being driven out of Ironforge. Carved deep into the jagged peaks separating Loch Modan and the Wetlands, the pass consists of sweeping stone tunnels, bastions, and watchposts. Its strategic value cannot be overstated: whoever holds Dun Algaz commands the only overland highway linking the dwarven heartlands to the western sea at Menethil Harbor.

Dun Garok. Dun Garok is a fortified dwarven mountain bastion situated in the southeastern heights of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Commanded by Captain Ironhill, the outpost's stalwart garrison defends regional Alliance interests and nearby operations like the Azurelode Mine against hostile encroachment. To the Forsaken of Tarren Mill, this entrenched dwarven stronghold stands as a constant military threat bordering their domain. Carved into the craggy southeastern hills of Hillsbrad Foothills, Dun Garok stands as a heavily defended redoubt of Ironforge mountaineers and riflemen. Commanded by Captain Ironhill, the dwarves here maintain a critical defensive perimeter, shielding human settlements in Hillsbrad and securing vital operations at the Azurelode Mine. Their sturdy stone architecture and deep entrenchments provide the Alliance with an anchor against nearby threats.

Dun Modr. Dun Modr is an ancient fortified dwarven town in northern Wetlands, guarding the southern approach to the Thandol Span. Once a critical fortress held and contested across multiple wars, it has recently fallen to a hostile force of Dark Iron dwarves. Situated at the northern edge of the Wetlands, Dun Modr commands the primary overland highway linking Khaz Modan with the northern human kingdoms. Because of this vital location, the stronghold has seen heavy bloodshed over the decades. During the Second War, the Orcish Horde captured and entrenched themselves within the dwarven fortress, using it as a forward staging ground to launch raids and repel Alliance armies. Stromgarde warriors launched a brutal amphibious assault from Tol Barad to reclaim it, only for the Orcs to strike back in a bloody tug-of-war. Alliance forces led by Lord Anduin Lothar ultimately drove the invaders south across the Thandol Span, restoring dwarven custody over the bastion.

Durnholde Keep. Durnholde Keep is a shattered fortress situated east of Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Once the nerve center of the Alliance's orc internment camps and the place where Warchief Thrall was raised as a captive gladiator, it now lies in ruin, occupied by outlaws of the Syndicate. Built by the Alliance, Durnholde served as the headquarters overseeing the southern internment camps following the Second War. Commanded by the ambitious and corrupt Lieutenant General Aedelas Blackmoore, it functioned as both an administrative fortress and a gladiatorial arena. It was here that Blackmoore raised the orphaned infant Go'el, naming him Thrall and training him to fight for sport and profit. Aided by Taretha Foxton, Thrall escaped captivity and later united the dispersed orc clans under the banner of the new Horde. Returning to Durnholde, Thrall laid siege to the fortress, slew Blackmoore, and called upon the earth spirits to shatter its walls.

Dust Plains. The Dust Plains form the dry, wind-scoured southern frontier of Westfall. Marked by arid ground and scarce scrub, the region is overrun by aggressive gnoll encampments and borders an old wizard's tower along its eastern rise. Stretching across southern Westfall, the Dust Plains mark the transition from troubled farmland to desolate wilderness. Unlike the plundered farmsteads to the north, this arid reach has long been surrendered to packs of feral gnolls who ambush travelers and challenge anyone venturing toward the coast or the nearby hills. On the eastern boundary sits Mortwake's Tower, a lonely magical retreat that offers no shelter from the beasts prowling the surrounding wastes.

Dustwind Cave. Dustwind Cave is a secluded hollow perched atop the cliffs of Razorwind Canyon, just northeast of Razor Hill. It serves as an active training ground and covert sanctuary for initiates of the nefarious Burning Blade cult operating within Durotar. Overlooking Razorwind Canyon, Dustwind Cave is one of the closest and most perilous threats to Razor Hill. While many assume demonic cultists gather only in deep subterranean depths, here the Burning Blade trains fresh recruits right under the noses of the Horde authorities. Shadowy cultists tutor initiates in forbidden dark magics and demonology, preparing them to undermine the young orcish realm from within Durotar's own borders.

Dwarven District. Tucked into the northern corner of Stormwind City, the Dwarven District is a bustling industrial enclave filled with roaring furnaces, ringing anvils, and thick smog. Established by Ironforge craftsmen who arrived to help rebuild the capital after the Second War, it serves as the beating mechanical heart of the city. Following the devastation of the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard sent hundreds of dwarven artisans, stonemasons, and engineers south to assist their human allies in rebuilding Stormwind. Rather than dispersing throughout the capital, they established their own enclave in the northern quarter. Today, the district retains the unmistakable character of Ironforge, dominated by heavy stone masonry, sprawling smelting operations, and bustling craft shops. Between the heat of Potts' Plates and the tavern chatter of The Golden Keg, the enclave provides a familiar haven for travelers from Khaz Modan. It also houses the Stormwind portal to the Deeprun Tram, tethering the human capital directly to Ironforge.

Eastvale Logging Camp. Eastvale Logging Camp is a vital lumber settlement tucked into the eastern woodlands of Elwynn Forest, near the border with the Redridge Mountains. The camp supplies vital timber to Stormwind and surrounding settlements, but its operations are constantly hampered by hungry predators prowling the surrounding forests. Orders for timber constantly stream into Eastvale Logging Camp from buyers across the Kingdom of Stormwind, but meeting these strict deadlines is a harrowing task. The dense wilderness surrounding the camp swarms with vicious wolves and prowling bears that routinely chase lumberjacks away from their worksites, leaving valuable cut timber abandoned in the woods. Under the direction of Supervisor Raelen, the camp frequently relies on wandering adventurers to cull the encroaching beasts and retrieve fallen wood before deliveries fall fatally behind schedule.

Echo Isles. The Echo Isles are a cluster of tropical islands lying just off the southeastern coast of Durotar. Originally settled by the Darkspear trolls after fleeing their ancestral islands, the archipelago is currently lost to the rogue witch doctor Zalazane, who drove his people into exile with dark magic and enslaved minions. Following their flight across the Great Sea alongside Thrall, the Darkspear tribe claimed the Echo Isles as their new home. Their peace was repeatedly shattered: first by the naval forces of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore during Kul Tiras' invasion of Durotar, and later from within. Shortly after the trolls drove back Proudmoore's fleet, one of their own witch doctors, Zalazane, seized dark arts to enslave the minds of his kin. Chieftain Vol'jin and the free Darkspears were forced to abandon the islands once more, seeking temporary refuge across the narrow strait at Sen'jin Village.

Echo Ridge Mine. Echo Ridge Mine is a small excavation carved into the northwestern cliffs of Northshire Valley. Rich in stone and ore, it has recently fallen into the clutches of a destructive kobold infestation, halting Northshire's local operations. Tucked away in the hills above Northshire Abbey, Echo Ridge Mine was meant to supply the valley with useful stone and metal. Instead, opportunistic kobolds swarmed through the tunnels, driving out the local workers. Marshal McBride views the infestation as an unacceptable security risk to Northshire's safety and recruitment efforts, directing new recruits straight into the tunnels to cull their numbers and reclaim the site.

Elder Rise. Elder Rise sits directly east of Thunder Bluff's central plateau, reachable across long suspension bridges from both the High and Middle Rises. It serves as the spiritual heart of the tauren capital, hosting the Cenarion Circle, tauren druids and priests, and the governing Council of Elders. Connected to the main mesas by swaying rope bridges, Elder Rise is dedicated to quiet reflection, sacred wisdom, and civic governance. Tauren druids and priests gather here to teach acolytes the ways of nature and spiritual devotion. High atop this mesa resides Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem, the revered leader who brought druidism back to the tauren people and forged close ties with the Cenarion Circle. Alongside these wild sanctuaries stands the Hall of Elders, where tribal leaders convene to deliberate on matters facing their fledgling capital.

Engineering Labs. The Engineering Labs are a multi-tiered research and manufacturing facility deep within Gnomeregan. Connected to the Workshop Entrance and Launch Bay, this bustling center of gnome innovation was overrun during the city's radioactive cataclysm and is now swarming with crazed leper gnomes and rogue mechanical contraptions. Built around a central mechanical structure, the Engineering Labs span two primary tiers connected by a central cargo lift. In Gnomeregan's prime, tinkerers here developed schematics and fine-tuned clockwork inventions. Today, radiation leaks have driven the remaining researchers mad, transforming them into deranged leper gnomes who mindlessly guard malfunctioning machinery alongside rogue constructs.

Falfarren River. The Falfarren River flows northeast to southwest through the heart of Ashenvale, originating on the slopes of Mount Hyjal before slipping underground beneath the Barrens' northern mountains. It forms a natural boundary between night elven domains around Astranaar to the west and the encroaching Horde outposts to the east. Travelers must tread carefully, as its shaded banks and shallows harbor hostile wildlife and mark the edge of open conflict. Feeding down from Mount Hyjal, the waters of the Falfarren cascade across waterfalls into Xavian before winding between Splintertree Post and Night Run. While it is neither exceptionally deep nor impassable under ordinary weather, it serves as the rough geopolitical dividing line in central Ashenvale. To the west lie Astranaar and the core holdings of the Kaldorei; to the east sit the camps and lumber operations of the Horde. Crossing the main road's wooden bridges brings travelers into the contested heart of the forest, where patrols clash along the banks.

Fallen Sky Lake. Fallen Sky Lake is a secluded body of water nestled deep within the forests of eastern Ashenvale. Situated between Silverwing Outpost and the encroaching Warsong Labor Camp, the serene waters hide danger in the form of hostile shadethicket woodkin that aggressively defend the lake and its central isle. Tucked south of Silverwing Outpost and just west of the Warsong Labor Camp, Fallen Sky Lake offers a fleeting glimpse of Ashenvale's natural splendor before the Orcish axes took root nearby. The shores and the small islet rising from the middle of the lake are inhabited by shadethickets—corrupted or territorial wildkin that view any two-legged intruder as a threat. The heart of the island serves as the domain of a powerful Shadethicket Oracle, whose presence keeps the local woodkin bound to the grove and relentlessly vigilant against travelers passing through.

Faol's Rest. Faol's Rest is a quiet, neglected gravesite situated in eastern Tirisfal Glades, just southwest of the Scarlet Monastery. It was erected as the tomb of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, the revered spiritual patriarch who founded the Knights of the Silver Hand. Today, untended beneath the blighted canopy, it serves as a release graveyard for those who perish near the monastery. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, this secluded hollow was a place of solemn pilgrimage. It holds the stone tomb of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, who led the Church of the Holy Light through the dark days of the Second War and instituted the order of paladins to protect humanity. Faol passed away peacefully prior to the arrival of the Scourge, spared the mortal agony of seeing his kingdom fall. In those brighter years, mourners regularly journeyed up the road from Capital City to leave offerings and pay respects to the beloved patriarch.

Far Watch Post. Far Watch Post is a fortified Horde outpost situated just west of the Southfury River bridge connecting Durotar to the Barrens. Serving as the front line of defense for the orcish homeland, the post guards vital trade caravans against aggressive quilboar packs and hostile Alliance incursions. Located at the western foot of the bridge out of Durotar, Far Watch Post is the first bastion of Horde authority travellers see when entering the vast, arid savannah of the Barrens. The settlement is Spartan but functional, built for tactical readiness rather than comfort. It features a sturdy orcish watchtower, a burrow, and pre-sighted siege catapults trained toward the dusty plains. Directly south of the main road, peons tend a pen of riding wolves ready to bear messengers or reinforcements. Far Watch Post exists primarily to keep the supply road to Crossroads secure, screening incoming traffic and repelling raids from roaming quilboar tribes and stealthy Alliance scouts.

Fargodeep Mine. Fargodeep Mine is an abandoned gold mine nestled in central Elwynn Forest, south of Goldshire. Once a productive source of wealth for the Kingdom of Stormwind, it has recently been overrun by a belligerent clan of kobolds. Fargodeep Mine once provided steady gold to Stormwind's treasury, but the Kingdom's dwindling military presence in Elwynn has left outlying resources vulnerable. Kobolds quickly swarmed into the dark tunnels, establishing a bustling warren beneath the hills. Marshal Dughan and the local authorities in Goldshire view the infestation with deep concern, not only because of lost ore, but because the emboldened creatures now threaten nearby farmsteads like the Stonefield and Maclure holdings.

Farstrider Lodge. Tucked away in the southeastern hills of Loch Modan, Farstrider Lodge is a tranquil hunting outpost built in high elven style. Though founded as an elven waystation, it now serves travelers, rangers, and trappers of all Alliance races looking to test their skills against the local wildlife. Farstrider Lodge stands apart from the sturdy stone and timber works typical of Khaz Modan. Bearing the graceful curves and vaulted woodwork of high elven craftsmanship, the outpost is named after the Farstriders, the renowned rangers of Quel'Thalas. Long before the recent wars shattered the elven homeland, Farstriders ranged far south of their borders to explore and build ties with the wider world. While only a solitary high elf remains to tend the lodge today, its hunting heritage endures under the stewardship of local dwarves and human woodsmen.

Fel Rock. Fel Rock is a blighted cavern hidden within the woods just north of Dolanaar on the boughs of Teldrassil. Once a tranquil hollow, it has fallen into corruption under the influence of the satyr Lord Melenas and his horde of vicious grells. Tucked away in the forested hills north of Dolanaar, Fel Rock was once an ordinary, peaceful cavern carved into the wood and stone of Teldrassil. Today, it stands as an unsettling reminder of the creeping taint encroaching on the world tree. Twisted roots and unnatural shadows dominate the cavern interior, overrun by swarms of wild grells and grellkin.

Felfire Hill. Felfire Hill is a blighted, demon-infested rise nestled in eastern Ashenvale. Struck by falling infernals during the Third War, its corrupted soil still burns with demonic power. The Horde maintains fortified guard posts on the bridges leading into the hill to safeguard their nearby settlements. During the cataclysmic invasion of the Third War, flaming meteors fell across Kalimdor as the Burning Legion unleashed its dread infernals. Several of those fiery behemoths struck this ridge in Ashenvale, scouring away the ancient woodlands and corrupting the earth itself. Today, the scorched landscape remains saturated with fel energy and prowled by lingering demons who survived the Legion's defeat at Mount Hyjal.

Fenris Isle. Fenris Isle is a large, mist-shrouded island in Lordamere Lake, bordering the eastern edge of Silverpine Forest. Once home to a bustling Lordaeron military stronghold, the island now lies under the iron grip of undead Rot Hide gnolls and a rogue Scourge necromancer. Before the Third War devastated northern Lordaeron, Fenris Isle served as a vital outpost for the kingdom, anchored by Fenris Keep. When the Scourge tore through the realm, the garrison was slaughtered or fled into exile, leaving the island abandoned to the dead. In the years since, the island became a stronghold for the Rot Hide gnolls—vile, plague-ridden creatures who established a crude empire across the lake's shores. The Forsaken of Silverpine Forest keep a vigilant watch on the island, viewing its entrenched inhabitants as a severe threat to their northern territories.

Fenris Keep. Fenris Keep is an isolated stone fortress situated atop Fenris Isle in the heart of Lordamere Lake. Once a strategic stronghold housing Lordaeron troops, it has fallen into the hands of the Scourge under the rogue mage Thule Ravenclaw. Before the Third War, Fenris Keep held strategic importance for the Kingdom of Lordaeron, stationing a sizable contingent of troops to safeguard Lordamere Lake. When the undead Scourge swept across the land, the island fortress was overwhelmed along with the rest of the realm. Rather than crumbling into forgotten ruin, it was seized by Thule Ravenclaw, a traitorous former wizard of the Kirin Tor. Ravenclaw allied himself with the Scourge, subjugated the resident gnolls with foul necromancy to create the ravenous Rot Hide pack, and entrenched himself deep inside the keep's stone halls.

Field of Giants. The Field of Giants is an expansive plain covering the southern Barrens between Camp Taurajo and the marshes of Dustwallow. Named for the towering kodo, thunder lizards, and massive beasts that graze its arid scrub, the region has recently grown far more perilous due to an encroaching silithid infestation. Stretching along the southern span of the Gold Road, the Field of Giants is remote, rugged, and lightly defended compared to the Barrens to the north. While the road's wooden watchtowers stand largely abandoned, the land itself thrums with life. Tremendous herds of Kalimdor's megafauna wander the vast flats, drawing hunters and naturalists alike. However, safety is elusive here: dwarven excavators from Bael Modan dig aggressively to the south, and a far more sinister menace has begun burrowing beneath the earth.

Fire Scar Shrine. Fire Scar Shrine is a despoiled night elf shrine nestled in the southwestern forests of Ashenvale. Once a serene place of worship, it has been corrupted by demonic forces and turned into a blister of fel energy right on Astranaar's doorstep. Located southwest of Astranaar and west of the Ruins of Stardust, Fire Scar Shrine stands as a grim reminder of the Burning Legion's lingering poison in Ashenvale. The shrine has fallen under the sway of demonic corruption, nurtured by servants of the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand and the Shadow Council. Fel magic has twisted the surrounding earth into scorched rock, where roaming demons now gather in open defiance of the forest's defenders.

Forest's Edge. Forest's Edge is a wooded wedge of land along the southwestern frontier of Elwynn Forest, flanked by rivers leading toward Westfall. Guarded to the north by Westbrook Garrison, this untamed area has become dangerously overrun by riverpaw gnolls under the command of the notorious Hogger. Tucked southwest of Stormwind City between Mirror Lake Orchard and the rivers bordering Westfall, Forest's Edge forms a natural peninsula of woodland. Despite its proximity to Westbrook Garrison, the Stormwind army's thin ranks have left the area vulnerable to wild beasts and raiding parties. Wandering boars roam among the trees and along the riverbanks, but the true menace is the concentration of Riverpaw gnolls who have made these woods their staging ground.

Forest Song. Forest Song is an ancient night elf ruin nestled in northeastern Ashenvale, near the tainted woods of Satyrnaar and the great portal at Bough Shadow. At present, it stands largely deserted save for the vigilant druid Kayneth Stillwind, who watches over the eastern border against emergent threats. Tucked away in the dense woodlands of northeastern Ashenvale, Forest Song was once an elegant settlement of the kaldorei. Today, white stone columns and crumbling archways are overgrown with ivy and wild ferns. Located northeast of Satyrnaar and just north of the encroaching Warsong Lumber Camp, the ruins hold a quiet, strategic overlook along the eastern trails toward Azshara and Bough Shadow. While the woods around it are plagued by demonic corruption and Horde incursions, the ruin itself maintains a haunting, tranquil stillness.

Forgotten Pools. The Forgotten Pools is the northernmost of the verdant oases scattered across the arid Barrens, located just northwest of the Crossroads. Fed by subterranean springs, this vibrant pocket of lush flora and waters is bitterly contested between indigenous wildlife, wandering Kolkar centaur, and the Horde. Situated off the western road leading out of the Crossroads, the Forgotten Pools offers a stark contrast to the parched savannas that surround it. Thick reeds, palm trees, and unusual flora like Laden Mushrooms cluster around its freshwater shore, drawing plainstriders, snapjaw turtles, and zhevras from miles around. However, the oasis is far from peaceful. Kolkar centaur maintain a constant encampment along the banks, jealously guarding the water supply against travelers and bringing them into direct conflict with Horde travelers from the Crossroads.

Forlorn Cavern. Tucked along the northern shores of Ironforge's subterranean lake, the Forlorn Cavern is a dimly lit, secluded district far removed from the city's bustling Great Forge. It serves as a shadowy refuge where thieves, cutpurses, and practitioners of the dark arts conduct their business away from prying dwarven guards. While the rest of Ironforge clangs with anvil strikes and radiates heat from the Great Forge, the Forlorn Cavern is cold, damp, and hushed. Wrapping along the northern edge of the mountain's underground lake, the winding pathways sit comfortably out of sight between the Mystic Ward and the Hall of Explorers. Its gloom makes it an ideal gathering place for those who prefer to keep their affairs discreet. Local authorities largely turn a blind eye, leaving cutpurses to compare poisons, warlocks to consult grimoires behind closed doors, and quiet tradesfolk—like weapon smiths and lone fishermen—to ply their crafts undisturbed.

Forlorn Rowe. The Forlorn Rowe is an ominous, shadowy hill perched on the northern boundary of the Raven Hill Cemetery in Duskwood. It is infamous as the dark abode of Morbent Fel, a necromancer whose malevolent magic animates the restless dead throughout the forest. Rising along the northern edge of the Raven Hill Cemetery, the Forlorn Rowe is perpetually cloaked in gloom. Atop this rise sits the home of Morbent Fel, the lich-like necromancer responsible for much of the walking dead haunting the surrounding wilderness. Bound by foul arcane enchantments, the master of the hill directs his skeletal servants from this vantage, rendering the entire northwestern corner of Duskwood perilous for travelers.

Fray Island. Fray Island is a windswept, rocky islet lying just off the Merchant Coast of the Barrens. Home to a rough-and-tumble training ring, it is famous as a neutral haven where warriors from across Azeroth come to test their mettle. Situated off the eastern bluffs of the Barrens, Fray Island is far removed from the watchful eyes of both Orgrimmar and Theramore. The island serves as a training place for warriors of all races and creeds. At its heart sits a fighting arena overseen by Klannoc Macleod, where seasoned fighters and raw recruits gather to compete in brutal brawls.

Freewind Post. Freewind Post is the primary Horde outpost in Thousand Needles, perched high atop one of the canyon's dramatic stone mesas. Accessible primarily by tauren lift and winding rope bridges, it serves as a defensive refuge against centaur warbands and a vital frontier staging ground. Built directly upon the canyon mesas, Freewind Post relies on ingenuity and height to safeguard its people. The Galak centaur dominate the arid canyon floor below, but they cannot effectively scale the towering cliffs or breach the heavy wooden elevators that haul Horde travelers up into the sky. A labyrinth of rope and plank bridges connects Freewind to neighboring spires, forming a secure aerie. Beyond keeping centaur raiding parties at bay, the outpost also helps manage the screeching harpies nesting along the bluffs and tends to the nearby wyvern grounds at Highperch, where wild eggs are culled and trained as loyal wind rider mounts for the Horde.

Frostmane Hold. Frostmane Hold is a fortified encampment and cavern complex claimed by the Frostmane ice trolls in western Dun Morogh. Tucked into the crags south of Gnomeregan, it serves as a central staging ground for troll raiders encroaching on dwarven territory. The Ironforge Guard keeps a close watch on the hold to gauge the growing troll threat. Carved into the freezing cliffs of western Dun Morogh, Frostmane Hold consists of rough outdoor structures and a winding cave system. For the Frostmane tribe, it functions as a primary stronghold, densely guarded by hideskinners and headhunters. From here, the trolls launch raids into the surrounding valleys, testing the defenses of nearby settlements like Kharanos and menacing travelers along the mountain passes.

Frostmane Hovel. Frostmane Hovel is a rugged cave den tucked into the southern crags of Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh. It serves as an entrenched shelter for aggressive Frostmane trolls pressing directly into dwarven training grounds. Carved into the southern mountains flanking Coldridge Valley, the Frostmane Hovel shelters indigenous Frostmane trolls who refuse to yield the high snows to Ironforge. Operating out of crude caverns like this, the trolls mount continuous raids against local dwarven camps and disrupt supply lines into the valley.

Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm. Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm is an overrun homestead in northern Westfall, just off the main road from Elwynn Forest. Once a prosperous plot tended by Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna, the fields and farmhouse have been seized by the Defias Brotherhood and prowling harvest golems. Situated near the northern border of Westfall, Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm was once known for producing robust crops to feed the kingdom. That ended when the Defias Brotherhood swept across the countryside. Outlaws drove Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna from their land, leaving their fields overrun with mechanical harvest golems programmed to attack anyone approaching. With the farm buildings occupied by bandits and the fields prowled by renegade machinery, the rightful owners have been forced to camp along the roadside near the Jansen Stead, mourning the loss of their home and livelihood.

Galardell Valley. Galardell Valley is a rugged, dangerous canyon nestled in the northeastern heights of the Redridge Mountains. The gorge is overrun by aggressive gnoll packs and sits beneath the shadow of the infamous Tower of Ilgalar. Carved into the northeastern cliffs of Redridge, Galardell Valley has fallen completely out of the control of Lakeshire's defenders. Fierce Redridge gnolls prowl the lowlands and camp along the canyon floor, organized under brutal pack leaders such as Lieutenant Fangore. Towering high above the ravines stands the dark spire of the Tower of Ilgalar, the stronghold of the renegade mage Morganth, making the entire valley a persistent source of dread for the surrounding settlements.

Gallows' End Tavern. Gallows' End Tavern is the principal inn of Brill and the heart of Forsaken hospitality in Tirisfal Glades. Beyond offering shelter and spirits to weary travelers, it serves as an essential hub for class mentors, trade instructors, and covert interrogations. Standing prominently along the road in Brill, Gallows' End Tavern serves as the primary gathering place for newly awakened Forsaken leaving Deathknell and journeying south toward the Undercity. Despite their undead condition, Forsaken still frequent its halls for fellowship, trade, and refuge. The inn houses various class instructors—guiding young warriors, priests, mages, rogues, and warlocks—as well as vendors and medical practitioners.

Garren's Haunt. Garren's Haunt is an abandoned farmstead nestled in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a prosperous human homestead, the farm fell to ruin when the Scourge wiped out the Garren family, leaving the overgrown grounds overrun by feral Rot Hide gnolls. Before the Third War, this farmstead supported a family and produced bountiful harvests under the Kingdom of Lordaeron. When the Plague of Undeath swept across the countryside, the Scourge descended upon the farm and slaughtered Garren and his kin. Today, the fields lie gray and withered, the farmhouse and barn decaying under the perpetual gloom of Tirisfal.

Gates of Ironforge. The Gates of Ironforge serve as the monumental main entrance leading travelers from the snowy mountain vales of Dun Morogh into the dwarven capital. Carved directly into the sheer stone face of the mountain, they are guarded inside by a colossal statue of High King Modimus Anvilmar. Approached by climbing the winding, fortified ramp ascending from central Dun Morogh, the Gates of Ironforge present an imposing facade visible across much of the snowy lowlands. Beyond the massive portal, visitors enter the city proper, greeted immediately by an enormous stone statue honoring High King Modimus Anvilmar—the legendary ruler who united the dwarven clans before the War of the Three Hammers. Passing through these gates leads directly into the bustling commercial district of the Commons.

Gates of Orgrimmar. The Gates of Orgrimmar form the imposing southern threshold of the Horde capital, carved directly into the red rock of northern Durotar. Flanked by heavy timber and iron battlements, this grand entryway connects the arid wastes outside to the busy commons of the Valley of Strength. It stands as a physical declaration of orcish endurance and martial strength. Framed by towering wooden palisades, massive iron spikes, and fortified watchtowers, the main gate guards the primary chasm cutting into the mountains sheltering Orgrimmar. For travelers approaching from Razor Hill and the scrublands of Durotar, the entrance serves as both a welcoming monument and a stark deterrent to any who would threaten the new Horde. Heavily armed Orgrimmar Grunts and Darkspear Headhunters patrol the approach, keeping vigilant watch over all traffic entering the city.

Goblin Foundry. The Goblin Foundry is an industrial workshop deep within the Deadmines where goblin tinkerers manufacture heavy metalwork for the Defias Brotherhood. A massive smelting cauldron dominates the chamber, which remains occupied by goblin craftsmen and engineers under Gilnid. Carved into the subterranean depths of Moonbrook, the Goblin Foundry provides the Defias Brotherhood with heavy manufacturing power. Goblin craftsmen and engineers work among the smelters and iron ramps, producing anchors and cannonballs.

Gol'Bolar Quarry. Gol'Bolar Quarry is a dwarven excavation site carved into the snowy hills of southeastern Dun Morogh. Rich in stone and ore, the bustling mining operation has ground to a halt after being overrun by vicious troggs surging from the depths. Situated southeast of Kharanos, Gol'Bolar Quarry was established by Ironforge dwarves to extract vital stone and mineral wealth from the mountains. However, deep excavation work uncovered underground warrens, unleashing a horde of hostile troggs that quickly drove out the miners. Today, the upper camp serves as an embattled staging ground where overseers, tradesfolk, and Prospector Gehn rally dwarven and gnomish recruits to drive the beasts back and reclaim the pit.

Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine. Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine is an overrun excavation pit deep within the heart of Gol'Bolar Quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. Originally worked by dwarven miners, the tunnels breached subterranean trogg caverns, unleashing a violent infestation that claimed the entire site. Today, the deepest shafts serve as the stronghold for the trogg warband led by the brute Hammerspine. The mine was established by Ironforge dwarves seeking stone and rich ore deposits beneath the craggy peaks of Dun Morogh. Work came to an abrupt, violent halt when pickaxes fractured a wall into an ancient subterranean cavern system inhabited by troggs. Swarming out from the dark, the subterranean beasts overwhelmed the work crews and forced a hasty retreat, ultimately spilling outward to overrun the surrounding quarry pit as well.

Gold Coast Quarry. The Gold Coast Quarry is an open-pit mine carved into the bluffs of southwestern Westfall. Once a prized source of stone, minerals, and gold for the Kingdom of Stormwind, it has been seized by the Defias Brotherhood to fuel their growing insurrection. Before the kingdom fell into neglect, the Gold Coast Quarry supplied raw building materials and precious gold to help rebuild Stormwind. When royal troops withdrew from Westfall and left the countryside unprotected, Defias highwaymen and renegade laborers took control of the diggings. The Brotherhood now patrols the terraced stone ramps, using the site's vantage over the coast and plundering whatever minerals remain to fund their rebellion.

Gold Road. The Gold Road is the primary north-south artery cutting through the arid expanse of the Barrens. Stretching from the Mor'shan Rampart on the border of Ashenvale down past the Crossroads toward the southern reaches, it serves as the vital transit line for the young Horde. The Gold Road is a long, sun-baked dirt highway that carves its way through the center of the Barrens. To the north, it begins near the fortified Mor'shan Rampart and Mor'shan Base Camp, which guard against night elf incursions from Ashenvale. Traveling south, it connects with the eastern roadway leading to Durotar before intersecting the bustling trading settlement of the Crossroads. Continuing southward past the lush waters of the local oases and the foothills near the Wailing Caverns, the northern span of the highway reaches a dried-up riverbed, where travelers cross into the more hazardous southern portion of the savanna.

Golden Plains. The Golden Plains form a vast, sun-drenched basin stretching southeast of Thunder Bluff in central Mulgore. Cherished by the tauren, these sweeping grasslands serve as prime hunting territory and a vital grazing habitat for wandering herds of kodo. Spreading out beneath the towering mesas of Thunder Bluff, the Golden Plains represent the untamed heart of Mulgore. The shifting sea of golden and green grass offers an abundant sanctuary for local wildlife, making it one of the most treasured traditional hunting grounds of the nomadic tauren. Broad kodo herds roam across the rolling basin, while hunters share stories of legendary quarry, most notably the great kodo Arra'chea, who wanders quietly through the tall stalks.

Goldshire. Goldshire is a vital human crossroads town nestled in central Elwynn Forest, connecting Stormwind City with Westfall, Redridge, and the southern frontier. Rebuilt after its destruction in the First War, it serves as a bustling waystation anchored by the famous Lion's Pride Inn and defended by a hard-pressed contingent of the Stormwind Guard. Positioned where the king's highways meet, Goldshire has long been the civic and commercial heart of rural Elwynn. However, the town's bucolic charm masks escalating peril in Year 25 ADP. With Stormwind's military resources stretched thin and King Varian Wrynn mysteriously absent, Marshal Dughan must rely on passing adventurers rather than regular troops to contain surrounding threats. Aggressive Riverpaw gnolls push inward from the western border, while vicious murlocs claim the shores of Stone Cairn Lake and Crystal Lake, claiming the lives of royal guards and encroaching dangerously close to the town center.

Grand Vestibule. The Grand Vestibule is the monumental entrance hall of the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades. Lined with crimson pillars and stone effigies of fallen crusaders, it serves as the threshold where adventurers prepare to breach the monastery's inner halls. Past the heavy outer gates of the Monastery lies the Grand Vestibule, an expansive marble hall dedicated to the martial pride of the Scarlet Crusade. Statues of armored champions stand vigil beside vaulted stone pillars, and zealous sentries, disciples, and augurs patrol the flagstones to strike down anyone daring to enter without the order's crimson tabard. For trespassers, it is the first taste of the Crusade's unrelenting discipline and fanaticism.

Great Forge. The Great Forge is the fiery heart and namesake of the dwarven capital of Ironforge. Situated at the very center of the city, its massive furnaces and famed Great Anvil never rest, producing legendary armaments and serving as the bustling center of civic life. The Great Forge was the very first structure built by the early dwarves beneath Ironforge Mountain, and the grand capital grew in concentric rings around it. Molten stone and slag pour constantly from giant foundries into glowing channels, illuminating the cavern with an amber haze. At its center stands the massive Great Anvil, overseen by Master of the Forge Myolor Sunderfury. Renowned masters of metalwork gather around its rim, hammering out armor, tools, and weapons day and night.

Great Lift. The Great Lift is a massive, tauren-engineered elevator system perched on the southern edge of the Barrens. It serves as the primary route lowering travelers and supplies hundreds of feet into the sheer canyon basin of Thousand Needles. Despite its strategic value, aggressive quilboar encroaching through the southern wastes have made approaching the rim increasingly perilous. Spanning the sheer cliff edge between the southern Barrens and the canyon floor of Thousand Needles, the Great Lift stands as a marvel of practical tauren construction. Built using heavy timber, braided rope, and counterweighted pulleys, its paired platforms carry caravans, couriers, and warriors safely across a vertical precipice that would otherwise break any wagon. At the top and bottom platforms, tauren like Brave Moonhorn and Grish Longrunner maintain watch, keeping travelers informed of the road ahead and ensuring cargo passes smoothly.

Greatwood Vale. Greatwood Vale is a forested valley nestled in the eastern foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains, reached via the perilous Webwinder Path. Recently, the hostile Grimtotem tribe seized the vale, using it as a staging ground for bloody assaults on neighboring settlements. Tucked away off the Webwinder Path, Greatwood Vale has become a violent frontier. The Grimtotem tribe, under the ruthless leadership of Grundig Darkcloud, has moved into the vale in force, cutting off safe passage and bringing terror to the surrounding foothills.

Greenpaw Village. Greenpaw Village is a furbolg settlement nestled in central Ashenvale, situated between Raynewood Retreat and Silverwind Refuge. It serves as the primary home of the Foulweald tribe, led by Chief Murgut and the shaman Oakpaw. Gripped by demonic corruption and embattled by outside forces, the village is an active conflict point for both Alliance and Horde travelers. Situated south of Raynewood Retreat and northeast of Silverwind Refuge, Greenpaw Village was once a quiet home for the forest's ursine denizens. In the wake of the Third War, its resident furbolgs—the Foulweald tribe—succumbed to the insidious corruption tainting Ashenvale's soil and spirits. Under the dominion of Chief Murgut and their corrupted spiritual guide, Shaman Oakpaw, the Foulweald have become hostile and unstable, attacking any travelers who stray into their forest territory.

Greymane Wall. The Greymane Wall is a massive stone bulwark spanning the southern frontier of Silverpine Forest. Built by King Genn Greymane after the Second War, it seals the kingdom of Gilneas away from the outside world behind impenetrable, locked gates. Following the Second War, King Genn Greymane grew resentful of the Alliance of Lordaeron, particularly the taxes required to maintain the orc internment camps and build Nethergarde Keep. Deciding Gilneas had given enough of its coin and blood for foreign troubles, Greymane withdrew from the Alliance and ordered a colossal barrier raised across the head of the peninsula. In doing so, he abandoned lands belonging to Lord Darius Crowley—including Pyrewood Village and Ambermill—leaving them stranded on the northern side of the stones. When the Third War brought the Plague of Undeath and countless desperate refugees to its foot, the gates remained pitilessly barred.

Grim Batol. Grim Batol is an ancient, ruined dwarven mountain fortress looming over the eastern edge of the Wetlands. Built by the Wildhammer clan, abandoned after a dark curse during the War of the Three Hammers, and later occupied by the Dragonmaw orcs as a dragon breeding lair, its sealed gates remain an ominous blight upon the highlands. Following the ancient civil war of the three clans, Thane Khardros Wildhammer carved Grim Batol out of the jagged mountains east of the marsh. During the subsequent War of the Three Hammers, the Dark Iron sorceress Modgud laid siege to the fortress. Although Khardros struck her down, Modgud cast a foul shadow across the stones before her death. The lingering taint rendered the halls uninhabitable, forcing the surviving Wildhammer dwarves to abandon their magnificent kingdom and migrate north into the Hinterlands.

Grizzled Den. The Grizzled Den is a cavern nestled in the snowy hills just southwest of Kharanos. It serves as a notorious lair for the ferocious, frost-breathing wendigos indigenous to Dun Morogh. Carved deep into the crags southwest of Kharanos, the Grizzled Den is notorious among local mountaineers as the nesting ground of Dun Morogh's wendigo packs. These aggressive, ape-like beasts wield frosty breath against intruders and band together to protect their hollows. Despite the peril, daring hunters regularly brave the cavern's depths to harvest thick wendigo manes, which fetch a respectable sum among craftsmen looking to line cold chairs and carriage seats with insulated fur.

Grizzlepaw Ridge. Grizzlepaw Ridge is a rugged, craggy hillside rising south of Thelsamar in Loch Modan. It is notorious among local mountaineers for its dense population of wild bears, led by the legendary beast Ol' Sooty. Overlooking the road south of Thelsamar and bordering Stonesplinter Valley to the west, Grizzlepaw Ridge is rough country dominated by predatory wildlife. The slopes are claimed by territorial bears that pose a hazard to travelers skirting the mountains. Deep within the ridge dwells Ol' Sooty, a massive and unusually fierce bear feared by local hunters. Travelers moving between the dwarven settlements must keep a wary eye on the tree line and rocky terraces above.

Grol'dom Farm. Grol'dom Farm is a modest orcish homestead situated in the northern Barrens along the road between Durotar and the Crossroads. Inhabited by Kranal Fiss and his family, the farm raises swine in the arid plains despite constant harassment from aggressive local quillboars. Established following the settlement of Durotar, Grol'dom Farm represents the Horde's early efforts to farm the dry expanse of the Barrens. Tended by the orc Kranal Fiss and his children, the small homestead primarily raises pigs while braving the harsh wildlife and aggressive Razormane quillboar raiders that prowl the nearby ridges. It is a lonely, rugged outpost that supplies vital sustenance to the emerging orcish nation.

Grommash Hold. Grommash Hold is the fortified seat of Warchief Thrall, nestled high in the red cliffs of the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar. Named in honor of Grommash Hellscream's sacrifice, the fortress serves as the command center and political heart of the new Horde. Perched within the tranquil Valley of Wisdom, Grommash Hold serves as the royal court and strategic sanctum of the Horde. Built into the towering canyon walls, its thick stone interior remains notably dim and chilly—a deliberate choice by Warchief Thrall to keep emissaries, petitioners, and warlords sharp and sober during audiences. Here, Thrall deliberates on the defense of Kalimdor, guided by veteran counselors like Eitrigg and visited by racial chieftains such as Vol'jin.

Grove of the Ancients. The Grove of the Ancients is a sacred night elven sanctuary set amidst old temple ruins in southeastern Darkshore. Nestled beside the Wildbend River, this serene haven serves as a gathering ground for nature spirits and is watched over by the venerable Ancient of Lore, Onu. Tucked away near the southeastern mountains of Darkshore, the Grove of the Ancients stands as a peaceful haven surrounded by aged temple stones. Through its heart flows the surging Wildbend River, providing a quiet refuge amidst a coastline increasingly plagued by corruption and restless wildlife. The grove serves as a meeting place for the Circle of Ancients, where nature spirits and kaldorei tend to the delicate balance of the forest.

Gryphon Roost. Perched along the ramparts just east of Stormwind's Trade District, the Gryphon Roost serves as the capital's primary transit hub for aerial travel. Managed by the human gryphon master Dungar Longdrink, it houses the majestic beasts that ferry couriers, soldiers, and adventurers across the Eastern Kingdoms. Situated atop the fortifications overlooking the Trade District canal, the Gryphon Roost connects the capital with outlying Alliance garrisons and settlements throughout the Eastern Kingdoms. The flight network is orchestrated by the seasoned master Dungar Longdrink, who coordinates routes to Ironforge, Lakeshire, Sentinel Hill, and beyond.

Gunther's Retreat. Gunther's Retreat is an isolated island sanctuary set in Brightwater Lake in central Tirisfal Glades. It serves as the refuge of Gunther Arcanus, a renegade necromancer who broke free from the Scourge through raw willpower. Distrustful of all outsiders, the recluse surrounds his campsite with loyal undead minions to keep intruders away. Situated amid the misty waters of Brightwater Lake, Gunther's Retreat is an unassuming island encampment easily mistaken for another pocket of the Scourge. Its master, Gunther Arcanus, achieved what few mortal sorcerers could: when raised in undeath, his arcane mastery allowed him to tear away his soul from the Lich King's iron grip without any outside help. Mistrusting everyone, Gunther assumed the rest of the undead wandering Lordaeron were still puppets of the Scourge. He retired to this lonely isle to practice his craft in peace, posting zombie sentinels to tear apart anyone who crosses the water.

Hall of Arms. The Hall of Arms serves as the headquarters of Ironforge's military might and the chief arsenal of the dwarven kingdom. Located within the Military Ward, this fortified compound trains dwarven combatants and orchestrates the deployment of heavy armor and aerial war machines. Situated in the southeastern corner of the Military Ward, the Hall of Arms is the operational command center for the armed forces of Ironforge. Beyond housing veteran trainers for warriors and hunters, the expansive facility serves as a massive depot and staging ground for mechanized warfare. Heavy steam tanks are assembled and maintained on-site to reinforce Alliance battlefields, while gyrocopters and flying machines are brought up via industrial conveyor belts and launched directly through vertical access shafts in the cavern ceiling toward the Ironforge Airfield above.

Hall of Arms (Northshire). The Hall of Arms is the martial wing of Northshire Abbey, situated south of the Main Hall. Here, veteran instructors drill the newest recruits of the Stormwind Army in the arts of the sword, shield, and holy combat. While the clerics and scholars ponder ancient tomes across the courtyard in the Library Wing, the Hall of Arms rings with the clash of blunted steel and the heavy cadence of martial instruction. Positioned on the south side of Northshire Abbey, this chamber serves as the primary training station for raw human fighters and devout aspirants taking up arms for the Stormwind Army. Here, seasoned battle instructors and paladin mentors teach the basic postures, disciplines, and fundamentals required to defend Elwynn Forest against encroaching kobolds, Defias bandits, and gnoll raiders.

Hall of Explorers. The Hall of Explorers is the sprawling archaeological wing of Ironforge and the bustling headquarters of the dwarven Explorers' League. Part museum, part archive, and part expedition command, it gathers relics, fossils, and ancient tomes from every corner of Azeroth to piece together the forgotten origins of the dwarven race. Occupying the northeastern cavern of Ironforge, the Hall of Explorers—sometimes referred to as the Assembly of Explorers—serves as the nerve center for all Alliance-sanctioned archaeological endeavors. Under the direction of High Explorer Muninn Magellas, scholars and field agents coordinate digs across distant lands, shipping back mysterious relics, ancient titan machinery, and prehistoric bones. The vast Library at its center functions as both a public museum and a restricted storehouse of historical lore.

Hall of Gears. The Hall of Gears is a multi-tiered industrial chamber situated inside the fallen city of Gnomeregan, just past the Clockwerk Run. Once a bustling center of mechanical movement, it has fallen into ruin, flooded with toxic sludge, roaming oozes, and irradiated troggs. Positioned just beyond the Clockwerk Run, the Hall of Gears illustrates the catastrophic collapse of the gnome capital. Divided into two main levels, the chamber's upper catwalks are held by aggressive, irradiated troggs that claw through collapsed access shafts. Below, the floor sits drenched in pools of radioactive fallout, where corrosive slimes and living poison elementals thrive in the toxic runoff.

Hall of Legends. The Hall of Legends is the elite military sanctuary and officer barracks of the Horde, nestled within Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. Behind its warded threshold, champions of the Horde gather around battle plans and arm themselves with premier weapons taken from conflicts across Azeroth and beyond. Located off the bustling avenues of the Valley of Strength, the Hall of Legends serves as the private redoubt for proven officers of the Horde. Beyond its guarded entrance, strategists and delegates from across the factions—including Chieftain Earthbind of Thunder Bluff, Blood Guard Hini'wana of the Darkspear, and Advisor Willington of the Undercity—confer over maps of contested lands and the military standing of both factions. Here, only warriors who have tested their mettle and achieved the rank of Stone Guard or higher are permitted entry to claim the spoils and armaments befitting their status.

Hall of Mysteries. Tucked into the Mystic Ward of Ironforge, the Hall of Mysteries serves as the city's spiritual and scholarly heart for the arcane and the divine. Within its blue-lit interior, dwarven and gnomish practitioners study ancient texts, train in the mysteries of the Holy Light, and weave arcane enchantments far from the clang of the Great Forge. Illuminated by a distinctive blue and purple luminescence, the Hall of Mysteries stands out starkly against the rest of Ironforge. While the city around it thrives on stone, iron, and heavy plate, the hall's five soaring pillars shelter scholars draped in soft, flowing robes. It bridges both arcane wizardry and holy devotion, serving as the headquarters for the dwarven priesthood and the Order of the Silver Hand within Khaz Modan. Here, young clerics and knights study holy texts like the Tome of Divinity and receive guidance before their journeys carry them onward to Stormwind's Cathedral of Light.

Hall of the Brave. The Hall of the Brave is the grand warrior barracks situated in the eastern heights of Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. It serves as the primary training compound and guild house for the Horde's front-line combatants, drillmasters, and battlemasters. Overlooking the tranquil waters and training rings of the Valley of Honor, the Hall of the Brave serves as a vital military hub for the burgeoning Horde. Inside, veteran officers and seasoned warriors instruct initiates in the brutal fundamentals of melee combat, stance mastery, and discipline. The hall is lined with training dummies and armaments, housing battlemasters who organize combatants for major military engagements across Azeroth.

Helm's Bed Lake. Helm's Bed Lake is a frozen body of water nestled in the southeastern hills of Dun Morogh. A maintained hole in the thick ice provides crucial fresh water to local mountaineers and travelers. However, the surrounding shoreline has become perilous due to prowling wildlife, encroaching troggs, and hostile Dark Iron infiltrators. Helm's Bed Lake sits quietly beneath a thick sheet of winter ice in southeastern Dun Morogh. Local dwarves keep an opening chopped through the frost to draw clean, fresh water. While crossing the frozen expanse is stable enough, lingering near the banks has become increasingly risky. Wild beasts wander the edges, displaced troggs scavenge along the ridges, and a cell of hostile Dark Iron dwarves has commandeered an abandoned lodge just south of the water, aggressively ambushing any travelers who pass through.

Heroes' Vigil. Heroes' Vigil is a quiet, sacred clearing situated on the central island within Stone Cairn Lake in eastern Elwynn Forest. Centered around a monument known as the Stone of Remembrance, it was dedicated to honor those who fell during the First War. Today, however, the shrine sits largely neglected by Stormwind and is overrun by dangerous renegade wizards. Erected after the First War, Heroes' Vigil centers upon the Stone of Remembrance, an inscribed stone circle meant to honor the soldiers and citizens slaughtered during the Old Horde's sacking of Goldshire and the surrounding valleys. Though once revered as a sacred bastion of faith and sacrifice, the vigil has gradually slipped from the attention of Stormwind's current rulers, leaving its hallowed grounds overgrown and unattended by the realm's soldiers.

Hidden Path. The Hidden Path is a secluded mountain trail winding through the crags above the Valley of Trials in Durotar. It serves as a rite of passage for aspiring shaman seeking the sacred Spirit Rock, while offering an overlooked vantage overlooking the rugged borders of the Barrens. Carved into the red peaks bordering the Valley of Trials, the Hidden Path is intentionally difficult to spot from the canyon floor. Young shaman are directed here by their mentors to prove their awareness and discipline before communing with the spirits at Spirit Rock. Along the trail's highest reaches, travelers are treated to expansive panoramic views stretching westward toward the rolling savannas of the Barrens.

High Rise. The High Rise is the uppermost tier of Thunder Bluff's central mesa, crowning the tauren capital. It hosts a bustling amphitheater centered around a communal bonfire alongside seasoned artisans, weapon merchants, and culinary masters. Unlike the lower tiers, this summit relies entirely on suspension rope bridges and the wind rider roost for travel. The High Rise perches atop Thunder Bluff's core plateau, catching the open winds high above the rolling plains of Mulgore. A focal gathering point for the united tribes, it centers around an open-air amphitheater and fire pit where citizens listen to important tribal announcements and fateful decisions. The surrounding tents and wooden stalls house renowned merchants, armories, and culinary trainers, including Aska's Kitchen and Mountaintop Bait & Tackle. While the lower tiers connect directly to Mulgore's prairie floor via massive wooden elevators, the High Rise stays aloft, accessible primarily through the wind rider roost and sweeping rope bridges linking to the neighboring Elder Rise and Hunter Rise.

High Seat. The High Seat is the grand throne room of Ironforge, situated between the Commons and the Great Forge. From this elevated chamber, King Magni Bronzebeard presides over the dwarven realm alongside his royal advisors and historians. The room also houses the sealed passageway leading down into the ancient depths of Old Ironforge. Overlooking the vibrant bustling rings of Ironforge, the High Seat serves as the royal seat of power for the kingdom of Khaz Modan. Within this vaulted chamber, King Magni Bronzebeard hears petitioners, holds council with his advisors, and directs the defense of the Alliance's northern bastions. Flanked by royal dignitaries such as Royal Historian Archesonus and Senator Barin Redstone, the High Seat remains a symbol of unyielding Bronzebeard authority and dwarven resilience amid troubling times across Azeroth.

Highperch. Highperch is an elevated plateau in western Thousand Needles, towering high above the canyon floor. It is renowned as a primary nesting ground for wild wyverns and wind riders. The roost is home to fierce prides defending their young among the windswept crags. Rising sharply out of the canyon floor, Highperch is a rugged sanctuary for Kalimdor's native wyverns. The plateau provides natural defense against predators and an unobstructed launch point for their hunting flights across Thousand Needles. Within its reaches, wyvern prides live under the protection of watchful patriarchs and matriarchs, tending to nests filled with pridelings. The beasts fiercely defend their territory against any intruders who manage to climb into their high domain.

Hillsbrad Fields. The Hillsbrad Fields encompass the cultivated farmlands and rustic settlement of Hillsbrad in western Hillsbrad Foothills. As one of the few surviving human communities in former Lordaeron that refused to succumb to the Scourge or join the fanatical Scarlet Crusade, its farmers and militia now face constant assaults from the nearby Forsaken at Tarren Mill. Spanning orchards, pumpkin patches, and pastures between Darrow Hill and the Azurelode Mine, the Hillsbrad Fields supply essential provisions to Southshore and the surviving Alliance resistance. While much of Lordaeron fell to the plague of undeath, the people of Hillsbrad endured, proudly retaining the royal tabard and heraldry of their fallen kingdom. Led by Magistrate Burnside and the Council of Hillsbrad, the township operates as an independent civic body under constant siege. The local blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices keep the populace armed, ensuring every farmer and laborer is prepared to defend their land.

Howling Vale. Tucked away in north-central Ashenvale near the Felwood border, the Howling Vale is a darkened dell overrun by savage, alien wolf-beasts known as the Terrowulf worgen. Hidden deep within its caves lies the ancient Shrine of Mel'Thandris, an Elune-blessed ruin tied intimately to the tragic origins of the worgen curse on Kalimdor.
