North of the road toward Felwood, the calm majesty of Ashenvale gives way to eerie, predatory howling. The vale shelters ancient trees alongside corrupted Terrowulf packlords and aggressive wildlife. At its heart lies a cave enshrining the memory of Mel'Thandris, an ancient night elf priestess. While the shrine once stood as a place of quiet devotion, its tranquil halls have fallen into ruined disrepair, defiled by feral wolf-men whose origin puzzles the Sentinels stationed nearby.

Hunter Rise. Hunter Rise is one of the elevated mesas making up the city of Thunder Bluff, situated just south of the central bluff. It serves as the primary training and gathering ground for the tauren's warriors, hunters, trackers, and skinners. Across its windswept platforms, young braves hone their martial skills and prepare for combat. Connected to the neighboring bluffs by swaying rope bridges, Hunter Rise is dedicated to the martial traditions of the tauren. It is anchored by the Hunter's Hall, where experienced marksmen, trackers, and warriors pass down their discipline to younger generations. Surrounding the lodge are practice grounds outfitted with training dummies, weapon racks, and skinning posts, making it a bustling center for those who live by spear, bow, and hide.

Hushed Bank. The Hushed Bank is the shadowy western shoreline of Duskwood, bordering the river that divides the forest from Westfall. Stretching from the junction near the Three Corners south toward Stranglethorn Vale, it is a quiet yet hazardous woodland stalked by prowling beasts and shadowed by dark mysteries. Running along the river boundary between Duskwood and Westfall, the Hushed Bank marks the transition from open plains and sunlit farms to pervasive, unnatural twilight. The wooden covered bridge crosses the river here, offering passage to travelers heading west out of the grim wood. Thick underbrush and creeping fog dominate the riverbanks, where large spiders and hungry forest wolves stalk unwary wayfarers who stray from the beaten path.

Iceflow Lake. Iceflow Lake is a frigid, partially frozen body of water situated in western Dun Morogh, directly north of Brewnall Village. Despite the relentless frost, local mountaineers maintain fishing holes through the sheet ice to secure fresh water and fish. The snow-covered islands in the center of the lake are prowled by aggressive winter wolves and their alpha, Timber. Spanning western Dun Morogh just outside Brewnall Village, Iceflow Lake battles the bitter Khaz Modan climate year-round. Thick ice sheets continually creep across the surface, forcing local residents like Paxton Ganter to regularly clear holes for ice fishing and drinking water. While the shore provides sustenance, the islands rising from the middle of the lake are far less welcoming. A fierce pack of wild wolves has made these icy mounds their territory, dominated by the notoriously savage gray worg known as Timber.

Iris Lake. Iris Lake is a blighted body of water resting in north-central Ashenvale, east of Astranaar. Once pristine, its waters have turned a sickly yellowish-green from demonic corruption seeping down from Felwood, and hostile bog beasts now prowl its shores. Nestled between Astranaar and the moonwell tended by Shael'dryn, Iris Lake stands as a grim reminder of the wounds inflicted during the Third War. Fel energies drifting south from the tainted heights of Felwood have poisoned the basin, turning its once-clear waters into a foul, sickly yellow-green mire. The corruption has twisted the native plant life and water spirits, raising aggressive bog beasts that lash out at any traveler who wanders near.

Ironband's Compound. Ironband's Compound is a fortified outpost tucked into the snowy hills south of Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh. Formerly home to the prospector Sturgy Ironband, the camp has been overrun by hostile Dark Iron dwarves who attack anyone venturing too close. Originally established by Sturgy Ironband, this compound south of Helm's Bed Lake once served as a staging post in the snowy wilderness of Dun Morogh. That changed when Dark Iron infiltrators pushed deep into Bronzebeard territory and seized the site for themselves. Now bristling with hostile dwarves, the compound serves as an enemy forward base threatening travelers and nearby settlements, right under the nose of Ironforge.

Ironband's Excavation Site. Ironband's Excavation Site is an expansive dwarven dig located in southeastern Loch Modan, just south of the lake and southwest of Farstrider Lodge. Led by Prospector Ironband, the archaeological operation was abruptly halted when aggressive, volatile troggs overran the trenches. Spurred by the dwarven drive to uncover their ancient Titan origins, Prospector Ironband established this sprawling digsite along the rugged cliffs of southeastern Loch Modan. What began as a promising excavation quickly turned into a disaster when the digging disturbed an unusually fierce and large breed of subterranean troggs. The creatures surged from the earth, driving back the miners and setting up camp amidst the scattered tools, broken carts, and half-excavated relics.

Ironbeard's Tomb. Ironbeard's Tomb is a defiled dwarven burial site situated west of the road leading north toward Dun Modr in the Wetlands. Marked by an outdoor graveyard and a stone statue of its namesake, the crypt has fallen into disuse as acidic oozes swarm the grounds. Travelers rarely set foot in the hollow unless searching for lost possessions swallowed by the slime. Overlooking the marshes along the road north to Dun Modr, Ironbeard's Tomb stands as a testament to the dwarven presence in the Wetlands. A monumental stone statue, presumed to depict Ironbeard himself, watches over the surrounding burial plot. Yet solemn peace no longer keeps vigil here. The subterranean crypt has been completely overrun by oozes of various black and crimson strains, leaving the tomb contaminated. Dwarves no longer bring their dead to this ruined sanctuary, and those brave enough to disturb the vaults do so primarily to hunt through the remains digested by the lurking slimes.

Ironclad Cove. Ironclad Cove is a massive subterranean cavern hidden beneath Westfall, housing an underground shipyard and dock. It serves as the secret construction dock for the Defias Brotherhood's war juggernaught and connects directly to the sea. Buried at the deepest point of the Deadmines, Ironclad Cove is a monumental sea cavern converted into a fortified dockyard. Here, Edwin VanCleef and the Defias Brotherhood have constructed an enormous warship known as the juggernaught. The cavern features extensive wooden scaffolding, islets, and loading catwalks manned by Defias pirates, deckhands, and overseers. Its existence reveals the true scale of the Defias threat: VanCleef intends not merely to raid Westfall's farmsteads, but to assemble a private naval force capable of bombarding the shores of Stormwind itself.

Ironforge Airfield. Tucked away high in the snowy peaks northeast of Ironforge, this remote dwarven airstrip serves as a proving ground and staging area for gnome flying machines and dwarven mountaineers. Unmarked by main roads, the plateau overlooks the jagged crags of Dun Morogh and the steep descent toward the Wetlands. Perched far above the beaten trails of Dun Morogh, the high-altitude airfield is a quiet marvel of Alliance cooperation. Sheltered by surrounding mountain peaks, dwarven masonry anchors the blustery ridgelines while gnomish flying machines sit parked along open landing strips. Mountaineers keep watch over the perimeter alongside engineers busy wrenching gears and inspecting steam-belching engines in the biting cold.

Ivar Patch. The Ivar Patch is a blighted pumpkin farm located in northern Silverpine Forest. Once a thriving agricultural homestead of Lordaeron, its residents were wiped out during the Third War and transformed into ravenous, mindlessly hostile ghouls. Before the Third War swept through Lordaeron, this pumpkin patch was a prosperous homestead owned by a farmer named Ivar, who employed a lively crew of farmhands and servants. When the Scourge unleashed the Plague of Undeath across the countryside, the farm was consumed completely. Rather than rising with their minds intact like the free-willed Forsaken, Ivar, his family, and his laborers were reduced to rotting, feral ghouls bound to prowl the ruined soil.

Jaggedswine Farm. Jaggedswine Farm is a modest livestock steading situated in northern Durotar, just south of the main entrance to Orgrimmar. Comprising a timber storage shed, a sprawling pen, and a muddy watering hole, it serves as a critical food source raising hardy swine for the nearby Horde capital. Carved out of Durotar's unforgiving, sunbaked earth, Jaggedswine Farm represents the harsh reality of sustaining an urban stronghold like Orgrimmar. The red soil of the region yields sparse agriculture, making robust livestock essential to feeding thousands of orcish warriors and laborers. The farm centers on a timber storehouse, a wide wooden pen, and a natural watering pond where swine are herded, bred, and butchered to keep the Horde's granaries stocked.

Jangolode Mine. Jangolode Mine is a rich mineral excavation located in the rolling hills of Westfall. Once a vital source of ore and raw materials for Stormwind City, the mine has been seized by the bandits of the Defias Brotherhood. Before Westfall fell into decline, the Jangolode Mine provided a steady flow of metals crucial to the reconstruction and supply of Stormwind City. As civil order deteriorated and the kingdom withdrew its garrisons, the Defias Brotherhood seized control of the site to feed their own operations. The bandits now work the rich veins for themselves, fiercely defending their subterranean prize.

Jansen Stead. Jansen Stead is the northernmost farmstead in Westfall, situated just down the road from the bridge to Elwynn Forest. Like much of the surrounding breadbasket, the homestead has fallen out of peasant hands and is swarming with rogue mechanical Harvest Watchers and roving Defias bandits. Positioned right past the Elwynn border, the Jansen Stead represents the harsh reality greeting anyone traveling westward into Westfall. Once a flourishing family farm feeding the kingdom, its rightful occupants have been driven away by the rising tide of unrest. In their place, hostile Harvest Watchers—malfunctioning clockwork automatons reprogrammed by the Defias Brotherhood—patrol the blighted fields alongside brigands. Its proximity to the main road makes it a prominent early hazard for couriers and travelers moving between Goldshire and Sentinel Hill.

Jasperlode Mine. Jasperlode Mine is an iron and mineral excavation in north-central Elwynn Forest that once supplied Stormwind City with vital resources. Today, the shafts are overrun by swarming kobolds and deadly giant spiders, leaving the resource-strapped kingdom unable to reclaim it. Jasperlode Mine was historically one of Stormwind's most productive mining operations, providing steady mineral wealth alongside nearby Fargodeep. With the kingdom's military stretched thin defending against external threats and unrest, local garrisons have been unable to protect the shafts. Kobolds seized the opportunity to burrow inside, driving human miners out and stockpiling stolen gold and tallow candles.

Jerod's Landing. Jerod's Landing is a modest river dock situated on the Elwynn Forest bank of the Nazferiti River. Currently seized by the Defias Brotherhood, the outpost serves as a clandestine transfer point for illicit shipments smuggled across the kingdom's waterways. Tucked away along the eastern waters of the Nazferiti River, Jerod's Landing provides river access connecting Elwynn Forest to neighboring territories. While originally an ordinary boat dock, the site has fallen firmly into the hands of the Defias Brotherhood. Under the watchful eye of a Defias dockmaster, outlaws utilize the dock as a hub to receive goods plundered from the Redridge Mountains, discreetly moving river cargo downstream toward holdings such as Klaven's Tower in Westfall.

Kargathia Keep. Kargathia Keep is a fortified Horde stronghold anchoring the eastern front of the Warsong Lumber Camp in Ashenvale. Serving as headquarters for the outpost's overseers, it guards the river border and ensures rapid reinforcement lines directly back to Orgrimmar. Perched on the eastern edge of the Warsong Lumber Camp just west of the Southfury River, Kargathia Keep serves as the command center for the Horde's logging operations in Ashenvale. Upgraded with heavy spiked barricades, this fortified outpost houses Overseer Gorthak and his officers. Its strategic position against the river border allows the Warsong clan to monitor incoming incursions and receive swift reinforcements directly from the neighboring lands of Durotar and Orgrimmar whenever night elf skirmishers strike.

Kharanos. Kharanos is a bustling mountain settlement nestled in the snowy heart of Dun Morogh, just down the road from Ironforge. Serving as the primary hub for travelers leaving Coldridge Valley, the town hosts a forge, gnomish workshops, and the famous Thunderbrew Distillery. Situated along the central road of Dun Morogh, Kharanos is the first true town welcoming recruits arriving from Anvilmar. Despite the biting cold and biting winds, the settlement thrives thanks to local dwarven grit and gnomish ingenuity. It centers around a roaring public forge and the Thunderbrew Distillery, renowned across the eastern mountains for producing some of the finest ale in Khaz Modan. Between bustling crafters and weary travelers seeking warmth, the town stands as the essential staging ground for business in the lower peaks.

Kodo Rock. Kodo Rock is a natural stone monument located in the plains of Red Cloud Mesa, between Camp Narache and Brambleblade Ravine. Standing quietly amid the grasses of Mulgore, it serves as an early pilgrimage site for young tauren shamans learning to commune with the spirits of the earth. Because of its modest silhouette against the rolling landscape, travelers must keep a keen eye out to spot it. Situated roughly halfway along the path connecting Camp Narache to the hostile quillboar territory of Brambleblade Ravine, Kodo Rock is marked by a patch of worn earth at its base. While it lacks the sheer grandeur of the towering bluffs surrounding Red Cloud Mesa, its distinct profile resembles the revered kodo beasts that wander the grasslands. For wandering tribesfolk, it acts as a quiet natural beacon in the windswept plains of Mulgore.

Kolkar Crag. Kolkar Crag is a sunbaked, jagged gorge in southern Durotar claimed by the hostile Kolkar centaur. Led by Warlord Kolkanis, this enclave serves as a staging ground for coordinated raids against nearby Horde settlements. Tucked away in the rugged canyons of southern Durotar, Kolkar Crag is a base of operations for the aggressive Kolkar clan. Despite the arid and unforgiving terrain, these centaur have fortified the natural choke points of the gorge. From this ravine, their scouts and marauders keep close watch over the surrounding flats, probing for vulnerabilities across orc and Darkspear holdings. For young warriors training in the Valley of Trials or patrolling the southern coast, Kolkar Crag represents the nearest organized front of centaur hostility.

Lake Al'Ameth. Lake Al'Ameth is one of the largest freshwater bodies nestled high in the boughs of Teldrassil, located just south of Dolanaar. Though once a tranquil haven featuring little more than a simple wooden jetty, its shores have grown perilous due to the violent agitation of the local plant life. Resting immediately south of the village of Dolanaar, Lake Al'Ameth serves as a vital natural basin in the heart of Teldrassil. Despite its serene waters and minimal settlement, peace here has evaporated. Swarms of agitated timberlings and timberling sprouts prowl the water's edge, driven mad by an unnatural sickness spreading through the world tree. Druids and researchers from Dolanaar frequently dispatch travelers to these shores to gather seeds and cull the aggressive creatures before the corruption spreads deeper into the surrounding forest.

Lake Everstill. Lake Everstill is the expansive azure body of water dominating the heart of the Redridge Mountains, flanking the town of Lakeshire. Once celebrated for tranquil fishing and clean mountain runoff, its shores and waters have lately turned treacherous due to aggressive murloc tribes and predatory lake beasts. Spanning the central basin of Redridge, Lake Everstill provides the scenic backdrop and vital waterway for the township of Lakeshire. Its crystal-clear waters drain eastward toward the looming heights of Stonewatch. Spanned by the town's central bridge, the lake has long sustained local trade and quiet anglers, though anyone walking the shoreline today will find its peaceful reputation thoroughly shattered by encroaching wilderness threats.

Lake Falathim. Lake Falathim is a tranquil body of water nestled in the forested hills of western Ashenvale, southwest of Maestra's Post. Revered for the constant touch of Elune's moonlight upon its surface day and night, it was once a beloved retreat for night elves. In recent days, however, aggressive murlocs have overrun its shores, turning a sacred haven into a perilous hazard. Tucked away southeast of the Zoram Strand, Lake Falathim was long cherished by the Kaldorei as a peaceful sanctuary for swimming and fishing. According to local lore, the gentle radiance of Elune rests upon these waters at all hours, day or night. Despite this sacred blessing, ferocious murlocs have surged inland to seize the shores, nesting in thick numbers and driving away local travelers and scholars alike.

Lakeridge Highway. Lakeridge Highway is an old thoroughfare running along the southern shore of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Once a vital and heavily traveled artery prior to the First War, it has fallen into ruin and disuse. Today, roving packs of gnolls and Blackrock orcs make passage along the road perilous for travelers. Before the devastation of the First War, the Lakeridge Highway served as a bustling trade corridor through Redridge, carrying goods and folk along the southern banks of Lake Everstill. In those peaceful days, travelers could journey between the valley settlements and the eastern heights under the protection of the Kingdom of Stormwind. That safety shattered when the Horde marched through the region, leaving eastern Redridge contested and desolate.

Lakeshire. Lakeshire is the primary human settlement in the Redridge Mountains, nestled along the northern shores of Lake Everstill. Led by Magistrate Solomon and guarded by Marshal Marris, the picturesque town is currently on the brink of collapse due to relentless assaults by Blackrock orcs, aggressive gnoll packs, and shoreline murlocs. Once a peaceful haven in the foothills east of Stormwind, Lakeshire has become the kingdom's most embattled frontier. The town's garrison at Stonewatch Keep was brutally overrun by Blackrock clan orcs sweeping down from the north, and dark wizardry has riled local Shadowhide gnoll packs into organized raiding parties. Blackrock saboteurs have even shattered parts of the Everstill Bridge, leaving Foreman Oslow and his crew struggling to repair the span while under constant threat of attack. With murlocs choking the lake's shores and gnolls stalking the high passes, Lakeshire's defenders are stretched to their breaking point.

Lakeshire Inn. The Lakeshire Inn is the social hub and primary refuge in the beleaguered town of Lakeshire. Situated in the heart of the Redridge Mountains, it provides warmth, ale, and safe lodging for local townsfolk and weary travelers contending with the surrounding perils. Perched on the shore of Lake Everstill, the Lakeshire Inn offers a brief respite from the gnoll bands and Blackrock orcs pressing in on the town. Despite Lakeshire's increasingly desperate military situation, the tavern maintains a cozy, bustling atmosphere. Barkeep Daniels and Innkeeper Brianna attend to the locals and travelers, serving up flagons of ale, wine, and warm meals. It is a vital meeting point where townspeople trade news, drown their sorrows, and seek hired blades to help defend the eastern border of the kingdom.

Lakeshire Town Hall. Lakeshire Town Hall serves as the administrative seat of the Redridge Mountains, standing at the heart of the lakeside settlement. Inside, Magistrate Solomon oversees local governance while wrestling with relentless threats from Blackrock orcs and gnolls. Lakeshire Town Hall is an aging stone structure that has been diligently refurbished multiple times over the years. Positioned prominently within Lakeshire, it houses Magistrate Solomon, a kind and dedicated civil leader tasked with maintaining order in the eastern reaches of the Kingdom of Stormwind. With Stormwind's military resources stretched thin and royal aid scarce, the hall has transformed from a quiet administrative office into an active command center where desperate appeals for volunteer defenders and mercenaries are processed daily.

Library (Ironforge). Tucked inside the eastern wing of the Hall of Explorers, the Library serves as Ironforge's foremost repository of historical knowledge, archeological relics, and ancient lore. Maintained diligently by the Explorers' League, it houses extensive historical tomes alongside rare artifacts recovered from digs across Azeroth. Occupying a massive chamber within the Hall of Explorers, the Library is where dwarven scholars sift through the relics and field reports recovered by adventurers across the world. Administered by the Explorers' League, the shelves are packed with foundational chronicles detailing the War of the Three Hammers, the ancient Troll Wars, and the origins of the dwarven race. Inquiries regarding rare books or archival locations are directed to Librarian Mae Paledust.

Library Wing (Northshire). The Library Wing is the quiet, book-lined southern wing of Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest. It serves as a sanctuary for scholars, offering early instruction to fledgling priests and mages joining the defense of Stormwind. Branching south from the Main Hall of Northshire Abbey, the Library Wing houses dusty shelves, study lecterns, and quiet alcoves dedicated to intellectual and spiritual training. While martial recruits drill in the northern Hall of Arms, aspiring mages and priests gather here to grasp the fundamentals of the Arcane and the Holy Light. Currently, Priestess Anetta guides novice priests in matters of faith and healing, while Khelden Bremen teaches budding mages how to shape primal elemental energy.

Lion's Pride Inn. The Lion's Pride Inn is the bustling tavern and community center of Goldshire in Elwynn Forest. Kept for generations by the Farley family, it serves as the primary resting place, meeting hall, and hiring house for travelers venturing just south of Stormwind City. Standing at the crossroads of Elwynn Forest, the Lion's Pride Inn is Goldshire's lively centerpiece. Operated by Innkeeper Farley under the tavern's traditional motto—'Rest and relaxation for the tired and cold'—the inn offers warm hearths, strong drinks, and rooms for weary adventurers fresh out of Northshire. Farley's family has managed the establishment with pride for generations, dating back through the reign of King Llane Wrynn I. Because Goldshire lies along the vital trade routes between Stormwind, Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood, the tavern serves as an indispensable rallying point where town marshals, local crafters, and seasoned trainers gather to share news and contract passing mercenaries.

Long Wash. The Long Wash is a bleak, windswept stretch of beach in Darkshore running just south of Auberdine toward the ruins of Ameth'Aran. Gloomy and scattered with marine carcasses and flotsam, the shoreline has recently grown dangerous due to an increasing presence of hostile murlocs. Despite its name, the Long Wash is actually the shortest distinct stretch of coastline in Darkshore. It sits under the region's perpetual overcast skies, an expanse of damp sand littered with flotsam, beached driftwood, and the carcasses of sea creatures washed up by the Veiled Sea. While local crabs and snails comb through the surf, travelers southward from Auberdine must tread cautiously: murloc tribes have established camps along the water's edge, aggressively attacking anyone encroaching on their scavenged territory.

Longshore. The Longshore is the expansive sandy coastline stretching along the entire western edge of Westfall. Despite its vast and scenic expanse, the shore is notoriously hazardous due to thick populations of aggressive murlocs and scattered wrecks off the coast. Running the full western length of Westfall, the Longshore is one of the widest unbroken beaches in the Eastern Kingdoms. Yet it offers little peace to travelers. Coastal murlocs dominate the surf, led by notorious terrors like Old Murk-Eye, while the remnants of sunken vessels—including ruined elven destroyers—litter the shallows. Near the southern reaches, isolated settlers like Daphne Stilwell struggle against marauding Defias bandits, standing within sight of the Westfall Lighthouse across the water.

Lordamere Lake. Lordamere Lake is one of the largest bodies of freshwater in the Eastern Kingdoms, bordered by Tirisfal Glades, Silverpine Forest, and the Alterac Mountains. Once the bustling aquatic heart of human civilization in the north, its cold waters and islands are now haunted by Scourge necromancers, feral murlocs, and the spreading shadow of the undead. In the golden age of the Alliance of Lordaeron, Lordamere Lake sat at the crossroads of human power. The Capital City of Lordaeron guarded its northern shores, the sorcerous city-state of Dalaran rose near its southern reach, and the kingdom of Alterac lined its mountainous eastern edge. Merchant vessels and fishing boats once crossed its broad, mist-covered expanse without fear. Following the devastation of the Third War, the lake was transformed from a hub of commerce into a natural barrier dividing the Forsaken-held lands of Tirisfal and Silverpine from the treacherous heights of Alterac.

Lushwater Oasis. Lushwater Oasis is one of the three life-giving watering holes nestled in the arid Barrens, located just south of the Crossroads. Despite its verdant appearance, the oasis is fraught with danger, infested by aggressive Kolkar centaur and harboring the entrance to the Wailing Caverns. Its tainted waters are well-known to anglers seeking the peculiar Deviate Fish. Situated a short march south of the Crossroads, Lushwater Oasis offers a deceptive respite amid the sun-bleached expanse of the Barrens. While its palm canopies and fresh springs draw thirsty beasts from across the savanna, Kolkar centaur claim the banks, lying in wait to butcher both game and unwary travelers. The oasis is also the gateway to the Wailing Caverns, whose sprawling underground networks seep corruptive energies into the pools above, breeding unnatural wildlife and bizarre mutations.

Maclure Vineyards. Maclure Vineyards is a sprawling agricultural estate in southern Elwynn Forest owned by the Maclure family. While known for producing grapes and wine for the kingdom of Stormwind, the farmstead is equally infamous for an ongoing, bitter feud with the neighboring Stonefield family. Nestled in the lush hills of southern Elwynn Forest, the Maclure Vineyards should be a peaceful haven of winecraft and farming. Instead, everyday labor is overshadowed by a vicious, long-standing rivalry with the Stonefields just down the road. Accusations of theft and bad blood run deep between the households, keeping tempers flaring even as common troubles—like hungry prowling boars and encroaching kobolds—threaten both homesteads.

Maestra's Post. Maestra's Post is a small Alliance settlement in western Ashenvale, perched along the road northwest of Astranaar and south of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran. Guarded by night elven Sentinels and hosting a rare human presence in Kalimdor's ancient forest, it serves as a forward watch against encroaching threats. Positioned under the canopy of western Ashenvale, Maestra's Post consists of a slender night elven tower and an open lodge. It sits as an essential waypoint for travelers marching between the coast of Darkshore and the larger hub of Astranaar. Despite its tranquil elven architecture, the outpost stands perpetually on edge. The local Sentinels keep a wary eye on the surrounding wilderness, where corrupted furbolg stir and nearby Horde movements constantly threaten the Alliance's supply lines.

Mage Quarter. The Mage Quarter forms the arcane heart of Stormwind City, resting across the canals in the capital's southwestern corner. Towering over its cobblestone streets and esoteric specialty shops stands the Wizard's Sanctum, where the kingdom's conjurers hone their craft. Beneath the district's scholarly surface also lie shadowy recesses, harboring practitioners of far darker arts. Reachable by bridges crossing the canals from Cathedral Square or the Trade District, the Mage Quarter caters entirely to the mystical needs of the Alliance. Centered around the spire of the Wizard's Sanctum, human and allied spellcasters gather to study the weave of arcane magic and train apprentices. The surrounding streets are crowded with purveyors of tailoring cloth, reagents, alchemical supplies, and enchanted staves, creating an insular district dedicated to research and the defense of the kingdom.

Magic Quarter. The Magic Quarter is the northeastern district of the Undercity, serving as the center for Forsaken arcane study and dark spellcraft. Dominated by an ominous Temple of the Damned, the quarter houses practitioners of both the arcane and fel arts. Occupying the northeastern quadrant of the subterranean city, the Magic Quarter is where the Forsaken preserve their arcane heritage and delve into darker methodologies. The centerpiece of the district is a looming Temple of the Damned, an architectural relic of Scourge design that has been repurposed by the free-willed undead. Beneath its vaulted, shadowy ceilings, mages practice subtle manipulations of magical energies alongside warlocks communing with demonic entities, making the quarter the nexus of intellectual power and occult research in Lordaeron.

Main Hall (Northshire). The Main Hall is the central entrance chamber of Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest. It serves as the primary crossroads connecting the abbey's grounds to its upper tower, the Hall of Arms, and the Library Wing. Here, newly recruited human adventurers report to receive their initial assignments in service of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Stepping through the grand archways of Northshire Abbey brings visitors directly into the Main Hall. As the building's central hub, it channels arriving trainees and clerical staff between the abbey's distinct wings: the martial Hall of Arms on one side, the scholastic Library Wing on the other, and the stairs rising into the abbey tower. The quiet sanctuary of the hall is tempered by the ongoing strife in the valley, as officers rally able-bodied newcomers to defend the kingdom's borders.

Malaka'jin. Malaka'jin is a small Horde encampment nestled in the lower hills of the Stonetalon Mountains, just south of the Grimtotem Post. Inhabited primarily by Darkspear troll hunters, the settlement serves as a rustic waystation and hunting outpost for travelers ascending into the rugged peaks from the Barrens. Tucked away near the main path into the Stonetalon Mountains, Malaka'jin provides a welcome sanctuary for Horde wanderers venturing into contested heights. The village is home to a band of rugged troll hunters who eke out a living off the crags and scrublands. While living modestly, these hunters offer supplies, trade their fresh game to weary adventurers, and keep a wary eye on the hostile mountain wildlife and the belligerent Grimtotem tauren lurking further up the trails.

Malden's Orchard. Malden's Orchard is a ruined farmstead in northern Silverpine Forest, named after the human owner who fled during the Scourge invasion of Lordaeron. Long abandoned, its dark evergreen trees sit overgrown while vicious black worgs stalk the grounds. The orchard's crumbling cottage served as a temporary refuge for a stranded Forsaken scout cut off from his unit. Before the Third War, this homestead supplied fresh fruit to the towns of Lordaeron, tended by a farmer named Malden. When the Scourge tore through the kingdom, Malden abandoned his land to flee the plague. In the years since, the orchard has choked under the dark, encroaching mists of Silverpine Forest. The evergreen trees remain unpruned and their fruit rots ungathered on blighted boughs, leaving the plot entirely reclaimed by wild predators.

Manor Mistmantle. Manor Mistmantle is a decaying estate nestled in the shadowed hills of northeastern Duskwood, north of Darkshire. Once a proper family homestead, it has fallen into ruin and horror, crawling with undead ghouls bound to its infamous master. Located west of Beggar's Haunt, Manor Mistmantle stands as a grim monument to murder and madness. The grounds are choked with decay and prowled by vicious ghouls who defend the ruined structure. Amidst the rot and withered vegetation, the only sign of living beauty on the entire property is a solitary, sorrowful blossom growing in the untended garden: the flower known as the Tear of Tilloa.

Mast Room. The Mast Room is a cavernous subterranean lumber mill nestled deep within the Deadmines. Overseen by the goblin taskmaster Sneed and his woodcarvers, this chamber processes timber stripped from Westfall to construct Edwin VanCleef's secret juggernaut.

Master's Glaive. The Master's Glaive is an ancient, unsettling landmark tucked into southwestern Darkshore where a colossal adamantine weapon stands impaled in a massive petrified skull. Long revered by local night elves as a sacred mystery, the site now swarms with Twilight's Hammer cultists drawn to the lingering malevolence of an ancient entity. Rising out of the Darkshore earth, the Master's Glaive is a massive adamantine blade buried deep in a colossal petrified skull. No record names the creature that died here or the hand that drove the blade home. Onu, the Ancient of Lore, says only that an old, old lord of the earth fell on this spot, and the night elves long believed that only the titans could have wielded so gigantic a weapon. Today, the impaled monolith stands as a stark, petrified monument to that forgotten struggle.

Menethil Harbor. Menethil Harbor is a heavily fortified dwarven port town perched on an island off the western shore of the Wetlands. Built over an old Orcish shipyard and named after King Terenas Menethil II, it acts as the primary maritime lifeline connecting the Eastern Kingdoms to the distant shores of Kalimdor. Sheltered behind massive stone battlements and the sturdy towers of Menethil Keep, it is a bustling hub for merchants, off-duty soldiers, and salty adventurers. The site of Menethil Harbor first served Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer during the Second War, when the Horde constructed an invasion armada out of timber and iron ransacked from Khaz Modan. After the orcs were routed, Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore oversaw the rebuilding of the anchorage into a premier Alliance haven, naming it in tribute to the late King Terenas Menethil II of Lordaeron. Despite its remote marshland setting, it remains a heavily defended bastion, reinforced by massive walls, a single bridged causeway, and the four stone watchtowers of Menethil Keep.

Merchant Coast. The Merchant Coast is the stretch of eastern shoreline in the Barrens bordering the Great Sea. Dominated by the bustling goblin port of Ratchet, the coast derives its name from lucrative sea trade, though it remains constantly contested by pirates. Running along the eastern edge of the Barrens, the Merchant Coast serves as a vital maritime artery connecting central Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms and Theramore. Its name honors the industrious goblin traders of the Steamwheedle Cartel, whose neutral port of Ratchet handles cargo for anyone with coin. However, the open sea lanes attract more than merchant vessels: Southsea Freebooters prowl the sands and nearby waters, preying on merchant ships and setting up illicit operations along the beaches.

Military Ward. The Military Ward serves as the martial heart of Ironforge, housing the city's command infrastructure, weapons masters, and barracks. Marked by bold red banners, it is where dwarven soldiers, hunters, and siege engineers train alongside mechanized siege engines and flying machines. Situated within the northern perimeter of the mountain fortress, the Military Ward concentrates Ironforge's defensive forces into a bustling staging ground. The central complex, the Hall of Arms, accommodates warrior and hunter trainers, battlemasters, and hangars housing dwarven flying machines and steam tanks. Surrounding the drill squares and training dummies are supply outlets such as Craghelm's Plate and Chain, Goldfury's Hunting Supplies, and Timberline Arms, making the ward the primary staging point for mountaineers and city defenders.

Mirage Raceway. The Mirage Raceway is an impromptu engineering proving ground situated in the shimmering salt flats of Thousand Needles. Founded on the heated rivalry between goblin tinkerer Pozzik and gnome engineer Fizzle Brassbolts, it pits high-speed rocket cars against one another across the baked earth. The track serves as a neutral gathering place where members of both the Alliance and Horde come to wager, tinker, and cheer on their favored machines. Sprawled across the vast white desert floor of the Shimmering Flats, the Mirage Raceway was born out of an unrelenting grudge match between two master tinkerers: the goblin Pozzik and the gnome Fizzle Brassbolts. Determined to settle once and for all whose race possesses superior technical ingenuity, the two constructed custom rocket-powered drag cars and recruited rival crews to pit them against each other in daily high-velocity showdowns. The relentless competition has turned the barren flats into a bustling hub of invention, sabotage, and testing as each crew desperately looks for any mechanical advantage.

Mirkfallon Lake. Mirkfallon Lake sits in a central highland basin in the Stonetalon Mountains, nestled beneath the sheer cliffs of Windshear Crag. Its waters and surrounding banks teem with native wildlife, including aggressive slimes, roaming thunder lizards, and descending wyverns. Positioned at the geographic center of the Stonetalon range, Mirkfallon Lake rests between the mountain passes leading south toward the Webwinder Path and north toward Stonetalon Peak. Fed by highland runoff, the lake offers a fertile oasis amidst the craggy peaks, drawing thunder lizards down to drink and wyverns from their roosts high above. The waters are also inhabited by strange, bubbling slimes, turning an otherwise serene mountain tarn into a hazardous crossing for lone travelers.

Mirror Lake. Mirror Lake is a picturesque body of water tucked into northwestern Elwynn Forest near an orchard. Fed by a gentle waterfall beneath the cliffs of Stormwind, its tranquil surface belies the dangers lurking on its shores, from prowling Defias bandits to strange disruptions in the local ley lines. Situated beneath the towering ramparts of Stormwind City, Mirror Lake ought to be a peaceful retreat for fishermen and weary travelers. Instead, brigands of the Defias Brotherhood stalk the surrounding orchards, making any prolonged stay perilous for passing locals. Worse still, mystical disturbances across Azeroth have begun warping the natural channels of arcane energy throughout the forest. The mages of the Wizard's Sanctum keep a cautious eye on the lake, sending practitioners to sample its currents and ensure that downstream communities are not poisoned by chaotic arcane runoff.

Mirror Lake Orchard. Mirror Lake Orchard is a quiet grove and cottage nestled on the southern banks of Mirror Lake in western Elwynn Forest. Once a peaceful homestead near Thunder Falls, it has fallen into the hands of Defias bandits who exploit the countryside while Stormwind's guards look elsewhere. Tucked away near the cascading waters of Thunder Falls, Mirror Lake Orchard was once a productive farmstead benefiting from the clean waters of Mirror Lake. Today, the peaceful cottage sits overrun, claimed by opportunistic thieves and brigands flying the colors of the Defias Brotherhood. With the kingdom's military stretched thin and King Varian Wrynn missing, rural properties like this orchard have become easy pickings for outlaws looking to secure hideouts across the Elwynn countryside.

Mist's Edge. Mist's Edge is the long, windswept coastline spanning the western border of Darkshore. Shrouded in damp ocean fog, these gray beaches are littered with shipwrecks, colossal sea creature remains, and roving packs of crabs and murlocs. Running along the western edge of Darkshore, Mist's Edge is defined by damp sands, rocky tidepools, and perpetual coastal fog. The beach is a graveyard of the sea, littered with decaying sea behemoths, drift timber, and the shattered ribs of wrecked vessels. While seemingly barren, the coastline teems with shoreline scavengers, notably aggressive crabs and territorial murloc tribes that nest in the surf.

Misty Pine Refuge. Misty Pine Refuge is a small outpost building of the Argent Dawn tucked amidst the frigid snows of central Dun Morogh. Situated amid the windswept hills of Dun Morogh, Misty Pine Refuge is an unassuming outpost of the Argent Dawn in the dwarven realm. While the surrounding crags are patrolled by Ironforge mountaineers, the refuge is home to Father Gavin, the order's lone agent here, who offers a quiet hearth amid the bitter elements and the perils that threaten the mountain roads.

Mo'grosh Stronghold. Mo'grosh Stronghold is a fortified den of ogres dug into the northeastern hills of Loch Modan. Nestled among ancient, weathered ruins, these brutal giants pose a constant threat to the dwarven settlements below. Tucked away in the crags of northeastern Loch Modan, Mo'grosh Stronghold serves as the primary base for the Mo'grosh clan of ogres in the region. The brute forces lurking within the caves and outer camps raid traveling dwarven supply caravans and present an enduring danger to the peace of Thelsamar. The rugged stonework scattered around the camp suggests the site once belonged to an older settlement, before the lumbering ogres claimed the territory and raised their distinctive mounds.

Molsen Farm. Molsen Farm is an abandoned homestead located in the breadbasket region of Westfall. Once a fertile piece of farmland feeding Stormwind, it has fallen into ruin following the rise of the Defias Brotherhood and the prowling mechanical harvest golems left in their wake. Like many homesteads across Westfall, Molsen Farm stands as a casualty of the kingdom's neglect and criminal uprising. When the Defias Brotherhood took control of the countryside, the resident farmers were driven out or worse, abandoning their crops and buildings. Now, instead of laborers gathering grain, hostile mechanical Harvest Watchers and wandering outlaws scour the untended fields, making the farm a hazard to anyone traveling through the province.

Moonbrook. Once a bustling agricultural hub and mining town in southwestern Westfall, Moonbrook now stands as a lawless ghost town. The town has been completely overrun by the Defias Brotherhood, who use it as a fortified screen to hide their subterranean headquarters in the Deadmines. Before the First War, Moonbrook was a vital community at the center of Westfall's breadbasket, supporting local farming families and the lucrative gold shafts of the Deadmines. Though it was razed by the Old Horde and painstakingly rebuilt after the Second War, its peace did not last. Neglected by the House of Nobles in Stormwind and stripped of military protection, the settlement could not resist the vengeful Stonemasons Guild when they fled into the wilderness. Bandits drove out the honest homesteaders, forcing citizens and teachers alike to flee toward Sentinel Hill and Elwynn Forest.

Moonbrook Schoolhouse. Standing in the northwestern corner of Moonbrook, the Schoolhouse is a prominent building resembling a town hall with a small graveyard behind it. Originally erected to educate local children under headmaster Stalvan Mistmantle, it now stands derelict amidst the Defias occupation of Westfall. Before Moonbrook fell to ruin and bandits, the community invested in the education of its youth by raising this grand schoolhouse. Stalvan Mistmantle, an educated scholar from the north, was invited to Westfall specifically to serve as its headmaster. In those brighter days, the hall bustled with students rather than thieves, standing as proof of Moonbrook's former prosperity. Now, the schoolhouse lies abandoned to the elements and infested with outlaws, while the weathered headstones of its rear cemetery silently oversee Westfall's steady decay.

Moonshrine Ruins. The Moonshrine Ruins are a flooded expanse of ancient night elven architecture deep within Blackfathom Deeps. Once dedicated to the worship of Elune, these crumbling halls have been desecrated and seized by the Twilight's Hammer cult. Past the cavernous Pool of Ask'ar lies the Moonshrine Ruins, a somber testament to the night elves' ancient past along the Ashenvale coast. These partially submerged halls once rang with chants honoring the Moon Goddess Elune, but the Great Sundering shattered the temple and drowned its lower levels in sea water. Today, the murky waters churn with feral aquatic beasts, from aggressive crabs to serpentine threshadons, while the Twilight's Hammer cult maintains an active presence throughout the stones, bent on dark rituals that mock the shrine's sacred origin.

Moonspray. The Moonspray is an Alliance transport vessel belonging to the Kaldorei Fleet. It provides essential maritime passage across the waters separating mainland Kalimdor from the great World Tree, Teldrassil. The Moonspray serves as an indispensable lifeline between the docks of Auberdine on Darkshore's coast and Rut'theran Village at the root of Teldrassil. Traversing the Veiled Sea, the transport carries adventurers, couriers, and vital provisions between the isolated night elf sanctuary in the crown of the World Tree and the ancient mainland of Kalimdor.

Moonwell (Ashenvale). This secluded shrine, known to the night elves as the Moonwell of Purity, rests in central Ashenvale east of Iris Lake and west of Raynewood Retreat. Its blessed waters channel the grace of Elune to nourish the ancient forest and cleanse creeping foulness from the land. Alliance travelers and night elf sentinels often seek out its tranquil basin to purify corrupted artifacts found in the woodland. Tucked away beneath the canopy of central Ashenvale, this moonwell serves as a spiritual anchor for the kaldorei. Its luminescent waters tap into nature's latent magic and the light of the Moon Goddess. As the surrounding forest suffers from satyr corruption, fel taint, and logging incursions, pure shrines like this one become vital lifelines for those trying to heal the woods.

Mor'shan Rampart. The Mor'shan Rampart is a heavily fortified Horde barricade positioned at the northern border of the Barrens, guarding the entrance to Ashenvale. Constructed primarily by the Warsong clan, it shields Horde territory from night elf counterattacks while serving as a staging ground for incursions deeper into the forest. Standing at the northern terminus of the Gold Road, the Mor'shan Rampart marks the transition between the arid plains of the Barrens and the ancient canopies of Ashenvale. Built from heavy timber, defensive palisades, and fortified watchtowers, this bulwark was raised to stem the retaliatory strikes of night elven forces outraged by the Horde's logging operations. It acts both as a shield securing the northern gate to Kalimdor's interior and as a forward staging post for raiding parties pushing north toward Astranaar.

Mortwake's Tower. Mortwake's Tower, commonly known as Klaven's Tower or simply the Defias Tower, is a fortified watchtower standing near the river in southeastern Westfall. Commanded by the rogue Klaven Mortwake, it serves as a critical waypoint for smuggling stolen goods across kingdom borders. Perched on the borderlands north of the Dagger Hills, Klaven's Tower is a vital hub for Defias Brotherhood operations in southern Westfall. Together with Jerod's Landing across the river in Elwynn Forest, the site acts as a receiving post and staging ground for contraband plundered from the Redridge Mountains. Its commanding vantage over the waterways allows the Brotherhood to slip supplies past Kingdom patrols, shielding their logistical network from the crown's eyes.

Mystic Ward. The Mystic Ward is the northwestern district of Ironforge, serving as the dwarven capital's quiet sanctuary for spiritual devotion and arcane study. Distinguishable by its cool, pale blue banners and quiet halls, it stands in stark contrast to the clanging anvils of the nearby Great Forge. Its grandest structure, the Hall of Mysteries, gathers priests, paladins, and mages beneath cavernous stone arches. While dwarves are famed across Azeroth for their prowess at the forge and on the battlefield, the Mystic Ward represents the kingdom's quieter intellectual and spiritual pursuits. Marked by pale blue heraldry, this cavernous quarter connects the bustling Commons to the Forlorn Cavern and the Great Forge. Within its reaches, merchants supply scholars and spellweavers with regalia, scrolls, and alchemical reagents from shops like The Fighting Wizard and Maeva's Mystical Apparel. Dominating the district is the majestic Hall of Mysteries, where the holy disciplines of the Holy Light intersect with the practiced arts of arcane magic, offering guidance to those who wield unseen powers in defense of the Alliance.

Mystral Lake. Mystral Lake is the largest body of water in Ashenvale, resting in the south-central forest just below Silverwind Refuge. Once a tranquil sanctuary guarded by water elementals loyal to the night elves, its waters have become fraught with danger due to corruption of the local elementals. Spanning a vast expanse south of Silverwind Refuge and east of Talondeep Vale, Mystral Lake was long cherished by the kaldorei for its pure waters and peaceful guardian elementals. However, dark interference has broken that ancient peace. The rogue mage Sarilus Foulborne turned his arts upon the lake's water spirits, corrupting them into hostile, violent entities. Today, travelers from both the Horde and Alliance frequently find their journeys pulling them to these troubled shores, contending with the wrath of spirits that once sheltered the woods.

Night Run. Night Run is a small, secluded satyr outpost perched atop a cliff-ringed bluff in east-central Ashenvale. Inhabited by the demonic Felmusk satyr, it serves as a corrupted encampment harboring dark soul magic within ancient elven ruins. Night Run is the smallest and most isolated of Ashenvale's three major satyr strongholds, alongside Xavian and Satyrnaar. Sheltered among crumbling elven stonework and broken pillars, the settlement juts outward on a high ridge bounded by steep, impassable cliffs. Reaching it requires a circuitous trek along the Falfarren River near the waters of Xavian or navigating a precarious northern ledge above Raynewood Retreat. Despite its modest size, the enclave poses a severe danger: the Felmusk satyr who dwell here work in concert with the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand, anchoring twisted soulgems to pool demonic essence within the forest.

Night Web's Hollow. Night Web's Hollow is a sunken vale and abandoned gold mine located just northwest of Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. Heavily overrun with arachnids, it serves as a testing ground for freshly awakened Forsaken sent to cull the vermin and prove their combat readiness. Tucked away in the northern hills of Deathknell, Night Web's Hollow was once an ordinary human gold mine before the plague swept through Lordaeron. In the aftermath of the kingdom's fall, the shafts were entirely abandoned to nature. Today, thick strands of webbing shroud the rock walls and suffocating shadows conceal a thriving colony of aggressive night web spiders. Freshly raised Forsaken are routinely dispatched into the hollow and its subterranean tunnels to cull the hatchlings, slay their voracious matriarch, and harden their resolve before moving onward into Tirisfal Glades.

Nightmare Vale. Nightmare Vale is a shadowed hollow nestled in southwestern Tirisfal Glades, just west of the Crusader's Outpost. Once a lush forest haven, its trees have withered under the blight, and vicious predators now roam among the twisted trunks. Before the Third War, this valley was a verdant part of the Tirisfal countryside, filled with songbirds and standard woodland game. In the wake of the Scourge's plague, the vegetation has blackened and rotted away. Ravenous darkhounds and massive vampire bats have devoured the native wildlife, turning the hollow into a grim haven for scavengers and beasts of prey.

Nightsong Woods. Nightsong Woods forms the embattled eastern expanse of Ashenvale, reaching from Raynewood Retreat toward the borders of Azshara. It serves as the primary battleground between the night elves defending their sacred forest and the Warsong clan harvesting lumber for the Horde. Across its shadowed glades, ancient groves clash with fortified encampments amidst persistent demonic corruption. Stretching eastward across Ashenvale to Azshara, Nightsong Woods is defined by escalating violence. The Falfarren River bisects the western reaches, creating a volatile boundary between Alliance settlements and Horde encroachments. Further east, the forest fractures into heavily disputed territories where Splintertree Post coordinates Horde campaigns against the Silverwing Sentinels. Orcish axes continuously clear southern groves to fuel the Horde's expansion, leaving clear-cut swaths that infuriate the Kaldorei. Adding to the peril, satyr strongholds like Satyrnaar and Xavian, alongside demonic remnants in Demon Fall Canyon and Felfire Hill, taint the eastern canopies.

North Coast. The North Coast is a bleak, fog-shrouded stretch of shoreline marking the northern edge of Tirisfal Glades along the Great Sea. Tainted by the fall of Lordaeron, the cold beaches are littered with rotting marine life and aggressively defended by tribes of hostile murlocs. Before the Third War, these northern waters and stony beaches were part of the peaceful northern boundary of Lordaeron. When the Plague of Undeath swept across the continent, its corrupting blight seeped down the bluffs and poisoned the coast. The waters turned chill and murky, washing up the carcasses of giant sea creatures that now rot upon the sand amid the perennial coastal fog.

North Gate Outpost. North Gate Outpost is a fortified dwarven camp situated high in the North Gate Pass of Dun Morogh. Manning the rugged route between Ironforge's snowy heartland and Loch Modan, its mountaineers guard travelers against the hostile wildlife that infests the crags. Positioned in the middle of North Gate Pass, this small settlement serves as the northeastern threshold of Dun Morogh. Dwarven mountaineers stationed here keep the main roadway cleared of prowling beasts and monitor traffic heading through the mountain tunnels into Loch Modan. The harsh climate and steep ravines make patrol duty treacherous, and the garrison frequently calls upon travelers to scout the surrounding ridges for missing patrols and dangerous predators.

North Gate Pass. North Gate Pass is a vital mountain thoroughfare connecting the snowy crags of Dun Morogh with the rolling basin of Loch Modan. It forms the northern corridor through the Khaz Modan peaks, watched over by a fortified dwarven outpost. Travelers heading toward the northern lowlands of the Wetlands frequently traverse this high road. Carved into the sheer stone of Khaz Modan, North Gate Pass serves as the northern arterial link between the high, frozen valleys of Dun Morogh and the temperate waters of Loch Modan. Descending through steep mountain tunnels, travelers emerging from the west are greeted by the broad expanse of the loch valley. Because it sits within easy striking distance of the paths heading down into the Wetlands, the pass carries heavy traffic of dwarven messengers, merchants, and roaming adventurers. Its strategic value is anchored by the North Gate Outpost, where mountaineers keep vigilant watch against troggs and mountain predators.

North Tide's Hollow. North Tide's Hollow is a rugged wilderness pocket in Silverpine Forest located just north of the Sepulcher. Haunted by feral Moonrage worgen loyal to the rogue Archmage Arugal, the clearing serves as a base of operations for the beasts stalking the coastal woods. Tucked away in the dense timber north of the Forsaken settlement of the Sepulcher, North Tide's Hollow is dominated by the savage Moonrage pack. These feral worgen, brought into Lordaeron through the reckless sorcery of Archmage Arugal, have established crude encampments throughout the hollow. Built with only the barest necessities required by the hardy beasts, these rough shelters provide a forward staging ground dangerously close to Forsaken travel routes.

North Tide's Run. North Tide's Run is the windswept northwestern shoreline of Silverpine Forest, skirting the edge of the Great Sea. Marked by a lonely campfire and a half-sunken shipwreck, this stretch of sand is known as a secluded trial ground for traveling druids seeking harmony with the waters. Stretching along the northwest edge of Silverpine Forest, North Tide's Run consists of cold sand, pounding surf, and a strip of the Great Sea. Its most unmistakable landmark is a partially submerged shipwreck tilted precariously in the shallows near the beach. Aside from the wreckage, the only sign of habitation is a humble campfire tended by Wallace the Blind, who keeps a quiet vigil beside the lapping tide.

Northshire Abbey. Northshire Abbey is a historic monastery nestled in Northshire Valley within the northern foothills of Elwynn Forest. Rebuilt after its destruction in the First War, it serves as the spiritual heart of the Brotherhood of Northshire and a premier training center for new defenders answering the kingdom of Stormwind's call. Centuries ago, clerics from Lordaeron traveled south into the kingdom of Stormwind to spread the worship of the Holy Light, establishing the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics and their abbey. The monastery quickly became an anchor of kingdom life, caring for the sick and even tending to the young Guardian Medivh during his years in a coma. During the First War, the abbey suffered repeated assaults by brigands and the Orcish Horde, culminating in its utter destruction. When the Alliance of Lordaeron liberated the region in the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol helped rebuild the sanctuary, refounding its protectors as the Brotherhood of Northshire.

What is the Brotherhood of Northshire? The Brotherhood of Northshire is a religious order of clerics, priests, and paladins based out of Northshire Abbey. Originally founded centuries ago by missioning clerics from Lordaeron, it was re-established by Archbishop Alonsus Faol after the First War to train faithful defenders and preserve sacred scripture.

Why was Northshire Abbey destroyed in the First War? During the First War, the abbey held strategic and spiritual importance for Stormwind. Orcish forces incited human brigands to attack it, and after the half-orc Garona was briefly held captive there, a massive Horde onslaught leveled the holy grounds. It remained ruined throughout the war until the Alliance drove out the orcish clans and rebuilt it.

Why are there Defias bandits and kobolds outside the abbey? Stormwind's military is stretched thin protecting distant borders, leaving outlying regions poorly guarded. Opportunistic kobolds have infested the local gold mines, while the Defias Brotherhood exploits the gaps to rob travelers, harass the local vineyards, and raid the abbey's library for arcane tomes and holy relics.

What is the connection between Northshire Abbey and the Deadmines? During the First War, an ogre chieftain named Turok stole the sacred Tome of Divinity from Northshire Abbey and retreated into the Deadmines. Sir Anduin Lothar led an expedition into the depths to recover the holy scripture, getting trapped until a royal rescue party saved him and returned the tome to the abbey's care.

Northshire Valley. Tucked away in the northern mountains of Elwynn Forest, Northshire Valley serves as the peaceful cradle and training ground for the kingdom of Stormwind's newest defenders. Surrounded by natural barriers, it hosts the historic Northshire Abbey, fertile vineyards, and the rich Echo Ridge Mine. Despite its tranquil appearance, the valley faces mounting unrest from rogue bandits, infesting kobolds, and displaced predators. Northshire Valley is framed by nearly impassable mountain ridges, with its only road heading south through a fortified gatehouse toward Goldshire and the rest of Elwynn Forest. A clear river winds through its pastures before feeding south into Crystal Lake. At the valley's heart stands Northshire Abbey, an ancient sanctuary where the Holy Light is taught and where recruits are trained by the Knights of the Silver Hand and seasoned veterans. Beyond the abbey walls lie the bountiful Northshire Vineyards and Echo Ridge Mine, forming a self-sustaining pocket of Stormwind territory that feels far removed from the wider world's wars.

Northshire Vineyards. The Northshire Vineyards are cultivated grape fields lying just east of Northshire Abbey in the valley's sheltered basin. Though once a peaceful source of wine for the clerics, the fields have fallen under the control of the Defias Brotherhood and their local brigands. Located east across the stream from Northshire Abbey, the Northshire Vineyards represent the valley's quiet agrarian life. The fields are tended by local workers like Milly Osworth, but rising civil unrest has left them unprotected. Bandits aligned with the Defias Brotherhood, led on the ground by a cutthroat named Garrick Padfoot, have seized the acreage. Rather than mere vandalism, the thieves occupy the fields to plunder the harvest and strip the local farmers of their livelihood, providing new recruits to the Brotherhood an easy foothold right under the abbey's nose.

Old Ironforge. Old Ironforge, also called the Assembly of Thanes, is an ancient subterranean chamber lying directly beneath the High Seat of Ironforge. Carved deep into the mountain's roots above glowing magma veins, it represents the ancestral heart of the dwarven capital. In the present day, its heavy access gates in the royal throne room remain sealed and vigilantly guarded. Beneath King Magni Bronzebeard's throne in the High Seat rests the cavernous hall known as Old Ironforge or the Assembly of Thanes. Deep inside these fiery subterranean foundations, winding stone bridges cross pools of subterranean lava. Long before the bustling halls of the Great Forge and the Commons echoed with modern dwarven commerce, early thanes gathered in these cavernous depths to deliberate and govern the mountain kingdom.

Old Town. Old Town is the oldest and grittiest quarter of Stormwind City, having largely survived the destruction of the First War intact. Rather than gleaming stone plazas, its narrow alleys feature weathered brick, working-class tenements, and bustling military facilities. It serves as home to the kingdom's military Command Center as well as the clandestine headquarters of SI:7. While the rest of Stormwind was painstakingly rebuilt from the ground up by the Stonemasons following the First War, Old Town escaped total ruin. Because it did not require wholesale reconstruction, it never received the pristine marble facades and grand canals seen in the Trade District or Cathedral Square. Instead, it remains a rustic, crowded quarter where working folk, laborers, and the city's poorest residents reside. Its cobbled streets are narrower, dirtier, and far more chaotic than the rest of the capital, yet they preserve the authentic atmosphere of pre-war Stormwind.

Olsen's Farthing. Olsen's Farthing was once a flourishing farmstead situated along the primary trade road running through Silverpine Forest. In the wake of the Third War, the fields fell into ruin and became overrun by reanimated thralls bound to the renegade necromancer Thule Ravenclaw. Before the plague consumed Lordaeron, Olsen's Farthing was a busy agricultural homestead with direct access to Silverpine's main overland trading route. Today, its tilled fields are choked with weeds, its structures lie broken, and any memory of honest farming has been erased by Scourge necromancy. Undead thralls, bound as slaves and raiders under the command of Thule Ravenclaw, wander the barren grounds to slaughter any travelers who stray too close.

Oracle Glade. Nestled in northwestern Teldrassil, the Oracle Glade is a sacred woodland sanctuary home to the wondrous Oracle Tree and the World Tree's premier moonwell. Despite its serene purpose as a center of communion and vigilance, the glade faces constant harassment from encroaching Bloodfeather harpies. The Oracle Glade rests quietly between Darnassus and Wellspring Lake, serving as a vital nexus of night elven communion with nature. At its center stands the Oracle Tree, an ancient specimen whose massive boughs evoke the silhouette of an eagle perched atop a bear. Nearby shimmers the first and most potent of Teldrassil's sacred moonwells, an oasis of lunar magic bathed in Elune's grace. Alongside the Circle of the Ancients, the Oracle Tree watches over the island boughs, shedding inscribed bark that acts as vital communiques to Archdruid Fandral Staghelm regarding the World Tree's health.

Palemane Rock. Palemane Rock is a cavern and campsite nestled into the western mountains of Mulgore. It serves as a primary stronghold for the aggressive Palemane gnoll tribe, posing a continual nuisance and threat to the nearby tauren of Bloodhoof Village. Situated along the western rim of the grassy plains of Mulgore, Palemane Rock consists of a sprawling open-air encampment fronting a deep, shadowed cavern carved into the mountainside. The Palemane gnolls have claimed both the cave interior and the immediate foothills outside as their territory. Hostile and territorial, these gnolls aggressively defend their den, attacking hunters, travelers, and scouts who wander too close to their rocky haven.

Park. Tucked along the western edge of Stormwind City between Cathedral Square and the Mage Quarter, the Park is a lush sanctuary of greenery and quiet reflection. Devoted to nature and leisure amidst the bustling stone capital, it serves as the primary haven for visiting night elves and houses the only druid trainers in the Eastern Kingdoms. While the rest of Stormwind is dominated by cobbled walkways, towering limestone ramparts, and crowded market stalls, the Park offers a tranquil breath of wilderness. Originally established as a quiet place of recreation for the city's populace, it naturally transformed into an enclave for night elf emissaries and travelers arriving from across the Great Sea. Sheltered beneath shaded canopies and surrounding a central Moonwell, the district brings a sliver of Kalimdor's sacred glades into the heart of the human kingdom.

Petitioner's Chamber. The Petitioner's Chamber, also known as the Hall of Petitioners, is an antechamber situated just off the main entrance ramp of Stormwind Keep. It serves as an official waiting room for nobility, church dignitaries, and visiting subjects seeking an audience with the crown. Those lingering here often pass the hours mingling, drinking, or waiting upon the regent's pleasure. Found immediately to the right upon ascending into Stormwind Keep, the Petitioner's Chamber is where matters of state meet everyday bureaucracy. Nobles such as Count Remington Ridgewell and high-ranking clergy like Bishop DeLavey pass their time in these halls while waiting for an audience with the boy-king Anduin Wrynn and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Behind the polished veneer of courtly etiquette, it is an ideal corner of the castle for gossip, quiet lobbying, and discerning who truly holds influence within the realm.

Pig and Whistle Tavern. The Pig and Whistle Tavern is a bustling tavern nestled within Stormwind City's rugged Old Town district. It serves as a favored gathering spot for Alliance travelers, local laborers, and weathered veterans recalling the kingdom's past conflicts. Situated amidst the gritty, winding alleys of Old Town, the Pig and Whistle Tavern offers warmth, ale, and lodging to those who walk the capital's rougher quarter. While the nobles of the city congregate in cathedral squares and marble plazas, this establishment caters to common citizens, working folk, and travelers fresh from the road. Inside, patrons can find merchants like the renowned recipe vendor Kendor Kabonka, alongside grizzled veterans who nurse their tankards while trading memories of the First and Second Wars.

Pool of Ask'ar. The Pool of Ask'ar is a sprawling, submerged cavern lake located deep within Blackfathom Deeps. Teeming with aquatic beasts and foul naga invaders, its waters conceal ancient night elven architecture alongside hidden passageways that wind deeper into the corrupted sanctuary. Situated just beyond the Drowned Sacellum, the Pool of Ask'ar fills a massive subterranean vault with murky, cold water. The natural caverns and ancient stonework have become a nesting ground for oversized snapping turtles and deep-sea crabs, overseen by the enormous ancient chelonian known as Ghamoo-ra. The naga who have taken over the temple utilize this submerged threshold as a defensive staging ground, guarding the waterlogged approaches that lead deeper into the complex toward Lady Sarevess and the Moonshrine Ruins.

Pools of Arlithrien. The Pools of Arlithrien are a cluster of secluded springs resting in western Teldrassil, just south of the gates to Darnassus. Once a tranquil retreat centered around a sacred moonwell, the area has fallen into neglect and danger as local wildlife and nearby hostile Gnarlpine furbolgs encroached upon it. Tucked along the shaded boughs south of Darnassus, the Pools of Arlithrien were originally meant to be a quiet place of natural harmony. At their heart lies a stone moonwell, a vessel for the waters imbued with the grace of Elune. Yet despite its proximity to the night elven capital, the sanctuary has become perilous. Agitated beasts roam the shallows, and the persistent hostility of the displaced Gnarlpine furbolgs forced the night elves to abandon routine upkeep of the site, leaving a peaceful wonder shadowed by the island's growing malaise.

Pools of Vision. The Pools of Vision are a subterranean cavern nestled beneath Spirit Rise in Thunder Bluff. Marked by still waters and dim caverns, this secluded subterranean space serves as the primary enclave for the Forsaken within the tauren capital. While the sunlit peaks of Thunder Bluff belong to the wind, earth, and sky, the Pools of Vision plunge directly beneath Spirit Rise into shadowy seclusion. Accessible from a discreet cave path off the bridge leading to the rise, this subterranean grotto offers subterranean respite quite unlike the open-air lodges above. Here, misty waters pool in the dark, creating an isolated atmosphere where Horde spellcasters gather far from the bustling central mesas.

Pyrewood Village. Pyrewood Village is an isolated human settlement nestled in southern Silverpine Forest beneath Shadowfang Keep. Originally part of Gilneas before being stranded outside the Greymane Wall, its living residents harbor a horrific secret brought upon them by the mad archmage Arugal. Pyrewood was once a prosperous Gilnean settlement owned by Lord Darius Crowley. When King Genn Greymane chose to isolate his kingdom behind the massive Greymane Wall following the Second War, Pyrewood and its neighbor Ambermill were abandoned on the northern side. Cut off from their homeland, the townsfolk were left entirely defenseless during the Third War as the Scourge marched across Lordaeron. Though they managed to survive the initial wave of the undead, their true nightmare began when the mage Arugal took refuge in the fortress above.

Ragefire Chasm (Classic). Ragefire Chasm is a sprawling network of volcanic tunnels carved directly beneath Orgrimmar, accessible through the shadowy depths of the Cleft of Shadow. Despite being situated under the Horde's sovereign capital, these fiery caverns crawl with hostile troggs and a subversive coven of cultists loyal to the Shadow Council. Beneath the stone streets and fortified towers of Orgrimmar lies Ragefire Chasm, a treacherous network of magma-filled subterranean caverns. The tunnels recently became overrun by the savage Ragefire troggs, who pushed upward from deep subterranean fissures. Magatha Grimtotem of the tauren attempted peaceful diplomacy with the creatures, but her overtures were violently rejected. Left unchecked, the troggs threaten to tunnel further into the foundations of the city itself.

Raptor Grounds. Tucked into the dusty hills of the southern Barrens, the Raptor Grounds is a secluded valley claimed by the Sunscale raptors. Unlike ordinary wild beasts, the pack here exhibits an eerie, tool-using cunning and a compulsive urge to steal bright trinkets from nearby settlements. Located west of Northwatch Hold, the Raptor Grounds serves as the primary nesting territory for the Sunscale raptors. Travelers quickly discover that these creatures are far from mindless predators: they display an unnatural intelligence, fashioning crude shelters, assembling primitive tools, and coordinating their hunts. Driven by a relentless fascination with shiny and unusual items, the pack regularly raids passing caravans and Horde encampments, dragging coins, trinkets, and supplies back into their canyon dens.

Ratchet. Ratchet is a bustling neutral port town run by the Steamwheedle Cartel on the eastern coast of the Barrens. Founded by chief engineer Gazlowe after he helped construct Orgrimmar, it serves as the primary maritime trade hub linking central Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms. Perched on the arid coastline between Durotar and Dustwallow Marsh, Ratchet offers safe harbor to anyone carrying coin. Founded by the entrepreneurial engineer Gazlowe following the Third War, the port arose from smugglers, exiles, and daring traders looking to exploit Kalimdor's frontier. It operates beneath the banner of the Steamwheedle Cartel, maintaining strict neutrality between the Horde and the Alliance. Ships like The Maiden's Fancy regularly ply the waters across the Great Sea to Booty Bay, transporting goods, mercenaries, and raw materials between continents. Local bruisers keep a watchful eye on the docks, ruthlessly thrashing anyone foolish enough to start a brawl and disrupt commerce.

Ravaged Caravan. The Ravaged Caravan is a smoldering wreck located on the northeastern shore of Stonebull Lake in Mulgore. Once a supply convoy bound for Supervisor Fizsprocket's mining operations, it was ambushed and destroyed by local tauren determined to halt goblin exploitation of their homeland. Perched on a rise above Stonebull Lake, the Ravaged Caravan marks an early clash between the tauren of Bloodhoof Village and the encroaching Venture Company. Sent to deliver mining supplies, blueprints, and equipment to Supervisor Fizsprocket's dig site, the caravan was cut off and wrecked by tauren defenders before it could reach its destination. Despite the devastation, stubborn Venture Co. survivors still cling to the ruined wagons and smoldering crates, jealously guarding what little cargo remains.

Raven Hill. Raven Hill is a desolate, ruined village in western Duskwood sitting in the long shadow of the vast Raven Hill Cemetery. Once a lively human settlement, it lies abandoned by all but a handful of frightened squatters and invisible spirits. Situated along the western thoroughfare of Duskwood just north of Addle's Stead, Raven Hill is a tragic shell of its former self. When dark magic and undead horrors swept through the Grand Hamlet region, the living evacuated eastward toward Darkshire or fled the territory entirely. Today, ruined timber homes rot beneath perpetual gloom, avoided by travelers who fear both the restless dead wandering down from the neighboring cemetery and the invisible Unseen lurking between the crumbling walls.

Raven Hill Cemetery. Raven Hill Cemetery is a vast, cursed graveyard stretching across the western reaches of Duskwood. Once a peaceful burial ground for local hamlets, the cemetery has been overrun by hordes of walking dead, scavenger spiders, and ruthless grave robbers. Before the darkness engulfed the Dawning Wood, Raven Hill Cemetery served as the primary resting place for the surrounding settlements. As dark sorceries fell upon the region, the dead failed to remain in their plots. Skeletons, ghouls, and shambling horrors clawed their way out of the soil, swelling the graveyard's grim boundaries. Today, it stands as one of the most perilous blights in Duskwood. The cemetery is prowled not only by rotting abominations and giant spiders, but also by desperate grave robbers eager to plunder ancestral crypts unhindered by local authorities.

Ravenholdt Manor. Tucked away high in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills, Ravenholdt Manor serves as the secluded headquarters for the guild of thieves and assassins known as Ravenholdt. Overseen by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the estate provides a discreet haven where practitioners of stealth hone their craft far from the eyes of authorities. Hidden behind a narrow mountain pass and a winding cave northwest of Durnholde Keep, Ravenholdt Manor sits isolated on the borderlands of the Alterac Mountains. The property belongs to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, a nobleman who maintains a disciplined enclave of rogues, assassins, and intelligence operatives. The grounds feature a tranquil garden and an outdoor training arena overseen by martial experts like Master Kang, providing a disciplined space to practice lockpicking, poison-crafting, and close-quarters combat. While the manor welcomes those with a talent for skullduggery, clumsy outsiders and unwanted visitors are treated with cold suspicion by the manor's watchful sentries.

Raynewood Retreat. Raynewood Retreat is an ancient night elf outpost perched around a massive great tree in north-central Ashenvale. Guarded by dryads and Cenarion protectors, it serves as a watchful sanctuary monitoring the northern passes toward corrupted Felwood. It is also the sanctuary of Keeper Ordanus, an elder son of Cenarius targeted by sinister outside forces. Long before the modern conflicts between the Alliance and Horde, Raynewood Retreat served as a military staging ground for night elf defenders during the ancient War of the Satyr millennia ago. Today, the encampment retains its sacred martial purpose. Nestled between Shael'dryn's moonwell and the satyr-infested ruins of Night Run, the outpost is fiercely guarded by Cenarion Protectors, faerie dragons, and Laughing Sisters.
